###### Sifrei Devarim 149:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/149:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/149:7)


**וּסְקַלְתָּם בָּאֲבָנִים**, יָכוֹל בַּאֲבָנִים מְרֻבּוֹת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (ויקרא כ כז): ״בָּאֶבֶן״. אִי בָּאֶבֶן, יָכוֹל בְּאֶבֶן אַחַת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **בָּאֲבָנִים**, אֱמֹר מֵעַתָּה: לֹא מֵת בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה – יָמוּת בַּשְּׁנִיָּה.


“And you shall pelt them with stones” (Dt. 17:5).
Is it possible to say that
*many* stones should be used in the pelting?
The Teaching states elsewhere:
“With *a* stone” (Lv. 20:27).
If you say *a stone*, is it possible to say that
the pelting is administered with a *single stone*? The Teaching states here:
“With *stones*” (Dt. 17:5)—
from this you may conclude:
if he doesn’t die from the first stone,
let him die from the second!



## Paragraph 150

###### Sifrei Devarim 150:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/150:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/150:1)


(דברים יז ו) **עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם עֵדִים אוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה עֵדִים יוּמַת הַמֵּת**, יָכוֹל אֵין לִי אֶלָּא זֶה בִּלְבַד? מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת שְׁאָר הַמּוּמָתִים? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם עֵדִים אוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה עֵדִים יוּמַת הַמֵּת**.


**Pisqa’ 150**⁵⁰
1. “By the testimony of *two* witnesses or *three* witnesses
shall *the condemned to die* be put to death” (Dt. 17:6).
Is it possible for me to infer that
*he alone* is put to death
[at the testimony of two or three]?
**How do I know that**
**[this rule of testimony]**
**includes all other capital offenses?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“By the testimony of two witnesses or three witnesses**
**shall *the condemned to die* be put to death**” (Dt. 17:6). ⁵¹

footnotes:
⁵⁰ H:188; JN1:15
⁵¹ Cf. Sifre Nu. 161.


###### Sifrei Devarim 150:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/150:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/150:2)


מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא יְלַמֵּד עֵד אֶחָד חוֹבָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **לֹא יוּמַת עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד**.


How do I know that, [in capital cases,]
one witness alone cannot present evidence for prosecution?
The Teaching states:
“He shall not be put to death by the testimony of one witness” (Dt. 17:6).


###### Sifrei Devarim 150:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/150:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/150:3)


וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא יְלַמֵּד תַּלְמִיד חוֹבָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **לֹא יוּמַת עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד**.


**And how do I know that**
**a disciple [of sages] cannot argue for prosecution?**⁵²
**The Teaching states:**
**“He shall not be put to death by the testimony of one witness” (Dt. 17:6).**⁵³

footnotes:
⁵² //M. San.5:4
⁵³ F:205, ls.3-4 notes the absence of this material from many versions.



## Paragraph 151

###### Sifrei Devarim 151:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/151:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/151:1)


(דברים יז ז) **יַד הָעֵדִים תִּהְיֶה בּוֹ בָרִאשֹׁנָה לַהֲמִיתוֹ** – מִצְוָה בָּעֵדִים לַהֲמִיתוֹ.


**Pisqa’ 151**⁵⁴
1. **“The hand of the witnesses shall be the first at him,**
**to execute him” (Dt. 17:7).**
**Thus, it is required that**
**the witnesses execute him.**⁵⁵

footnotes:
⁵⁴ H:189; JN2:16
⁵⁵ //Sifre Nu. 114.


###### Sifrei Devarim 151:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/151:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/151:2)


מִנַּיִן לֹא מֵת בְּיַד הָעֵדִים – יָמוּת בְּיַד כָּל אָדָם? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וְיַד כָּל הָעָם בָּאַחֲרֹנָה**.


**How do I know that**
**if he doesn’t die at**
**the hand of the witnesses,**
**he may be put to death at**
**the hand of any other person?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“And the hand of all**
**the people afterwards”**⁵⁶ **(Dt. 17:7).**

footnotes:
⁵⁶ //M. San.6:4; Sifre Nu 114


###### Sifrei Devarim 151:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/151:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/151:3)


**וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִקִּרְבֶּךָ** – בַּעֵר עוֹשֵׂי הָרָעוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל!


**“And you must expunge this evil from your midst” (Dt. 17:7)—**
**that is, expunge the evil-doers from Israel**.⁵⁷ 86.1, 155.1, 187.3, 220.2, etc

footnotes:
⁵⁷ Cf. Pisqa’



## Paragraph 152

###### Sifrei Devarim 152:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:1)


(דברים יז ח) **כִּי יִפָּלֵא** – מְלַמֵּד שֶׁבְּמֻפְלָא הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר.


**Pisqa’ 152**⁵⁸
1. “*If* you are bedazzled”⁵⁹ literally: “extraordinary,” “baffling.” Following is the JPS rendering of the first clause of Dt. 17:8: “If a case is *too baffling* for you to decide, be it a controversy over homicide, civil law or assault—matters of dispute in your courts.” The midrashic reading of the verse, presented in my own rendering of Sifre’s text, takes pains to re-signify the verse to make room for characteristic institutions associated with the oral Torah’s institutions of jurisprudence. Cf. Fraade, p.84-85. (Dt. 17:8).
This teaches that
the verse speaks [even] of a judicial appointee
of dazzling intellect.⁶⁰ Tannaitic memory recognizes the *mufla’ shel bet din* as an appointed office (e.g., M. Hor.1:4, T. San.7:1) that should go to the most brilliant judge in the Sanhedrin.

footnotes:
⁵⁸ H:189-190; JN2:17-18
⁵⁹ Heb: yipalei;
⁶⁰ Heb: mufla’.


###### Sifrei Devarim 152:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:2)


**מִמְּךָ** – זוֹ עֵצָה.


“Beyond your own [capacities]” (Dt. 17:8)—
of deliberation.


###### Sifrei Devarim 152:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:3)


**דָּבָר** – זוֹ הֲלָכָה.


“By an issue” (Dt. 17:8)—
concerning the oral legal tradition.


###### Sifrei Devarim 152:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:4)


**לַמִּשְׁפָּט** – זֶה הַדִּין.


“Of case-law” (Dt. 17:8)—
that requires adjudication.


###### Sifrei Devarim 152:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:5)


**בֵּין דָּם לְדָם** – בֵּין דַּם נִדָּה לְדַם יוֹלֶדֶת לְדַם זִיבָה.


“In distinguishing between *blood* and *blood*” (Dt. 17:8)—
whether menstrual blood,
parturient blood,
or a bloody venereal discharge.


###### Sifrei Devarim 152:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:6)


**בֵּין דִּין לְדִין** – בֵּין דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת לְדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת לְדִינֵי מַכּוֹת.


“Between *judgment* and *judgment*” (Dt. 17:8)—
whether monetary judgments,
capital judgments,
or judgments [regarding judicial] lashings.⁶¹ I follow RH and Fraade, p. 84 in rendering this phrase. Cf. H:189, “bodily injury law” and JN2:17. “assault.”

footnotes:
⁶¹ Heb: dinei makot.


###### Sifrei Devarim 152:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:7)


**בֵּין נֶגַע לָנֶגַע** – בֵּין נִגְעֵי אָדָם לְנִגְעֵי בְגָדִים לְנִגְעֵי בָתִּים.


“Between one *plague-sign* and *another*” (Dt. 17:8)—
whether those affecting human bodies, clothing, or homes.


###### Sifrei Devarim 152:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:8)


**דִּבְרֵי** – אֵלּוּ עֲרָכִים וַחֲרָמִים וְהֶקְדֵּשׁוֹת.


“And words” (Dt. 17:8)—
[declarations of vows]
concerning the monetary value
of persons, devoted objects, or consecrated gifts (Lv. 27:1-34).⁶², and *heqdeshot* denote vows to offer the monetary value of specific persons or objects to the upkeep of the Sanctuary.

footnotes:
⁶² `Arachim, kheremim


###### Sifrei Devarim 152:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:9)


**רִיבוֹת** – זוֹ הַשְׁקָיַת סוֹטָה וַעֲרִיפַת עֶגְלָה וְטָהֳרַת מְצוֹרָע.


“Of conflict” (Dt. 17:8)—
whether the ordeal of the accused adulteress (Nu. 5:12ff.),
the rite of the beheaded calf (Dt. 21:1-9),
or the purification of victims of Scale-disease (Lv. 14:1ff.).


###### Sifrei Devarim 152:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:10)


**בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ** – זֶה לֶקֶט שִׁכְחָה וּפֵאָה.


“Within your gates (Dt. 17:8)—
whether Gleanings, the Forgotten Sheaf, or Corner-offerings.⁶³

footnotes:
⁶³ These are agricultural offerings that remain in the fields unharvested for the exclusive benefit of the poor (see Lv. 19:19, Dt. 24:19, Dt. 26:12).


###### Sifrei Devarim 152:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:11)


**וְקַמְתָּ** – מִיָּד.


2. “*Then* shall you arise” (Dt. 17:8)—immediately!


###### Sifrei Devarim 152:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:12)


**וְקַמְתָּ** – בְּבֵית דִּין,


“*Arise*” (Dt. 17:8)—in the court.


###### Sifrei Devarim 152:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:13)


מִכָּן אָמְרוּ (סנהדרין פי״א מ״ב): שְׁלֹשָׁה בָּתֵּי דִינִים הָיוּ שָׁם, אֶחָד עַל פֶּתַח הַר הַבַּיִת, וְאֶחָד עַל פֶּתַח הָעֲזָרָה, וְאֶחָד בְּלִשְׁכַּת הַגָּזִית.


On this basis they taught:
**Three courts were there:**
**one at the entrance to the Mount of the Abode;**
**and one at the entrance to the Courtyard;**
**and one in the Chamber of Carved Stone.**


###### Sifrei Devarim 152:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:14)


בָּאִים לָזֶה שֶׁל שַׁעַר הַר הַבַּיִת וְאוֹמֵר: ״כָּךְ דָּרַשְׁתִּי וְכָךְ דָּרְשׁוּ חֲבֵרַי, כָּךְ לִמַּדְתִּי וְכָךְ לִמְּדוּ חֲבֵרַי״. אִם שָׁמְעוּ, אָמְרוּ לָהֶם, וְאִם לָאו – בָּאִים לָזֶה שֶׁעַל פֶּתַח הָעֲזָרָה וְאוֹמֵר: ״כָּךְ דָּרַשְׁתִּי וְכָךְ דָּרְשׁוּ חֲבֵרַי, כָּךְ לִמַּדְתִּי וְכָךְ לִמְּדוּ חֲבֵרַי״. אִם שָׁמְעוּ, אָמְרוּ לָהֶם, וְאִם לָאו – אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ בָּאִים לְבֵית דִּין הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבְּלִשְׁכַּת הַגָּזִית, שֶׁמִּשָּׁם תּוֹרָה יוֹצְאָה לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: **מִן הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר ה׳**.


**They would first reach**
**the one at the entrance to the Mount of the Abode.**
**And [he presiding justice]would announce:**
**Thus have I expounded the matter**
**and thus have my colleagues expounded it.**
**Thus have I studied the matter**
**and thus have my colleagues studied it.**
**If [the judges] had heard a tradition [on the matter],**
**they would declare it.**
**But if not, they would go**
**to the High Court in the Chamber of Carved Stone.**
**From there would Torah go forth to all Israel,**
**as it is said:**
**“From that very place which HASHEM shall choose”**⁶⁴ **(Dt. 17:10)**

footnotes:
⁶⁴ =M. San.11:2; cf. T. San.7:1.


###### Sifrei Devarim 152:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/152:15)


**וְקַמְתָּ וְעָלִיתָ**, מַגִּיד שֶׁאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל גְּבוֹהָה מִכָּל הָאֲרָצוֹת וּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ גָּבוֹהַּ מִכָּל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל.


3. “Then shall you *arise* and *ascend*” (Dt. 17:8)—
**this explains that**
**the Land of Israel is higher than all other lands,**
**and the Holy Abode is higher than all the Land of Israel**.⁶⁵ 37.18.

footnotes:
⁶⁵ See Pisqa’



## Paragraph 153

###### Sifrei Devarim 153:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/153:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/153:1)


(דברים יז ט) **וּבָאתָ** – לְרַבּוֹת בֵּית דִּין שֶׁבְּיַבְנֶה.


**Pisqa’ 153**⁶⁶
1. “And when you *reach”*(Dt. 17:9).
Including the court at Yavneh⁶⁷
[as the successor of the Sanhedrin⁶⁸ 154.1.].

footnotes:
⁶⁶ H:190; JN2:19-20.
⁶⁷ Yavneh, a coastal town on the Mediterranean, was a major center of rabbinic learning in the latter decades of the first century and the first third of the second century CE.
⁶⁸ The Yavnean court was not equal in all respects to the ancient Sanhedrin that presided over the Chamber of Carved Stone. For example, it could not administer capital punishment (M. San.11:4). Cf. Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 153:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/153:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/153:2)


**אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים הַלְוִיִּם**, מִצְוָה בְּבֵית דִּין שֶׁיִּהְיוּ בוֹ כֹּהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם.


“The *levitical Priest*” (Dt. 17:9)—
it is a requirement that the court
include Priests and Levites.


###### Sifrei Devarim 153:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/153:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/153:3)


יָכוֹל מִצְוָה, וְאִם אֵין בּוֹ יְהֵא פָסוּל? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וְאֶל הַשֹּׁפֵט** – אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כֹּהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם כָּשֵׁר.


Is it possible to say that
in the absence of a Priest or Levite,
the court shall be disqualified?
The Teaching states:
“Or to the *justice*” (Dt. 17:9)—
even though there is no Priest or Levite,
the court is an appropriate legal venue.


###### Sifrei Devarim 153:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/153:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/153:4)


**אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם**, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי: וְכִי עָלָת עַל דַּעְתְּךָ שֶׁתֵּלֵךְ אֵצֶל שׁוֹפֵט שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּיָמֶיךָ? אֶלָּא שׁוֹפֵט שֶׁהוּא כָּשֵׁר וּמֻחְזָק בְּאוֹתָם הַיָּמִים. הָיָה קָרוֹב וְנִתְרַחֵק – כָּשֵׁר, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר (קהלת ז י): ״אַל תֹּאמַר מֶה הָיָה שֶׁהַיָּמִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים הָיוּ טוֹבִים מֵאֵלֶּה כִּי לֹא מֵחָכְמָה שָׁאַלְתָּ עַל זֶה״.


2. “Who shall preside *in those days*” (Dt. 17:9).
**Said R. Yose the Galilean:**
**Now, can you imagine that**
**you would go to a justice**
**who is *not* alive *in those days*?**
**The point is, select a justice**
**who is eminently qualified**
***among his contemporaries*.**
**If he had been kin [to the litigants],**
**but then severed the connection [e.g., through death],**
**he is qualified [to sit in judgment of them].**
**And in this connection,**
**He states**:
**“Do not wonder why the old days were better than today,**
**for such a question does not proceed from wisdom” (Ecc. 7:10).**⁶⁹ 190.3.

footnotes:
⁶⁹ Cf. T. RH. 2:3 and Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 153:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/153:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/153:5)


**וְדָרַשְׁתָּ וְהִגִּידוּ לְךָ אֵת דְּבַר הַמִּשְׁפָּט** – אֵלּוּ דִּקְדּוּקֵי מִשְׁפָּט.


“And you shall inquire, and they shall declare to you
the *word of judgment*” (Dt. 17:9)—
in accord with *every detail* of legal procedure.



## Paragraph 154

###### Sifrei Devarim 154:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/154:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/154:1)


(דברים יז י) **וְעָשִׂיתָ עַל פִּי הַדָּבָר**, עַל הוֹרָיַת בֵּית דִּין הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלִַם חַיָּבִים מִיתָה, וְאֵין חַיָּבִים מִיתָה עַל הוֹרָיַת בֵּית דִּין שֶׁבְּיַבְנֶה.


**Pisqa’ 154**⁷⁰
1. “And you shall behave according to *the ruling*” *(*Dt. 17:10).
Those who violate the instructions
of the High Court in Jerusalem
are liable for execution;
but there is no threat of execution
for violating the instructions
of the court in Yavneh.

footnotes:
⁷⁰ H:190; JN2:20.


###### Sifrei Devarim 154:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/154:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/154:2)


(דברים יז יא) ״עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה אֲשֶׁר יוֹרוּךָ״, עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה חַיָּבִים מִיתָה וְאֵין חַיָּבִים מִיתָה עַל דִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים.


“According *to the sense* of the *Torah* that *they shall teach* you” (Dt. 17:11).
Those who violate rulings of *the Torah*
are liable for execution;
but there is no threat of execution
for violating *scribal traditions*.


###### Sifrei Devarim 154:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/154:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/154:3)


**וְעַל הַמִּשְׁפָּט אֲשֶׁר יֹאמְרוּ לְךָ תַּעֲשֶׂה** – מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה.


“And according *to the rule which they explain* to you *must you act*” (Dt. 17:11)—
this refers to a prescriptive commandment.


###### Sifrei Devarim 154:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/154:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/154:4)


**לֹא תָסוּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה אֲשֶׁר יַגִּידוּ לְךָ** – מִצְוַת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.


“Do not deviate from the Torah *they shall impart* to you” (Dt. 17:11)—
this refers to a proscriptive commandment.


###### Sifrei Devarim 154:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/154:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/154:5)


**יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאל** – אֲפִילּוּ מַרְאִים בְּעֵינֶיךָ עַל יָמִין שֶׁהוּא שְׂמֹאל וְעַל שְׂמֹאל שֶׁהוּא יָמִין – שְׁמַע לָהֶם!


“To the right or the left” (Dt. 17:11)—
even if, before your very eyes,
they instruct that right is left, or left is right,
you must obey them.



## Paragraph 155

###### Sifrei Devarim 155:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/155:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/155:1)


(דברים יז יב) **וְהָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה בְזָדוֹן**, אֲשֶׁר לֹא שָׁמַע מִפִּי בֵּית דִּין וּמוֹרֶה.


**Pisqa’ 155**⁷¹
1. “As for the man who acts in *defiance*” (Dt. 17:12).
This refers to one who
does not submit to the court
and insists upon his teaching.

footnotes:
⁷¹ H:190; JN2:21-22


###### Sifrei Devarim 155:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/155:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/155:2)


**אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה** – עַל מַעֲשֶׂה הוּא חַיָּב וְאֵינוֹ חַיָּב עַל הוֹרָיָה.


“Who *acts*” (Dt. 17;12)—
he is held liable for an actual *act*,
but he is not held liable for merely teaching.


###### Sifrei Devarim 155:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/155:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/155:3)


**בְזָדוֹן** – עַל זָדוֹן הוּא חַיָּב וְאֵינוֹ חַיָּב עַל שְׁגָגָה.


“Who acts *defiantly*” (Dt. 17:12)—
he is held liable for teaching *defiantly*,
but he is not held liable for *inadvertent error*.


###### Sifrei Devarim 155:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/155:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/155:4)


**לְבִלְתִּי שְׁמֹעַ** – וְלֹא שׁוֹמֵעַ מִפִּי שׁוֹמֵעַ.


“By not *listening*” (Dt. 17:12)—
but not one who violates a teaching heard at second-hand.


###### Sifrei Devarim 155:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/155:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/155:5)


**אֶל הַכֹּהֵן הָעֹמֵד לְשָׁרֵת**, מַגִּיד שֶׁאֵין שֵׁרוּת כָּשֵׁר אֶלָּא מֵעוֹמֵד. הָא אִם יָשַׁב וְעָבַד – עֲבוֹדָתוֹ פְּסוּלָה.


“**To the Priest who *stands* there in service” (Dt. 17:12)—**
**this indicates that proper service**
**is performed only while standing.**
**Therefore, if he served while seated,**
**his service is disqualified.** ⁷² 167.1.

footnotes:
⁷² Sifre Nu. 39; cf. Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 155:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/155:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/155:6)


**אוֹ אֶל הַשּׁוֹפֵט** – זֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כֹּהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם כָּשֵׁר.


**“Or to the justice” (Dt. 17:12)—**
as we have taught:⁷³ 153.1.
**even though a court has no Priests or Levites,**
**it is qualified.**

footnotes:
⁷³ At Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 155:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/155:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/155:7)


**וּמֵת הָאִישׁ** – בִּסְתָם מִיתָה הָאֲמוּרָה בַּתּוֹרָה, בְּחֶנֶק.


**“Then that man shall *die*” (Dt. 17:12)—**
**Where the mode of execution is unspecified in the Torah,**
**we assume strangulation.**⁷⁴, 5, s.v., *khol mitah ha’amurah stam.* Cf, *Pisqa’* 273.1.

footnotes:
⁷⁴ //Mech ISH, neziqin


###### Sifrei Devarim 155:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/155:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/155:8)


**הַהוּא** – לֹא אָנוּס וְלֹא שׁוֹגֵג וְלֹא מֻטְעֶה.


**“*That* man” (Dt. 17:12)—**
**but not if he is coerced [into apostasy by a threat to his life],**
**nor one who acted unintentionally,**
**nor one who was misled [out of ignorance].**⁷⁵ 149.4.

footnotes:
⁷⁵ Cf. Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 155:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/155:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/155:9)


**וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל** – בַּעֵר עוֹשֵׂי הָרָעוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל!


**“And you must expunge this evil from Israel” (Dt. 17:12)—**
**that is, expunge the evil-doers from Israel**.⁷⁶ 140.1 (Dt. 22:1) and Dt. 22:2 (141.1).

footnotes:
⁷⁶ This mandate for expunging evil is appears commonly in Sifre, attached to several verses in Deuteronomy. Cf. Pisqa’ot



## Paragraph 156

###### Sifrei Devarim 156:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/156:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/156:1)


(דברים יז יד) **כִּי תָבוֹא אֶל הָאָרֶץ** – עֲשֵׂה מִצְוָה הָאֲמוּרָה בָּעִנְיָן, שֶׁבִּשְׂכָרָהּ תִּכָּנֵס לָאָרֶץ.


**Pisqa’ 156**⁷⁷
1. **“When you enter into the Land” (Dt. 17:14)—**
**perform the commandment specified in this context,**
**for by virtue of this will you enter the Land.**

footnotes:
⁷⁷ H:191; JN2:23-24


###### Sifrei Devarim 156:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/156:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/156:2)


**אֲשֶׁר ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לָךְ** – בִּזְכוּתְךָ.


**“Which HASHEM your God is giving you” (Dt. 17:14)—**
**because you deserve it.**


###### Sifrei Devarim 156:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/156:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/156:3)


**וִירִשְׁתָּהּ וְיָשַׁבְתָּה בָּהּ** – בִּשְׂכַר שֶׁתִּירַשׁ תֵּשֵׁב.


**“And you shall inherit it, and settle within it” (Dt. 17:14)—**
**the reward for inheriting it is settling it**.⁷⁸ 160.1, 162.1, 170.1 and 297.

footnotes:
⁷⁸ This formula is commonly used in Sifre to draw attention to the significance of various commandments concerned with the Land. Other examples appear, e.g., at Pisqa’ot


###### Sifrei Devarim 156:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/156:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/156:4)


**וְאָמַרְתָּ אָשִׂימָה עָלַי מֶלֶךְ**, רַבִּי נְהוֹרַי אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי זֶה דְּבַר גְּנַי לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמואל א ח ז): ״כִּי לֹא אוֹתְךָ מָאָסוּ כִּי אוֹתִי מָאֲסוּ מִמְּלֹךְ עֲלֵיהֶם״.


2. “And should you say, I will appoint over me a king” (Dt. 17:14).
**R. Nehorai says:**
**This is, indeed, an insult to Israel!**
**For it is said:**
**“Because it is not you whom they reject;**
**rather they have rejected Me from ruling over them” (1Sam. 8:7)**⁷⁹

footnotes:
⁷⁹ //T.San.4:5


###### Sifrei Devarim 156:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/156:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/156:5)


אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וַהֲלֹא מִצְוָה מִן הַתּוֹרָה לִשְׁאוֹל לָהֶם מֶלֶךְ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים יז טו): ״שׂוֹם תָּשִׂים עָלֶיךָ מֶלֶךְ״! לָמָּה נֶעֶנְשׁוּ בִּימֵי שְׁמוּאֵל? לְפִי שֶׁהִקְדִּימוּ עַל יָדָם.


**Said R. Judah:**
**Look, now—isn’t Israel commanded in the Torah**
**to request for themselves a king?**⁸⁰ 67.1.
For it is said:
“You should indeed appoint over yourself a king” (Dt. 17:14).
Why, then, were they punished for this
in the days of Samuel?
Because they took the initiative.

footnotes:
⁸⁰ Cf, Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 156:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/156:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/156:6)


**כְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר סְבִיבֹתָי**, רַבִּי נְהוֹרַי אוֹמֵר: לֹא בִקְשׁוּ לָהֶם מֶלֶךְ אֶלָּא לְהַעֲבִידָם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמואל א ח כ): ״וְהָיִינוּ גַם אֲנַחְנוּ כְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם וּשְׁפָטָנוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ וְיָצָא לְפָנֵינוּ וְנִלְחַם אֶת מִלְחֲמֹתֵינוּ״.


“Like all the nations that surround me” (Dt. 17:14).
**R. Nehorai says:**
**They only requested a king for themselves**
**in order to establish for themselves a *foreign cult*,**
**for it is said:**
**“And even we shall be *like all the nations*, with our king to judge us,**
**to go out before us, and to fight our wars” (1Sam. 8:20)**⁸¹

footnotes:
⁸¹ //T. San.4:5



## Paragraph 157

###### Sifrei Devarim 157:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:1)


(דברים יז טו) **שׂוֹם תָּשִׂים**, מֵת – מַנֵּה אַחֵר תַּחְתָּיו.


**Pisqa’ 157**⁸²
1. “You should indeed *place* over yourself *a king*” (Dt. 17:15)—
and if he dies, appoint another in his *place*.

footnotes:
⁸² H:192; JN2:25-26


###### Sifrei Devarim 157:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:2)


**מֶלֶךְ** – וְלֹא מַלְכָּה.


“A king” (Dt. 17:15)—
but not a queen.


###### Sifrei Devarim 157:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:3)


**אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ בּוֹ** – עַל פִּי נָבִיא.


“Whom HASHEM your God shall choose” (Dt. 17:15)—
according to the guidance of a prophet.


###### Sifrei Devarim 157:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:4)


**מִקֶּרֶב** – וְלֹא מֵחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ.


“*From among* your brothers” (Dt. 17:15)—
but not an Israelite from beyond the Land.


###### Sifrei Devarim 157:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:5)


**אַחֶיךָ** – וְלֹא מֵאֲחֵרִים.


“From among *your brothers*” (Dt. 17:15)—
but not from [gentile] outsiders.⁸³. But, see *Pisqa’ 4*3.18- 30, for word-plays which exploit the assonance of *‘akheirim* with *‘elohim ‘akheirim*, yielding “gods of the others” as well as “other gods.”

footnotes:
⁸³ A literal rendering of the Hebrew: ‘akheirim


###### Sifrei Devarim 157:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:6)


**תָּשִׂים עָלֶיךָ מֶלֶךְ**, וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר **שׂוֹם תָּשִׂים עָלֶיךָ מֶלֶךְ**, וּמַה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר **תָּשִׂים עָלֶיךָ מֶלֶךְ**? שֶׁתְּהֵא אֵימָתוֹ עָלֶיךָ! מִכָּן אָמְרוּ: מֶלֶךְ אֵין רוֹכְבִים עַל סוּסוֹ וְאֵין יוֹשְׁבִים עַל כִּסְאוֹ וְאֵין מִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁים בְּשַׁרְבִיטוֹ וְאֵין רוֹאִים אוֹתוֹ עָרוֹם וְלֹא כְּשֶׁהוּא מִסְתַּפֵּר וְלֹא בְּבֵית הַמֶּרְחָץ.


2. “Shall you place over yourself a king” (Dt. 17:15).
Now, wasn’t it just said
[in the very same verse]:
“You should indeed place *over yourself* a king” (Dt. 17:15)?
Why, then, does the Teaching state twice:
“Shall you place *over yourself* a king” (Dt. 17:15)?
So that his *majesty* awes you.
On this basis they taught:
**A king—**
**they don’t ride his horse, or sit on his throne,**
**or use his scepter.**
**Nor may they see him naked, or getting a haircut,**
**or in the bath house**⁸⁴

footnotes:
⁸⁴ =M/San.2:5; cf. T.San.4;2


###### Sifrei Devarim 157:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:7)


דָּבָר אַחֵר: **שׂוֹם תָּשִׂים עָלֶיךָ מֶלֶךְ** – מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה.


3. Another word:
“You *should indeed* place over yourself a king” (Dt. 17:15)—
this is a prescriptive commandment.


###### Sifrei Devarim 157:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:8)


**לֹא תוּכַל לָתֵת עָלֶיךָ אִישׁ נָכְרִי** – מִצְוַת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.


“You *will not* be permitted to place over yourself a *foreign* man” (Dt. 17:15)—
this is a proscriptive commandment.


###### Sifrei Devarim 157:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:9)


**אִישׁ נָכְרִי** – מִכָּן אָמְרוּ: הָאִישׁ מְמַנִּים פַּרְנָס עַל הַצִּבּוּר, וְאֵין מְמַנִּים הָאִשָּׁה פַּרְנֶסֶת עַל הַצִּבּוּר.


“A foreign *man*” (Dt. 17:15)—
On this basis they taught:
*A man* may be appointed
to provide for the community,
but they may not appoint *a woman*
to provide for the community.


###### Sifrei Devarim 157:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/157:10)

2. **“And he should not amass *for himself* much silver and gold” (Dt. 17:17).**
**Is it possible to say that**
**he should not amass for himself wealth**
**in order to *provision his army*?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“He should not amass *for himself*” (Dt. 17:17)—**
**for *himself* he may not amass wealth,**
**but he may amass wealth**
**in order to *provision his army.***⁹²
Another word:
**In order to provision his army?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“He should not amass for himself” (Dt. 17:17).**
**For himself he may not amass wealth,**
**but he may amass wealth**
**in order to provision his army**.⁹³
And this is what David did,
as it is said:
“Indeed, though unworthy, I have provisioned
the Abode of HASHEM with gold,
at a hundred thousand ingots,
and with silver
at a thousand thousand ingots” (1Chron. 22:14) .
But Solomon devalued the currency,
in accord with what is said:
“And he made silver in Jerusalem
as common as stones” (1Ki. 10:26).⁹⁴

**Pisqa’ 161**¹⁰⁹
1. “And it shall remain *with him*, and he shall read in it, *all the days* of his life” (Dt. 17:19).
On this basis they taught:
**The king goes to war,**
**and his [copy of the Torah goes] *with him*;**
**he returns, and it returns *with him*;**
**he sits in judgment, and it is nearby;**
**he reclines to dine,**
**and it is before him,**
**as it is said:**
**“And it shall remain with him . . .all the days of his life”**¹¹⁰ (Dt. 17:19).
**If the verse had [only] said:**
**“The *days* of his life,”**
**I might have assumed it referred *only* to the *days*.**
**But the present reading is:**

2. “So that he might learn to revere HASHEM his God” (Dt. 17:19).
This teaches that:
Reverence leads to [mastery of] Scripture,
and Scripture leads to [mastery of] Translation,
and Translation leads to [mastery of] Repeated Tradition (*mishnah*),
and Repeated Tradition leads to [mastery of] Dialectics,
and Dialectics leads to Practice (*ma`aseh*),
and Practice leads back to Reverence.
3 Since we find that
commoners share with the king
an obligation to learn words of Torah,
might they be equivalent in other matters?
The Teaching states:
“To preserve all the *words* of this Torah and *these* statutes” (Dt. 17:19).
Thus, commoners share with the king
an obligation to learn words of Torah,
but they are not equivalent in other matters.

2. R. Hananya b. Gamliel says:
Look at what He says to King Solomon—
“And, also, I gave you what you *didn’t request*—wealth and honor” (1Ki. 3:13).
As if to say: good things,
which I *didn’t* make conditional upon
your observance of the Torah, I have freely given you;
but good things which I *did* make conditional upon
your observance of the Torah, I will not give them to you—
unless you observe it!

“And if you walk in My *paths*, observing my statutes” (1Ki. 3:14).

2. “The Fire-offerings of HASHEM . . . shall they eat” (Dt. 18:1)—
this refers to the offerings
consecrated for consumption in the Holy Abode.¹²³his rubric includes twelve offerings: the Purification-offering, the Guilt-offering, the Public Communion-offering, and the hide of the Holocaust-offering, and the remaining portion of the *log* of oil from the Plague-victim’s purification rite, and the remainder of the Barley-sheaf offering, and the two leavened barley-loaves, and the twelve unleavened Presentation-loaves, and the left-over meal offering,
How do I know to include, among the levitical emoluments,
items consecrated as “Boundary-offerings?”¹²⁴) . The tradition debates whether these “boundaries” delimit enjoyment within Jerusalem, beyond the walls of the Temple, or beyond the walls of Jerusalem itself in the Land. These “boundary offerings’ are as follows: The priestly Gift, and the Gift from the Tithe, the Dough-offering, the First-fruits, the First-Shearing, and the gifts of the Firstling, and Firstling of the clean animal, the Firstling of an ass, and items vowed as a ban, and an ancestral field, and a stolen article belonging to the migrant.
The Teaching states:
“And *His* inheritance they shall eat” (Dt. 18:1)—
[but not the inherited bounty of the other tribes].

**מֵאֵת זֹבְחֵי הַזֶּבַח** – אֵין לוֹ בּוֹ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁעַת זְבִיחָה בִּלְבַד. מִכָּן אָמְרוּ (חולין פ״י מ״ד): גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּר וְהָיְתָה לוֹ פָּרָה, נִשְׁחֲטָה עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְגַּיֵּר – פָּטוּר; מִשֶּׁנִּתְגַּיֵּר – חַיָּב. סָפֵק – פָּטוּר, הַמּוֹצִיא מֵחֲבֵרוֹ עָלָיו הָרְאָיָה.


“From those slaughtering an *obligatory* offering” (Dt. 18:3)—
the Priest has a claim to it
only at the moment of slaughter.
On this basis they taught:
**A proselyte who converted,**
**and had a cow which had been slaughtered—**
**prior to the conversion,**
**[insofar as he was a gentile at the time of the slaughter],**
**he is exempt [from the Priestly-gifts];**
**after the conversion,**
**[insofar as he was an Israelite at the time of the slaughter],**
**he stands under obligation.**
**If there is a doubt about the timing of the slaughter—**
**he is exempt,**
**[under the principle that]**
**the burden of proof is borne by the claimant.**¹³⁰

¹³⁰ =M.Hul.10:4.


###### Sifrei Devarim 165:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/165:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/165:6)


**אִם שׁוֹר אִם שֶׂה** – לְרַבּוֹת כִּלְאַיִם, **אִם שׁוֹר אִם שֶׂה** – בֵּין בָּאָרֶץ בֵּין בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ. וַהֲלֹא דִין הוּא: חִיֵּיב כָּאן וְחִיֵּיב בְּרֵאשִׁית הַגֵּז; מַה מָּצִינוּ בְּרֵאשִׁית הַגֵּז, נוֹהֵג בָּאָרֶץ וּבְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ – אַף מַתָּנוֹת נוֹהֲגוֹת בָּאָרֶץ וּבְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ! אוֹ כַּלֵּךְ לְדֶרֶךְ זוֹ: חִיֵּיב כָּאן וְחִיֵּיב בִּתְרוּמַת רֵאשִׁית; מַה תְּרוּמַת רֵאשִׁית, אֵינוֹ חַיָּב אֶלָּא בָּאָרֶץ – אַף מַתָּנוֹת אֵינָן נוֹהֲגוֹת אֶלָּא בָּאָרֶץ!


4. “Whether an *ox* or a *sheep*” (Dt. 18:3)—
include in the rule
Priestly-gifts from an animal of incompatible species.
“Whether an *ox* or a *sheep*” (Dt. 18:3)—
[include in the rule]
an animal slaughtered in the Land or beyond the Land.
Doesn’t reason dictate as much?
He is under obligation here [for the Priestly-gift],
and he is also under obligation
for the Finest¹³¹, which can also mean “first,” as in “First shearing.” Cf. *Pisqa’* 166.4.-fleece (Dt. 18:5).
Now, we have found that
an obligation to offer the Finest-fleece
is in force both in the Land and beyond the Land.
So, too, should the obligation to offer Priestly-gifts
be in force both in the Land and beyond the Land!
Or, perhaps we can try this approach?
He is under obligation here [for the Priestly-gifts],
and he is also under obligation to offer [a Tithe of]
“the *finest* of your grain, your must, and your oil” (Dt. 18:4).
Just as the obligation to offer [a Tithe of]
“the *finest*” is in force only in the Land,
so, too, should the obligation to offer the Priestly-gifts
be in force only in the Land!

footnotes:
¹³¹ “Finest” here renders Heb: r’eishit


###### Sifrei Devarim 165:7

נִרְאֶה לְמִי דוֹמֶה? דָּנִים דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין תָּלוּי בָּאָרֶץ וּבַקֹּדֶשׁ מִדָּבָר שֶׁאֵין תָּלוּי בָּאָרֶץ וּבַקֹּדֶשׁ, וְאַל תּוֹכִיחַ תְּרוּמַת רֵאשִׁית, שֶׁהִיא תְּלוּיָה בָּאָרֶץ וּבַקֹּדֶשׁ.


But, let us compare the key terms!
We may draw an inference to a matter
that is *not* dependent on the Land
or on a consecrated animal,
from another matter
that is not dependent on the Land
or on a consecrated an animal.
Therefore, the obligation to offer “the finest”
[as Tithe] has no bearing on this matter,
since it *is* dependent on the Land
and on consecration of an object.

אוֹ כַּלֵּךְ לְדֶרֶךְ זוֹ: דָּנִים דָּבָר שֶׁנּוֹהֵג בֵּין בַּמְרֻבֶּה בֵּין בַּמּוּעָט מִדָּבָר שֶׁנּוֹהֵג בַּמְרֻבֶּה וּבַמּוּעָט, וְאַל יוֹכִיחַ רֵאשִׁית הַגֵּז, שֶׁאֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא בַּמְרֻבֶּה.


Or, perhaps, we can try this approach?
We draw an inference about a matter
that applies to both a large and small class
[of individuals],
only from another matter
that applies to both a large and small class
[of individuals].
Therefore, the obligation for the Finest-Fleece
has no bearing on this,
for it applies only when there are [five or more¹³² 166.4 below.] sheep.

רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת אוֹמְרִים: נָתַן לוֹ זְרוֹעַ תַּחַת הַיָּד, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר (במדבר כה ז): ״וַיָּקָם מִתּוֹךְ הָעֵדָה וַיִּקַּח רֹמַח בְּיָדוֹ״; וְהַלְּחָיַיִם תַּחַת תְּפִלָּה, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר (תהלים קו ל) ״וַיַּעֲמֹד פִּינְחָס וַיְפַלֵּל״; הַקֵּבָה תַּחַת קֵיבָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (במדבר כה ח): ״וְאֶל הָאִשָּׁה אֶל קֳבָתָהּ״!


6. R. Judah says:
The Close Readers¹³⁴. Literally: “expounders of hints.” Presumably, a group attracted to allegorical exegesis of some kind. Hammer renders: “those who interpret the law metaphorically.” (H:196); Neusner: “those who interpret matters in a figurative way” (JN2:38). Some mss variants and B. Hul.134b’s parallel text reads: *dorshei khamurot* (“exopunders of difficulties”), interpreted by Rashi, loc. cit., as: expounders of “obscure scriptures.” teach that
[the All-Present] gave the shoulder [to the Priests]
to compensate the hand [offered by Phineas].
And, indeed, He says:
“Then Phineas arose in the midst of the community,
and he took a spear in his *hand*” (Nu. 25:7).
He gave [to the Priesthood] the *cheeks*,
to compensate the *prayer* offered by Phineas.
And so He says:
“Then Phineas stood and *prayed*” (Ps. 106:30).
He gave [to the Priesthood] the maw
to compensate the *belly* of Kosbi b. Tzur,
as it is said:
“And he speared them *both*—the Israelite man and the woman—through her *belly*” (Nu. 25:8)

## Paragraph 166

###### Sifrei Devarim 166:1

(דברים יח ד) **רֵאשִׁית דְּגָנְךָ תִּירוֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ**, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאֵין תּוֹרְמִים אוֹתוֹ אֶלָּא מִן הַמֻּבְחָר. מַה מָּצִינוּ בִּשְׁנֵי מִינִים שֶׁבָּאִילָן – אֵין תּוֹרְמִים מִזֶּה עַל זֶה, כָּךְ שְׁנֵי מִינִים שֶׁבַּתְּבוּאָה וְשֶׁבַּיָּרָק – אֵין תּוֹרְמִים מִזֶּה עַל זֶה.


**Pisqa’ 166**¹³⁵
1. “The *finest* of your grain, your must, and your oil” (Dt. 18:4).
This teaches that
**one offers up Threshing-floor-offering**
**only from the *select* produce.**¹³⁶
**Just as we find that**
**in the case of two kinds of fruit-trees,**
**we do not offer up Threshing-floor-offering**
**from the fruit of this tree**
**on behalf of the fruit of that tree,**
**so, too, if there are two species of grain or leafy-greens,**
**we do not offer up Threshing-floor-offering**
**from this type of produce [e.g., wheat or lettuce]**
**on behalf of that type [barley or onions]**.¹³⁷

**צֹאנְךָ**, וְלֹא שֶׁל אֲחֵרִים. מִכָּן אָמְרוּ (חולין פי״א מ״ב): הַלּוֹקֵחַ גֵּז צֹאנוֹ שֶׁל נָכְרִי – פָּטוּר מֵרֵאשִׁית הַגֵּז. לָקַח גֵּז צֹאנוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ, אִם שִׁיֵּר הַמּוֹכֵר – חַיָּב, וְאִם לָאו – הַלּוֹקֵחַ חַיָּב.


“Of *your* flocks” (Dt. 18:4)—
but not that of [gentile] others.
On this basis they taught:
**One who purchases shorn fleece**
**from the flock of a foreigner**
**is exempt from offering the Finest-Fleece.**
**If he purchased shorn fleece**
**from the flock of his Israelite companion—**
**if there is shorn fleece left over [in the seller’s possession],**
**the seller is obliged [to offer the First-Fleece].**
**But if not, the purchaser is obliged.**¹⁴⁰

**תִּתֶּן לוֹ**, שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ כְּדֵי מַתָּנָה. מִיכָּן אָמְרוּ (שם): כַּמָּה נוֹתֵן לוֹ? מִשְׁקַל חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים בִּיהוּדָה, שֶׁהֵם עֶשֶׂר בַּגָּלִיל, מְלֻבָּן וְלֹא צוֹיִ, כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת מִמֶּנּוּ בֶּגֶד קָטָן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: **תִּתֶּן לוֹ** שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ כְּדֵי מַתָּנָה.


3. **“The finest . . . shall you give to him” (Dt. 18:4)—**
**there should be enough for a [generous] gift.**¹⁴¹

**How much fleece should he give to him?**
**A weight of five *selas* in Judea,**

**And it should be white, not filthy,**
**and enough to make a small garment,**
**for it is said:**
**“Shall you give to him” (Dt. 18:4)—**
**enough for a generous gift.**¹⁴²

## Paragraph 167

###### Sifrei Devarim 167:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/167:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/167:1)


(דברים יח ה) **כִּי בוֹ בָחַר ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ מִכָּל שְׁבָטֶיךָ** – מַגִּיד שֶׁאֵין שֵׁרוּת כָּשֵׁר בּוֹ אֶלָּא מֵעוֹמֵד; הָא אִם יָשַׁב וְשֵׁרֵת – עֲבוֹדָתוֹ פְּסוּלָה.


**Pisqa’ 167**¹⁴⁵

2. Yet I still wonder:
here [the verse states] *fire* (Dt. 18:10),
but there [it states] *Molekh* (Lv. 18:21).
How can I apply what is said here [about *fire*]
to the context there [which speaks of Molekh]?
And how can I apply what is said there [about Molekh]
to the context here which speaks of *fire*?
[The repeated terms,]
*pass through* (Dt. 18:10) and *pass through* (Lv. 18:21),
permit the following analogical inference:
Just as *pass through* mentioned here (Dt. 18:10)
specifies *fire*,
so, too, *pass through* mentioned there (Lv. 18:21)
specifies *fire*.
And just as *pass through* mentioned there
specifies Molekh (Lv. 18:21),
so, too, *pass through* mentioned here
specifies Molekh (Dt. 18:10).
**It turns out that you can say:**
**[The proscription applies]**
**only when one hands over and passes**
**[the child *first]* through fire and [*afterward]* through Molekh.**
**Indeed—[the proscription] depends upon both verses.**
**Had they not been stated [in complementary terms],**
**we’d have heard no proscription**.¹⁶³

דָּבָר אַחֵר: **מַעֲבִיר בְּנוֹ וּבִתּוֹ בָּאֵשׁ** – זֶה הַבּוֹעֵל אֲרַמִּית וּמַעֲמִיד מִמֶּנָּה בֵּן אוֹיֵב לַמָּקוֹם. עֹנֶשׁ שָׁמַעְנוּ, אַזְהָרָה לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ! תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **לֹא יִמָּצֵא בְךָ מַעֲבִיר בְּנוֹ וּבִתּוֹ בָּאֵשׁ**. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: זֶה שֶׁהוּא מַעֲבִיר בְּנוֹ וּבִתּוֹ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְכוֹרֵת עִמָּהּ בְּרִית, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ירמיה לד יח): ״הָעֵגֶל אֲשֶׁר כָּרְתוּ לִשְׁנַיִם וַיַּעַבְרוּ בֵּין בְּתָרָיו״.


4. Another word :
[he infers the portent of]
a fox that passes on his right or his left.
Another word:
“Any one who passes his *son* or *daughter* through fire” (Dt. 18:10)—
this refers to one who
sexually mounts an Aramean¹⁶⁶ woman,
and then raises with her a son,
who becomes an enemy of the All-Present.
We have heard the punishment [for this],
but we haven’t heard the warning [against it]!
The Teaching states:
“There *shall not* be found among you
anyone who passes his son or daughter through fire” (Dt. 18:10)—
[this is certainly sufficient warning]!
R. Judah says:
This refers to one who passes his son or daughter
through [the rite of] a foreign cult,
and *cuts*¹⁶⁷ in this context, “cutting” means to “seal a pact.” a covenant with it.
As it is said:
“Like the calf which they *cut* in two¹⁶⁸
and then passed between the parts” (Jer. 34:18). ¹⁶⁹

footnotes:
¹⁶⁶ That is, a gentile.
¹⁶⁷ Heb: koret;
¹⁶⁸ Jeremiah’s reference is to the description of “the covenant between the parts” at Gn. 15:9-19.
¹⁶⁹ F:218, ls. 10-13 regards 161.4 as a marginal insertion.

**before responding**.¹⁷² per. 6:2, T. Shab. 7:14.

רַבִּי עֲקִיבָה אוֹמֵר: אֵלּוּ נוֹתְנֵי הָעִתִּים, כְּגוֹן אֵלּוּ הָאוֹמְרִים: לִמּוּדֵי עַרְבִית שְׁבִיעִיּוֹת לִהְיוֹת חִטִּים יָפוֹת, עֲקוּרוֹת קִטְנִיּוֹת לִהְיוֹת רָעוֹת. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵלּוּ אוֹחֲזֵי הָעֵינַיִם.

**These declare auspicious times [for commerce].**
**For example, they might say:**

**the wheat harvest will be exceptional,**
**but [trade in] uprooted beans will be bad.**
**And sages say:**
**These deceive the eyes**¹⁷³ A second word-play based upon the root, *`-y-n.*
**[through apparitions].**¹⁷⁴

6. **“Or an omen-whisperer”**¹⁷⁵ “to hiss.” See *nakhash* (“snake”) below. **(Dt. 18:10).**

**Or: a snake (*nakhash*) is passing to my right,**
**or a fox to my left,**
**or a deer is blocking my way!**

**וּמְכַשֵּׁף**, הָעוֹשֶׂה מַעֲשֶׂה, וְלֹא הָאוֹחֵז אֶת הָעֵינַיִם. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָה אוֹמֵר מִשֵּׁם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: שְׁנַיִם מְלַקְּטִים קִשּׁוּאִים, אֶחָד מְלַקֵּט וְהוּא פָּטוּר, וְאֶחָד מְלַקֵּט וְהוּא חַיָּב. הָעוֹשֶׂה מַעֲשֶׂה חַיָּב, הָאוֹחֵז אֶת הָעֵינַיִם פָּטוּר.


7. **“Or a sorcerer” (*mechashef;* Dt. 18;10).**
**This is one who tricks,**
**but not by deceiving the eyes**
**[through apparitions].**
**R. Akiva says in the name of R. Joshua:**
**Two [sorcerers] are gathering squash—**
**one gathers [the entire field] and is exempt**
**[from suspicion of using sorcery,]**
**while the other gathers [the entire field] and is liable.**
**[Now why is this so?]**
**The one actually *performing* the trick is liable,**
**but the one who only *deceives the eyes* is exempt!**¹⁷⁸

**וְדֹרֵשׁ אֶל הַמֵּתִים**, אֶחָד הַמַּעֲלֶה בִזְכוּרוֹ וְאֶחָד הַנִּשְׁאָל בְּגֻלְגֹּלֶת. מַה בֵּין מַעֲלֶה בִזְכוּרוֹ לְנִשְׁאָל בְּגֻלְגֹּלֶת? מַעֲלֶה בִזְכוּרוֹ אֵין עוֹלֶה כְּדַרְכּוֹ וְאֵין נִשְׁאָל בְּשַׁבָּת, וְהַנִּשְׁאָל בְּגֻלְגֹּלֶת עוֹלֶה כְּדַרְכּוֹ וְנִשְׁאָל בְּשַׁבָּת.


2. “Or a petitioner of the dead”¹⁸⁴ (Dt. 18:11).
All the same is
[the rule regarding]
one who conjures through a necromantic apparition¹⁸⁵ H:201 translates: “by divination”; JN2:49: “through his penis.” See Rashi, B. San. 65b, s.v., *zachrut.*
and one who petitions a skull.
What is the difference between [the results of]
conjuring through a necromantic apparition
and petitioning a skull?
The one who conjures a necromantic apparition—
[the ghost] does not reliably arise,
and accepts no petitions on the Sabbath.
But the one who petitions a skull—
[the ghost] reliably arises,
and accepts petitions on the Sabbath.

## Paragraph 173

###### Sifrei Devarim 173:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/173:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/173:1)


(דברים יח יב) **כִּי תוֹעֲבַת ה׳ כָּל עֹשֵׂה אֵלֶּה**, יָכוֹל לֹא יְהֵא חַיָּב עַד שֶׁיַּעֲבוֹר עַל כֻּלָּם? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **כָּל עֹשֵׂה אֵלֶּה** אֲפִלּוּ עַל אַחַת מֵהֶם.


**Pisqa’ 173**¹⁸⁶
1. “Indeed, *all* who commit *these acts* are abominable to HASHEM” (Dt. 18:12).
Is it possible to say that
he should not be held liable
[for violating *any* of them]
until transgressing *all* of them?
The Teaching states:
“*All* who commit *these acts*” (Dt. 18:12)—
even if he transgresses only *one* of them.

footnotes:
¹⁸⁶ H:201; JN2:50-51.


###### Sifrei Devarim 173:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/173:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/173:2)


**וּבִגְלַל הַתּוֹעֵבֹת הָאֵלֶּה ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ מוֹרִישׁ אוֹתָם מִפָּנֶיךָ**, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהוּזְהֲרוּ כְּנַעֲנִים עַל כָּל הַמַּעֲשִׂים הָאֵלּוּ, שֶׁאֵין עוֹנְשִׁים אֶת הָאָדָם עַד שֶׁמַּזְהִירִים אוֹתוֹ. כְּשֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מַגִּיעַ לְפָסוּק זֶה הָיָה אוֹמֵר: חֲבָל עָלֵינוּ, וּמָה מִי שֶׁמִּדַּבֵּק בַּטֻּמְאָה – רוּחַ טֻמְאָה שׁוֹרָה עָלָיו, הַמִּדַּבֵּק בַּשְּׁכִינָה – דִּין הוּא שֶׁתִּשְׁרֶה עָלָיו רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ! וּמִי גָּרַם? (ישעיה נט ב) ״עֲוֹנוֹתֵיכֶם הָיוּ מַבְדִּילִים בֵּינֵיכֶם וּבֵין אֱלֹהֵיכֶם״.


2. “*Because of* these abominations, HASHEM your God has *dispossessed* them
from before you” (Dt. 18:12).
**Said R. Shimon:**
**This teaches that**
**the Canaanites were forewarned**
**about all these practices—**
**for they do not punish a person**
**unless he has also been forewarned.**¹⁸⁷
When R. Eliezer would reach this verse,
he would say: More’s the pity!
Just as a person who clings to uncleanness—
the stink of uncleanness hovers over him,
doesn’t reason demand that
one who clings to the Presence—
the aroma of the spirit of the Holy One hovers over him?
So what happened?
“Your iniquities have sundered you from your God” (Is. 59:2)

footnotes:
¹⁸⁷ //T. AZ.8:6.


###### Sifrei Devarim 173:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/173:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/173:3)


(דברים יח יג) **תָּמִים תִּהְיֶה עִם ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ**, כְּשֶׁאַתָּה תָם – חֶלְקְךָ עִם ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ. וְכֵן דָּוִד אָמַר (תהלים כו יא): ״וַאֲנִי בְּתֻמִּי אֵלֵךְ – פְּדֵנִי וְחָנֵּנִי״, (תהלים מא יג) ״וַאֲנִי בְּתֻמִּי – תָּמַכְתָּ בִּי וַתַּצִּיבֵנִי לְפָנֶיךָ לְעוֹלָם״.


3. “Be *whole* (*tamim*) with HASHEM your God” (Dt. 18:13).
If you *are innocent*,¹⁸⁸.The assonance of *tam* (“complete, whole, innocent”) and *tamim* (“perfect”) governs the exegetical thought of this unit.
your portion is with HASHEM your God.
And so David said:
“And I, in my innocence,¹⁸⁹ shall walk.
Spare me and show me mercy” (Ps. 26:11).
[And, moreover:]
“And I—in my innocence, you supported me,
and helped me stand before You forever” (Ps. 41:13).

footnotes:
¹⁸⁸ Heb: tam
¹⁸⁹ Heb: tummi.


###### Sifrei Devarim 173:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/173:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/173:4)


**תָּמִים תִּהְיֶה עִם ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ**, אִם עָשִׂיתָ כָּל הָאָמוּר בָּעִנְיָן – הֲרֵי אַתָּה תָּמִים לַה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ.


[Finally the verse states here:]
“Be whole with HASHEM your God” (Dt. 18:13)—
that is, if you perform all that is specified in this passage,
you will indeed be whole with HASHEM your God.



## Paragraph 174

###### Sifrei Devarim 174:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/174:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/174:1)


(דברים יח יד) **כִּי הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה יוֹרֵשׁ אוֹתָם**, עֲשֵׂה מִצְוָה הָאֲמוּרָה בָּעִנְיָן, שֶׁבִּשְׂכָרָהּ אַתָּה יוֹרֵשׁ אֶת הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה.


**Pisqa’ 174**¹⁹⁰
1. “For these nations which you are dispossessing” (Dt. 18:14).
**Perform the commandment specified in this context,**
**for by virtue of this will you dispossess these nations**.¹⁹¹ 156.1, 162.1, 170.1, 173.3, 174.1, 297, etc., for Sifre’s usage of this very common trope.

footnotes:
¹⁹⁰ H:201-202; JN2:52.
¹⁹¹ Cf. Pisqa’ot


###### Sifrei Devarim 174:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/174:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/174:2)


**אֶל מְעוֹנְנִים וְאֶל קוֹסְמִים יִשְׁמָעוּ**, שֶׁמָּא תֹאמַר: לָהֶם יֵשׁ בַּמֶּה לְהִשָּׁאֵל וְלִי אֵין לִי? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וְאַתָּה לֹא כֵן: נָתַן לְךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ**. נָתַן לְךָ – לְךָ נִתְּנָה, וְאַתָּה מַנִּיחַ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּמִתְעַסֵּק בְּבִטּוּלָהּ?


2. “They consulted the oracles and augurs” (Dt. 18:14).
Lest you say—
they have oracular methods, but I do not!
The Teaching states:
“But, as for you, you are not permitted to do this to HASHEM your God” (Dt. 18:14).3. “Which HASHEM your God is giving you” (Dt. 18:9).
The Land has been given to you,
yet you abandon the words of Torah
to busy yourself in its nullification?¹⁹²

footnotes:
¹⁹² According to F:220, n.14, this material appears in very few textual testimonies and is probably a copyist’s insertion. It is also likely to be misplaced, as it cites Dr.18:9 out of sequence.



## Paragraph 175

###### Sifrei Devarim 175:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/175:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/175:1)


(דברים יח טו) **נָבִיא מִקִּרְבְּךָ** – וְלֹא מֵחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ. **מֵאַחֶיךָ** – וְלֹא מֵאֲחֵרִים. **יָקִים לְךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ** – וְלֹא לַגּוֹיִם. וּמָה אֲנִי מְקַיֵּם (ירמיה א ה) ״נָבִיא לַגּוֹיִם נְתַתִּיךָ״? בְּנוֹהֵג מִנְהַג גּוֹיִם.


**Pisqa’ 175**¹⁹³
1. “A prophet from *your midst*” (Dt. 18:15)—
but *not* from *beyond the Land*.
“From your brothers” (Dt. 18:15)—
but *not* from *[the gentile] others*.
“Shall HASHEM your God raise up for *you*” (Dt. 18:15)—
but not *for gentiles.*
Then, how do I explain this:
“I have appointed you a prophet to *the gentiles*” (Jer. 1:5)?
[This refers to Israelites] who *act* like the gentiles.

footnotes:
¹⁹³ H:201-202; JN2: 53.


###### Sifrei Devarim 175:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/175:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/175:2)


**אֵלָיו תִּשְׁמָעוּן**, אֲפִלּוּ אוֹמֵר לְךָ עֲבֹר עַל אַחַת מִן הַמִּצְווֹת הָאֲמוּרוֹת בַּתּוֹרָה כְּאֵלִיָּהוּ בְּהַר הַכַּרְמֶל – לְפִי שָׁעָה – שְׁמַע לוֹ!


“To him shall you listen” (Dt. 18:15)—
even if he commands you to transgress
one of the commandments stated in the Torah—
like Elijah on Mt. Carmel—
for the time being, obey him.



## Paragraph 176

###### Sifrei Devarim 176:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/176:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/176:1)


(דברים יח טז) **כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר שָׁאַלְתָּ מֵעִם ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּחֹרֵב** בָּזוֹ זָכוּ שֶׁיַּעַמְדוּ לָהֶם נְבִיאִים: **לֹא אוֹסִיף לִשְׁמֹעַ אֶת קוֹל ה׳ אֱלֹהַי**.


**Pisqa’ 176**¹⁹⁴
1. “According to *all you asked* from HASHEM my God at Horeb” (Dt. 18:16)—
with *this request*
they became worthy of having prophets arise for them,
[as it is said:]
“I wish no longer to hear the *voice* of HASHEM my God!” (Dt. 18:16)—
[but, rather, His message through prophecy]!

footnotes:
¹⁹⁴ H:202; JN2:54.


###### Sifrei Devarim 176:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/176:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/176:2)


(דברים יח יז) **וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ אֵלָי הֵיטִיבוּ אֲשֶׁר דִּבֵּרוּ** – כִּוְּנוּ לְדַעְתִּי, **נָבִיא אָקִים לָהֶם**. הָא לָמַדְתָּ שֶׁבִּשְׂכַר יִרְאָה שֶׁיָּרְאוּ – זָכוּ שֶׁיַּעַמְדוּ לָהֶם נְבִיאִים.


2. **“Then HASHEM said to me: their words are indeed well-chosen” (Dt. 18:17)—**
**sharing, [as they do,] My opinion!**
**“I will raise up for them a prophet” (Dt. 18:18)—**
**indeed, you learn from this that,**
**as a reward for their awe,**
**they became worthy of having prophets arise for them.**¹⁹⁵, 9. Cf. Mechilta Shimon-Nelson, *bakhodesh,* p.253.

footnotes:
¹⁹⁵ //Mechilta Ishmael, bakhodesh


###### Sifrei Devarim 176:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/176:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/176:3)


(דברים יח יח) **וְנָתַתִּי דְבָרַי בְּפִיו** – דְּבָרַי בְּפִיו אֲנִי נוֹתֵן, אֲבָל אֵינִי מְדַבֵּר עִמּוֹ פָּנִים בְּפָנִים. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **וְנָתַתִּי דְבָרַי בְּפִיו**, מִכָּן וָאֵילָךְ הֱוֵי יוֹדֵעַ הֵיאַךְ רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ נִתֶּנֶת בְּפִי הַנְּבִיאִים.


**“And I shall place my words in his mouth” (Dt. 18:18)—**
**My words will I place in his mouth,**
**but I will not speak to him face to face**
**[as I do with Moses].**¹⁹⁶ 11:8.

footnotes:
¹⁹⁶ This material, lacking in most sources for Sifre, has a loose parallel at SZ, beha`alotecha,


###### Sifrei Devarim 176:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/176:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/176:4)


**וְדִבֶּר אֲלֵיהֶם** – שֶׁלֹּא לְהוֹשִׁיב אֶת הַתּוּרְגְּמָן.


3. Another word:
“And I shall place *my words* in *his mouth*” (Dt. 18:18)—
from now on, be aware that
the *Spirit of the Holy One* is placed in the mouths of the *prophets*.
“And he will declare *to them*” (Dt. 18:18)—
with no need to appoint a translator.¹⁹⁷

**אֵת כָּל אֲשֶׁר אֲצַוֶּנּוּ** – אוֹמֵר עַל רִאשׁוֹן רִאשׁוֹן וְעַל אַחֲרוֹן אַחֲרוֹן.


“*Whatever* I shall command him” (Dt. 18:18)—
**he will explain primary points first,**

## Paragraph 177

###### Sifrei Devarim 177:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/177:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/177:1)


(דברים יח יט) **וְהָיָה הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִשְׁמַע אֶל דְּבָרַי** – שְׁלֹשָׁה מִיתָתָם בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם: הַכּוֹבֵשׁ נְבוּאָתוֹ, כְּיוֹנָה בֶן אֲמִתַּי, וְהַמְּוַתֵּר עַל דִּבְרֵי נָבִיא, כַּחֲבֵירוֹ שֶׁל מִיכָה, וְנָבִיא שֶׁעוֹבֵר עַל דִּבְרֵי עַצְמוֹ כְּעִידּוֹא. וּשְׁלֹשָׁה מִיתָתָם בְּבֵית דִּין: הַמִּתְנַבֵּא מַה שֶּׁלֹּא שָׁמַע, כְּצִדְקִיָּה בֶן כְּנַעֲנָה; וּמַה שֶּׁלֹּא נֶאֱמַר לוֹ, כַּחֲנַנְיָה בֶן עַזּוּר, שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹמֵעַ דְּבָרִים מִפִּי יִרְמְיָה שֶׁהָיָה מִתְנַבֵּא בַּשּׁוּק הָעֶלְיוֹן וְחוֹזֵר וּמִתְנַבֵּא בַּשּׁוּק הַתַּחְתּוֹן; וְהַמִּתְנַבֵּא בְּשֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְאוֹמֵר: כָּךְ אָמְרָה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, אֲפִלּוּ כִּוֵּן אֶת הַהֲלָכָה לְטַמֵּא אֶת הַטָּמֵא וּלְטַהֵר אֶת הַטָּהוֹר!


**Pisqa’ 177**¹⁹⁹
1. “Now, as for the person who does *not obey* my words” (Dt. 18:19)—
**there are three**
**who are condemned to death**
**at the hands of Heaven:**
**[A prophet] who suppresses his prophetic message,**
**like Jonah b. Amitai (Jon. 1:1-3);**
**one who adds his words to the words of a prophet,**
**like the companions of Micah (Jud. 17:1ff.);**
**and a prophet who violates his own prophetic message,**
**like Ido**²⁰⁰ **(1Ki. 13:11-19).**
**And there are three**
**who are condemned to death**
**at the hands of the court:**
**One who prophesies what he never heard,**
**like Zedekiah b. Chenaanah (1Ki. 22:24-28);**
**one who said what was not said to him,**
**like Hananiah b. Azzur (Jer. 28:1-17)—**
**who heard things from Jeremiah’s mouth**
**as Jeremiah delivered prophecy**
**in the Upper Market,**
**and Hananiah b. Azzur went and prophesied**
**in the Lower Market**;²⁰¹
**and one who prophesies in the name of a foreign cult,**
**saying: thus says [the god of] a foreign cult!**
**[And he is condemned to death by the court]—**
**even if his words confirm the [sages’] tradition**
**regarding what is unclean and what is clean.**²⁰²

footnotes:
¹⁹⁹ H:202-203; JN2:55
²⁰⁰ =T. San.14:15; cf. M. San. 11:5.
²⁰¹ =T. San.14:14.
²⁰² =M. San. 11:6.



## Paragraph 178

###### Sifrei Devarim 178:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/178:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/178:1)


(דברים יח כ) **אַךְ הַנָּבִיא אֲשֶׁר יָזִיד לְדַבֵּר דָּבָר בִּשְׁמִי וּמֵת** – בִּסְתָם מִיתָה הָאֲמוּרָה בַּתּוֹרָה, בְּחֶנֶק.


**Pisqa’ 178**²⁰³
1. “But the prophet so defiant as to speak a word in My Name
which I did not order him to speak . . .*shall die*” (Dt. 18:20).
**Where the mode of execution is unspecified by the Torah,**
**we assume strangulation**.²⁰⁴ 155.1 and Mechilta Ishmael, *neziqin*, 5.

footnotes:
²⁰³ H:203; JN2:56-57.
²⁰⁴ See, for example, Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 178:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/178:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/178:2)


(דברים יח כא) **וְכִי תֹאמַר**, עֲתִידִים אַתֶּם לוֹמַר **אֵיכָה נֵדַע הַדָּבָר**; יִרְמְיָה אָמַר: הִנֵּה כְּלֵי בֵית ה׳ הוֹלְכִים בָּבֶלָה (ראו ירמיה כז כב) וַחֲנַנְיָה אוֹמֵר (ירמיה כז טז): ״הִנֵּה כְּלֵי בֵית ה׳ מוּשָׁבִים מִבָּבֶל״, וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ לְמִי אֶשְׁמַע! תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (דברים יח כב): **אֲשֶׁר יְדַבֵּר הַנָּבִיא בְּשֵׁם ה׳ וְלֹא יִהְיֶה הַדָּבָר וְלֹא יָבֹא הוּא הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר לֹא דִבְּרוֹ ה׳**. אֵיזֶהוּ דָּבָר שֶׁדִּבְּרוֹ הַמָּקוֹם? זֶה שֶׁאוֹמֵר וּבָא. **בְּזָדוֹן דִּבְּרוֹ הַנָּבִיא**, עַל זָדוֹן הוּא חַיָּב, וְאֵינוֹ חַיָּב עַל שְׁגָגָה.


2. “Now, if you should say in your heart: *how shall we know* . . .” (Dt. 18:21)?
In the future, you will say:
*How shall we know* the truth of the matter?
For Jeremiah said:
“Look! All the utensils of the House of HASHEM
will be deported to Babylonia!” (cf. Jer. 27:22).
But Hananiah said:
“Look! All the utensils of the House of HASHEM
will be returned from Babylonia!” (Jer. 27:16)—.
and *I don’t know* whom to believe!3. The Teaching states:
“When the prophet speaks . . ., and *the event never transpires* . . .,
*this* is the thing that HASHEM has *not* spoken” (Dt. 18:22).
Now, of which prophetic utterance
did the All-Present really speak?
The one which [the prophet] fore-told
*and it actually transpired*.
[But as for the prophet
whose prediction did not transpire:]
“That prophet has spoken in defiance” (Dt. 18:22)—
he is therefore held liable to strangulation
for intentional transgression,
but he bears no liability
for inadvertent transgression.


###### Sifrei Devarim 178:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/178:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/178:3)


**לֹא תָגוּר מִמֶּנּוּ**, אַל תִּמְנַע עַצְמְךָ מִלְּלַמֵּד עָלָיו חוֹבָה.


“Have no fear of him” (Dt. 18:22)—
don’t hesitate to testify in court
for the prosecution.



## Paragraph 179

###### Sifrei Devarim 179:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/179:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/179:1)


(דברים יט א) **כִּי יַכְרִית ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶת הַגּוֹיִם**, בִּזְכוּתְךָ.


**Pisqa’ 179**²⁰⁵
1. “When HASHEM your God cuts down *the gentiles*” (Dt. 19:1)—
because *you* deserve it.

footnotes:
²⁰⁵ H: 203-204; JN2: 58-59.


###### Sifrei Devarim 179:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/179:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/179:2)


**וִירִשְׁתָּם וְיָשַׁבְתָּ בְעָרֵיהֶם וּבְבָתֵּיהֶם**, מִכְּלָל שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר **וְיָשַׁבְתָּ בְעָרֵיהֶם וּבְבָתֵּיהֶם** יָכוֹל אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁי לְהוֹסִיף עַל הַבִּנְיָן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (דברים יב כט): ״וְיָשַׁבְתָּ בְּאַרְצָם״; כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה רוֹצֶה לִבְנוֹת – בְּנֵה!


“And you dispossess them, settling in their cities and houses” (Dt. 19:1).
Inferring from what is stated—
“settling in their cities and houses” (Dt. 19:1)—
is it possible to say that
you are not free to add to existing structures?
The Teaching states:
“And *you* shall *settle* their Land” Dt. 13:29)—
*wherever* you want to build, build!

###### Sifrei Devarim 180:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/180:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/180:4)


**אֲשֶׁר ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ נוֹתֵן לְךָ לְרִשְׁתָּהּ**, מַה שֶּׁתִּירַשׁ – תִּכְבֹּשׁ.


“Which HASHEM your God is giving you to *inherit*” (Dt. 19:2)—
you will have to *conquer* whatever you inherit.


###### Sifrei Devarim 180:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/180:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/180:5)


(דברים יט ג) **תָּכִין לְךָ הַדֶּרֶךְ**, תָּכִין לְךָ סְטְרָטְיָאוֹת שֶׁיְּהוּ מְפֹרָשׁוֹת לְתוֹכָהּ.


2. “Prepare for yourself the *way*” (Dt. 19:3)—
prepare for yourself *highways* that
lead straight to it.


###### Sifrei Devarim 180:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/180:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/180:6)


**וְשִׁלַּשְׁתָּ אֶת גְּבוּל אַרְצְךָ**, שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ מְפֻזָּרוֹת אֶלָּא יִהְיוּ מְכֻוָּנוֹת, כִּשְׁתֵּי שׁוּרוֹת שֶׁבַּכֶּרֶם.


**“And tri-sect the boundary of your Land” (Dt. 19:3)—**
**so that the [three cities] are not scattered,**
**but are aligned like two rows of a vineyard.**²¹⁰

footnotes:
²¹⁰ Cf. T. Mak. 2:3, M. Mak.2:5.


###### Sifrei Devarim 180:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/180:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/180:7)


**אֲשֶׁר יַנְחִילְךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ** – לְרַבּוֹת עֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן.


**“Which HASHEM your God is bequeathing to you” (Dt. 19:3)—**
**this includes the trans-Jordanian territories**
**[of Gad, Reuben, and Menasseh].**²¹¹ 164.1

footnotes:
²¹¹ Cf. Sifre Nu, 160 and Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 180:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/180:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/180:8)


**וְהָיָה לָנוּס שָׁמָּה כָּל רוֹצֵחַ**, שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה גוֹלֶה מֵעִיר לְעִיר.


“So that any one who unwittingly kills [an innocent party]
might seek *asylum* there” (Dt. 19:3)—
so that he needn’t be expelled from city to city.²¹² 183.2

footnotes:
²¹² Cf. Pisqa’



## Paragraph 181

###### Sifrei Devarim 181:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/181:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/181:1)


(דברים יט ד) **וְזֶה דְּבַר הָרוֹצֵחַ**, מִכָּן אַתָּה אוֹמֵר (מכות ב ח) רוֹצֵחַ שֶׁגּוֹלֶה מֵעִיר לְעִיר מִקְלָט.


**Pisqa’ 181**²¹³
1. “Now, *this rule* is applied to the *unwitting* killer” (Dt. 19:4).
On this basis you teach:
**An unwitting killer who is expelled**
**to the city of [his] refuge,**
**{and whom the residents of that city**
**wish to honor —**
**he must inform them:**
**I am a killer!**
**If they reply: Even so!—**
**he may accept the honor,**
**for it is said:**
**“This rule is applied to the unwitting killer”}**²¹⁴ ****(Dt. 19:4).

footnotes:
²¹³ H:204-205; JN2:61-62.
²¹⁴ =T.Mak.3:8, M. Mak.2:8. Sifre’s text is abbreviated. I have supplied in brackets that omits the bulk of the mishnaic-toseftan citation. See H: 458, n.2.


###### Sifrei Devarim 181:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/181:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/181:2)


מִכְּלָל שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים יט ו) ״פֶּן יִרְדֹּף גֹּאֵל הַדָּם אַחֲרֵי הָרוֹצֵחַ״, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא רוֹדֵף וְגוֹאֵל; רוֹדֵף וְלֹא גוֹאֵל, גּוֹאֵל וְלֹא רוֹדֵף, לֹא רוֹדֵף וְלֹא גוֹאֵל מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: רֹצֵחַ רֹצֵחַ, רִבָּה.


2. Inferring from what is stated:
“Lest the blood-avenger pursue the unwitting killer” (Dt. 19:6)—
I know only about a case involving
a pursuer who is himself the blood-avenger.²¹⁵
But on what basis do I rule when
the pursuer is *not* the blood-avenger,
[and who must fear family-vengeance or the court]?
Or, the blood-avenger is not the pursuer
[and, therefore, is not entitled to exact vengeance]?
Or, neither the pursuer nor the blood-avenger
[has been clearly identified]?
The Teaching states:
“*Unwitting* killer” (Dt. 19:4), and repeats,
“Unwitting *killer*” (Dt. 19:6) in order to mandate an inclusive rule
[protecting anyone who avenges the blood of an innocent victim].

footnotes:
²¹⁵ Therefore, the pursuer needn’t fear the vengeance of the killer’s family or the justice of the court


###### Sifrei Devarim 181:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/181:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/181:3)


מִכְּלָל שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״כִּי יֵחַם לְבָבוֹ״, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ חַמּוּת הַלֵּב; הָאָב אֶת הַבֵּן וְהַבֵּן אֶת הָאָב מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: רֹצֵחַ רֹצֵחַ, רִבָּה.


3. Inferring from what is stated:
“For his heart boiled with rage” (Dt. 19:6),
**I know only about a case**
**involving an avenger who suffers boiling rage**.²¹⁶
But on what basis do I rule when
a father must take vengeance upon his child,
or a child upon his father?²¹⁷
The Teaching states:
“*Unwitting* killer” (Dt. 19:4), and repeats,
“Unwitting *killer*” (Dt. 19:6) in order to mandate an inclusive rule
[in which the avenger’s state of mind doesn’t weaken his claim to the city’s protection].

footnotes:
²¹⁶ Cf. Sifre Nu. 160.
²¹⁷ Since that father will have compassion on his son, the killer—does he forfeit the protection of the city of refuge?


###### Sifrei Devarim 181:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/181:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/181:4)


מַה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר **שָׁמָּה שָׁמָּה שָׁמָּה** שְׁלֹשָׁה פְעָמִים? שָׁם תְּהֵא דִירָתוֹ, שָׁם תְּהֵא מִיתָתוֹ, שָׁם תְּהֵא קְבוּרָתוֹ.


4. What does the Teaching add
by the three-fold repetition of the term:
“There” (Nu. 35:6), “there” (Nu. 35:11), and “there” (Nu. 35:15)?
***There* in the city of his refuge, shall he *reside*,**
***there* shall he *die*,**
***there* shall he *be buried***.²¹⁸

footnotes:
²¹⁸ = M.Mak.2:7; T.Mak.3:5.


###### Sifrei Devarim 181:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/181:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/181:5)


מַה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר **רֵעֵהוּ רֵעֵהוּ רֵעֵהוּ** שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים? רֵעֵהוּ – פְּרָט לַאֲחֵרִים, רֵעֵהוּ – פְּרָט לְגֵר תּוֹשָׁב, רֵעֵהוּ – כְּבָר קְרָאַתּוּ הַתּוֹרָה רֵעֵהוּ! **אֲשֶׁר יַכֶּה אֶת רֵעֵהוּ בִּבְלִי דַעַת וְהוּא לֹא שֹׂנֵא לוֹ**, הָא אִם שׂוֹנֵא לוֹ – אֵינוֹ גוֹלֶה.


5. What does the Teaching add
by the three-fold repetition of the term:
**“His kinsman” (Dt. 19:4), “his kinsman” (Dt. 19:5), and “his kinsman” (Dt. 19:5)?**²¹⁹ without intending to or previously hating him, or joined his *kinsman* in the forest to chop wood, . . . and the axe-handle struck his *kinsman*, and he died.” See *Pisqa’* 182 below
**The [first] k*insman* excludes [gentile] others**
**[from the rule of blood-vengeance];**²²⁰
**The [second] *kinsman* excludes the resident alien;**²²¹
**In [the third] *kinsman*—the Torah now calls the victim *kinsman***
**“When he strikes his *kinsman* unwittingly**
***without having hated him*” (Dt. 19:4).**
**So, if he’d hated him,**
**he *wouldn’t* be expelled from his city?**²²²

footnotes:
²¹⁹ Dt. 19:4-5 reads: “One who beat his kinsman
²²⁰ A gentile who unwittingly kills a gentile or an Israelite is neither protected from blood-vengeance nor entitled to take it. See M. Mak.2:3.
²²¹ =M. Mak.2:3, Acccording to this Mishnah: “A resident alien may not be expelled from his city except for causing the unwitting death of another resident alien.”.
²²² Cf. M. Mak.2:3.


###### Sifrei Devarim 181:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/181:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/181:6)


**מִתְּמוֹל שִׁלְשֹׁם**, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: תְּמוֹל – שְׁנַיִם, שִׁלְשֹׁם – שְׁלֹשָׁה.


“Either *yesterday* or the *day before*” (Dt. 19:4)—
R. Judah says:
*Yesterday*—counts for two days;
*The day before*—makes it three.²²³

footnotes:
²²³ Thus, prior to the inadvertent killing, at least three days without anger must have elapsed for the rule of blood-vengeance to protect the avenger from retaliation.



## Paragraph 182

###### Sifrei Devarim 182:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/182:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/182:1)


(דברים יט ה) **וַאֲשֶׁר יָבֹא אֶת רֵעֵהוּ בַּיַּעַר**, מָה יַּעַר, רְשׁוּת לַנִּזָּק וְלַמַּזִּיק לִכָּנֵס שָׁם – אַף כָּל שֶׁהוּא רְשׁוּת לַנִּזָּק וְלַמַּזִּיק לִכָּנֵס לְשָׁם. יָצָאת חֲצַר שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת שֶׁאֵין רְשׁוּת לַנִּזָּק וְלַמַּזִּיק לִכָּנֵס שָׁם.


**Pisqa’ 182**²²⁴
1. “When he goes into the forest with his kinsman” (Dt. 19:5)
[and an accidental death results,]—
**just as a forest affords both**
**the injured and the injurer**
**equally free access,**
**[where each party is responsible**
**for his own safety,]**
**so, too, any place**
**which affords to the injured and the injurer**
**equally free access**
**[imposes upon each party responsibility**
**for his own safety].**
**This precludes application of the rule**
**[of the unwitting killer]**
**to [an accidental death in] a householder’s courtyard,**
**for it does *not* afford to the injured and the injurer**
**equally free access.**²²⁵

footnotes:
²²⁴ H:205; JN2:63-65.
²²⁵ =M. Mak.2:2. The injured party must receive permission from the householder to be in the latter’s courtyard.


###### Sifrei Devarim 182:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/182:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/182:2)


**לַחְטֹב עֵצִים**, אַבָּה שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: מַה חֲטִיבַת עֵצִים רְשׁוּת – אַף כָּל שֶׁהוּא רְשׁוּת, יָצָא הָאָב הַמַּכֶּה אֶת בְּנוֹ, וְהָרַב הָרוֹדֶה אֶת תַּלְמִידוֹ, וּשְׁלִיחַ בֵּית דִּין.


2. “To chop wood” (Dt. 19:5).
**Abba Saul says:**
**Just as wood-chopping, is an optional act**
**[that may result in an accidental death],**
**so, too, any optional act**
**[resulting in an accidental death**
**releases the injuring party from the charge of murder].**
**This excludes from our rule**
**the father who [inadvertently]**
**beats his son to death**
**[since disciplining the son is not optional],**
**the master who [inadvertently]**
**whips his disciple to death**
**[while disciplining him],**
**or an agent of the court**
**[who accidentally kills a prisoner**
**while administering lashes].**²²⁶, 4. In each case, the death was caused by a well-intentioned, but misapplied, desire to fulfill the commandment to administer corporal punishment.

footnotes:
²²⁶ =M. Mak.2:2; //T. Mak.2:5, cf. Mechilta Ishmael, neziqin



## Paragraph 183

###### Sifrei Devarim 183:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/183:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/183:1)


**וְנִדְּחָה יָדוֹ בַגַּרְזֶן לִכְרוֹת הָעֵץ**, מִכָּן אַתָּה אוֹמֵר: נִתְכַּוֵּן לָקוּץ אֶת הָאִילָן וְנָפַל עַל אָדָם וַהֲרָגוֹ – הֲרֵי זֶה גּוֹלֶה.


**Pisqa’ 183**²²⁷
1. “And his hand wields the ax to cut down the tree” (Dt. 19:5).
On this basis you can teach:
**if he intended to fell the tree,**
**but it fell on a person, killing him—**
**indeed, this one is expelled from his city**

footnotes:
²²⁷ H:205-206; JN2: 64-65.


###### Sifrei Devarim 183:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/183:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/183:2)


**וְנָשַׁל הַבַּרְזֶל מִן הָעֵץ** הַמְבַקֵּעַ, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: **מִן הָעֵץ** הַמִּתְבַּקֵּעַ.


**[to the city of refuge].**²²⁸
“And the iron ax-head slipped from the wood” (Dt. 19:5)—
**that is, [from the wooden handle] wielded by the chopper.**
**Rabbi says:**
**from the wood being chopped.**²²⁹
“And found his kinsman” (Dt. 19:5)—
this refers to [a victim] already in [harm’s] way.

footnotes:
²²⁸ //T. Mak.2:1.
²²⁹ //T. Mak.2:6.


###### Sifrei Devarim 183:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/183:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/183:3)


**וּמָצָא**, בַּמָּצוּי. מִכָּן הָיָה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: אִם מִשֶּׁיָּצָאת אֶבֶן מִיָּדוֹ הוֹצִיא הַלָּה אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ וְקִבְּלָהּ – הֲרֵי זֶה פָּטוּר.


2. On this basis
**R. Eliezer b. Jacob would say:**
**[Where a person threw a stone in the public domain],**
**if at the time the stone left his hand,**
**someone stuck his head out of a window,**
**and he took the blow—**
**this stone-thrower is exempt**
**[from the charge of murder]**.²³⁰

footnotes:
²³⁰ =M. Mak.2:2. 181.5


###### Sifrei Devarim 183:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/183:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/183:4)


**הוּא יָנוּס אֶל אַחַת הֶעָרִים הָאֵלֶּה וָחָי**, שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא גּוֹלֶה מֵעִיר לְעִיר.


“He shall take refuge in *one* of these cities and live” (Dt. 19:5)—
so that he needn’t be expelled from city to city.²³¹ 180.2

footnotes:
²³¹ Cf. Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 183:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/183:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/183:5)


(דברים יט ו) **פֶּן יִרְדֹּף גֹּאֵל הַדָּם אַחֲרֵי הָרוֹצֵחַ**, מִצְוָה בְּיַד גּוֹאֵל הַדָּם לִרְדֹּף.


3. “Lest the *blood-avenger* pursue the unwitting killer” (Dt. 19:6)—
the *blood-avenger* is responsible for pursuit.


###### Sifrei Devarim 183:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/183:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/183:6)


**כִּי יֵחַם לְבָבוֹ וְהוּא לֹא שֹׂנֵא הוּא לוֹ**, הָא אִם שׂוֹנֵא – אֵינוֹ גוֹלֶה.


“For his heart boiled in rage, yet he *hadn’t hated* him” (Dt. 19:7)—
**So, if he’d hated him,**
**he wouldn’t be expelled from his city**?²³² 181.5.

footnotes:
²³² //M. Mak.2:2. See also Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 183:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/183:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/183:7)


**מִתְּמוֹל שִׁלְשׁוֹם**, זוֹ שֶׁרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: תְּמוֹל – שְׁנַיִם; שִׁלְשׁוֹם – שְׁלֹשָׁה.


“Either *yesterday* or *the day before*” (Dt. 19:7)—
R. Judah says:
*Yesterday* counts for two days;
*The day before* makes it three


###### Sifrei Devarim 183:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/183:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/183:8)


(דברים יט ז) **עַל כֵּן אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ לֵאמֹר** – לְהַזְהִיר בֵּית דִּין עַל כָּךְ.


“Therefore, I command you, saying” (Dt. 19:7)—
**this clause cautions the court**
**to be vigilant [in applying the rule].**²³³ 171.1.

footnotes:
²³³ Cf. Pisqa’



## Paragraph 184

###### Sifrei Devarim 184:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/184:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/184:1)

## Paragraph 185

###### Sifrei Devarim 185:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/185:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/185:1)


(דברים יט ט) **כִּי תִשְׁמֹר אֶת כָּל הַמִּצְוָה הַזֹּאת לַעֲשֹׂתָהּ... וְיָסַפְתָּ לְךָ עוֹד שָׁלֹשׁ עָרִים עַל הַשָּׁלֹשׁ הָאֵלֶּה**, מִכָּן אַתָּה אוֹמֵר: שָׁלֹשׁ עָרִים הִפְרִישׁ מֹשֶׁה בְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן, וּכְשֶׁבָּאוּ לָאָרֶץ הִפְרִישׁוּ עוֹד שָׁלֹשׁ וְלֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא מַפְרִישִׁים עוֹד שָׁלֹשׁ; שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ – הֲרֵי שֵׁשׁ, וְעוֹד שָׁלֹשׁ – הֲרֵי תֵּשַׁע.


**Pisqa’ 185**²³⁶
1. “If you preserve all this commandment, to perform it . . .,
then you shall add for yourself *another three cities* to these *three*” (Dt. 19:9).
On this basis you teach:
**Moses designated *three* cities**
**in the trans-Jordan (Nu. 35:14).**
**Upon reaching the Land**
**they designated *three* more (Nu. 35:14)**
**And in the future [after the conquest of the Land],**
**they will designate another *three*.**
**Three plus three—that equals six,**
**and *another three* (Dt. 19:9)—equals nine.**²³⁷ 164.1.

footnotes:
²³⁶ H:206; JN2:67.
²³⁷ Cf. M.Mak. 2:4. See also Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 185:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/185:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/185:2)


רַבִּי נְהוֹרַי אוֹמֵר: **שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ**, וְ**עוֹד** – הֲרֵי תֵּשַׁע, **עַל הַשָּׁלֹשׁ** – הֲרֵי שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה.


R. Nehorai says:
*Three* (Nu. 35:14) [in the trans-Jordan],
plus *three* (Nu. 35:14 [in the Land—that equals six].
*Another three* (Dt. 19:9)—that equals nine.
Plus *three* (Dt. 19:9)—equals twelve.


###### Sifrei Devarim 185:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/185:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/185:3)


רַבִּי שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: **שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ**, וְ**עוֹד** – הֲרֵי תֵּשַׁע, **עַל הַשָּׁלֹשׁ** – הֲרֵי שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה, **הָאֵלֶּה** – הֲרֵי חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה.


R. Saul says:
*Three* (Nu. 35:14) plus *three* (Nu. 35:14),
and *another three* (Dt. 19:9)—that equals nine.
Plus *three* (Dt. 19:9)—equals twelve.
“To these” (Dt. 19:9)—[implies at least three more], yielding a total of fifteen cities of refuge.

**Pisqa’ 186-187**²³⁸ labeled “186-187.” See Finkelstein’s comment at F:226, n.5. Ish-Shalom:108 suggests that the mss tradition has failed to mark a *saliq pisqa’* between 186 and 187 (which would fall, in F: 226, at the middle of l.6). Pardo notes the problem in his commentary, loc. cit., and divides the text into two units, 186 and 187, as do RH and TA. H:206 and JN2:68 follow F without comment, labeling the material here “*Pisqa’* 186-187.”

*{Pisqa 187}*²⁴⁰

(דברים יט יא) ״כִּי יִהְיֶה אִישׁ שׂוֹנֵא לְרֵעֵהוּ וְאָרַב לוֹ וְקָם עָלָיו״, מִכָּן אָמְרוּ: עָבַר אָדָם עַל מִצְוָה קַלָּה – סוֹפוֹ לַעֲבוֹר עַל מִצְוָה חֲמוּרָה. עָבַר עַל (ויקרא יט יח) ״וְאָהַבְתָּ לְרֵעֲךָ כָּמוֹךָ״ – סוֹפוֹ לַעֲבוֹר עַל ״לֹא תִקֹּם וְלֹא תִטֹּר״, וְעַל (ויקרא יט יז) ״לֹא תִשְׂנָא אֶת אָחִיךָ״, וְעַל (ויקרא כה לו) ״וְחֵי אָחִיךָ עִמָּךְ״ עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא לִידֵי שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים! לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר ״כִּי יִהְיֶה אִישׁ שׂוֹנֵא לְרֵעֵהוּ וְאָרַב לוֹ וְקָם עָלָיו״.


1. “If it happens that a person hates his kinsman, and lies in wait for him to attack him” (Dt. 19:11).
On this basis they taught:
**If someone transgresses**
**a simple commandment**
**—[suffering no consequences]—**
**he will eventually transgress**
**an arduous commandment.**
**If, for example, he transgressed**
**“You shall love your kinsman as yourself” (Lv. 19:18),**
**he will eventually transgress**
**“Do not retaliate” (Lv. 19:18) or**
**“Do not harbor a grudge” (Lv. 19:18), or**
**“Do not hate your brother” (Lv. 19:17), or**
**“So that your brother can live with you” (Lv. 25:36)—**
**until, eventually, he’ll spill blood.** ²⁴¹
This is why it is said:
“If it happens that a person hates his kinsman, and lies in wait for him to attack him,
and wounds him mortally, and he dies—then he may take refuge in one of these cities” (Dt. 19:11).
