## Paragraph 188

###### Sifrei Devarim 188:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/188:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/188:1)


(דברים יט יד) **לֹא תַסִּיג גְּבוּל רֵעֲךָ**, וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר (ויקרא יט יג) ״לֹא תִגְזֹל״, וּמַה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר **לֹא תַסִּיג**? מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכָּל הָעוֹקֵר תְּחוּמוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ עוֹבֵר בִּשְׁנֵי לָאוִים.


**Pisqa’ 188**²⁴⁹
1. “You *shall not* remove your *kinsman’s* boundary marker” (Dt. 19:14).
Hasn’t it already been stated:
“*Do not* rob” (Lv. 19:13)?
What, then, does the Teaching add by:
“You *shall not* remove . . .” (Dt. 19:14)?
It teaches that
anyone who dislodges
the boundaries of his *companion’s* territory
transgresses *these two* proscriptions—
[one against theft and the other against removing boundaries].

footnotes:
²⁴⁹ H:207-209; JN2:70-72.


###### Sifrei Devarim 188:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/188:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/188:2)


יָכוֹל בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **בְּנַחֲלָתְךָ אֲשֶׁר תִּנְחַל**. בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹבֵר בִּשְׁנֵי לָאוִים, בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ אֵינוֹ עוֹבֵר אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם לָאו אֶחָד בִּלְבַד.


2. Is it possible to say that
*these* proscriptions apply
*beyond* the Land?
The Teaching states:
“Of *your heritage* that you *will inherit*” (Dt. 19:14)—
Thus, the two proscriptions apply
*in* the Land of Israel.
But *beyond* the Land
one only transgresses a
single proscription [against robbery]

The Teaching states:

R. Yose says:
[A single witness alone] does not suffice to offer
testimony of wrong-doing [against a woman],
but he may offer testimony regarding her oaths.6. **Explained R. Yose:**
**This is a matter of logical argument!**
**Just as in a capital case [the accused’s] testimony *cannot* combine**
**with that of a single witness to his act [to yield valid testimony],**
**yet he takes an [exculpating] oath on his own volition—**
**isn’t it reasonable to suppose that**
**where [the accused’s] testimony *may* combine**
**with that of a single witness [to yield valid testimony],**
**such as, a monetary dispute,**
**[the accused surely] takes an oath on his own volition?**
**No!**
**For [the one] who takes an [exculpating] oath on his own volition,**
**[in a monetary dispute] must pay his penalty on his own admission.**
**Therefore, he may take an oath**
**that combines with that of a single witness.**²⁵⁸
**But should a person *take an oath***
**on the testimony of a single witness,**
**when, indeed, he does *not pay***
**on the testimony of a single witness?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“For *any* wrong-doing” (Dt. 19:15)—**
**on the question of his *own* wrong-doing he may *not* testify,**
**but he *may* testify by taking an oath.**²⁵⁹

**עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם**, מִכָּן אָמְרוּ: הַמְקַנֵּא לְאִשְׁתּוֹ – רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מְקַנֵּא עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם וּמַשְׁקָהּ עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד. שֶׁהָיָה בַדִּין: מָה אִם עֵדוּת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, שֶׁאֵינָהּ אוֹסַרְתָּהּ אִיסּוּר עוֹלָם – אֵין מִתְקַיֶּמֶת פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁנַיִם, עֵדוּת הָאַחֲרוֹנָה, שֶׁאוֹסַרְתָּהּ אִסּוּר עוֹלָם – אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁלֹּא תִתְקַיֵּם בְּפָחוֹת מִשְּׁנַיִם? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״, כָּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ לֹא הָיְתָה שׁוֹתָה.


“On the word of two witnesses” (Dt. 19:15).
From this verse they taught:
**One charging his wife with infidelity—**
**R. Eliezer says:**
**he *charges* her**
**on the basis of two [eye-witness testimonies],**
**and *forces* her to drink the bitter waters**
**on the basis of one.**²⁶²
**One might have reasoned:**
**just as the *first* testimony,**
**which *does not* prohibit her permanently to her husband,**
**is invalid with fewer than two witnesses,**
**isn’t it reasonable that**
**the *second* testimony—**
**which *does* prohibit her permanently to her husband,**
**[unless she passes the ordeal of the bitter waters],**
**should be invalid with fewer than two?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“And there is *no witness* to her act” (Nu. 5:13)—**
**any woman whose act *was* witnessed**
**would not drink the bitter waters**
**[since the ordeal resolves doubts about infidelity,**
**only in the absence of two witnesses].**²⁶³

**Pisqa’ 189**²⁶⁴
1. “If a *malicious* witness offers testimony against a man, charging him *arbitrarily*” (Dt. 19:16).
Actually, *malicious* implies that he has stolen
[the defendant’s reputation by]
“charging him *arbitrarily*”²⁶⁵. Cf. the usage of *sarah* (“rebellious”) at Dt. 13:6/*Pisqa’* 86.1. (Dt. 19:16).
Actually, *arbitrarily* implies commission of a transgression,
as it is said [of the lying prophet]:
“For he spoke *arbitrarily*” (Dt. 13:6).
And He says:
“This year shall you die, for you have spoken *arbitrarily* (*sarah*) of HASHEM” (Jer. 28:17).

2. “Charging *him*” (Dt. 19:16)—
this explains that a malicious witness
is liable only if he contradicts *himself*.²⁶⁶189, n. 2
On this basis they taught:
**Witnesses are deemed to be refuted**²⁶⁷ “refuted” “discredited,” also “malicious”, depending upon context.
**[and thus liable to punishment]**

**[as reported by a second pair of witnesses]**

**If [the first pair said]:**

**{If**²⁶⁹ **others replied:**
**How can you testify?**
**The victim or the murderer was with us that very day,**
**in some other place—**
**this is *not* a case of refuted witnesses,**
**[for only the first witnesses’ *testimony* is questioned, not their *character*].**
**But if others replied:**
**How can you testify?**
**For, indeed, you both were with us that very day,**
**in some other place—**
**this is a case of refuted witnesses,**
**[for the second witnesses’ testimony impugns the character of the first].**²⁷⁰
**And in capital cases, they are executed**
**on the basis of their own statements.}**

**שְׁנֵי הָאֲנָשִׁים**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵם שְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים; אִישׁ עִם אִשָּׁה, וְאִשָּׁה עִם אִישׁ, שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים זוֹ עִם זוֹ מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אֲשֶׁר לָהֶם הָרִיב״, מִכָּל מָקוֹם.


“Two *men*” (Dt. 19:17)—
I might infer only that
[judicial procedures are conducted]
when two *men* have a dispute.
On what basis do I know that
a man [can initiate legal action] against a woman,
a woman [can initiate legal action] against a man,
and that two women [can initiate legal action] against each other?
The Teaching states:
“*Who* have a dispute” (Dt. 19:17)—
with whomever.


###### Sifrei Devarim 190:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/190:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/190:3)


יָכוֹל אַף אִשָּׁה תְּהֵא כְּשֵׁרָה לְעֵדוּת? – נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״שְׁנֵי״ וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן (דברים יט טו) ״שְׁנֵי״, מַה שְׁנֵי הָאָמוּר כָּאן, אֲנָשִׁים וְלֹא נָשִׁים – אַף שְׁנֵי הָאָמוּר לְהַלָּן אֲנָשִׁים וְלֹא נָשִׁים.


Is it possible to say that
a *woman* could also be qualified to testify?
“Two (*shnei*) witnesses” (Dt. 19:15) is stated here,
and “Two (*shnayim*)²⁷⁴ Cf. H:460, *Pisqa’* 190, n. 1 witnesses” (Dt. 17:6) is stated elsewhere.
Just as the *two* stated here
specifies male witnesses, rather than women,
[*shnei* being gendered masculine],
so, the *shnayim* stated elsewhere
specifies male witnesses, rather than women.

**לִפְנֵי ה׳** – הֵם סְבוּרִים לִפְנֵי בָּשָׂר וָדָם הֵם עוֹמְדִים, וְאֵינָם אֶלָּא לִפְנֵי הַמָּקוֹם!


“Before HASHEM” (Dt. 19:17)—

**לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים וְהַשּׁוֹפְטִים אֲשֶׁר יִהְיוּ בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם**, זוֹ הִיא שֶׁאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי: וְכִי עָלְתָה עַל דַּעְתֵּנוּ שׁוֹפֵט שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְיָמֶיךָ? אֶלָּא שׁוֹפֵט שֶׁהוּא כָּשֵׁר וּמֻחְזָק לְךָ בְּאוֹתָם הַיָּמִים. הָיָה קָרוֹב וְנִתְרַחֵק – כָּשֵׁר, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר (קהלת ז י): ״אַל תֹּאמַר מֶה הָיָה״.


“Before the Priests and justices who shall preside in those days” (Dt. 19:17).
**This is what R. Yose the Galilean taught:**
**Now, can you imagine that**
**you would go to a justice**
**who is *not* alive *in those days*?**
**The point is, seek the rulings of a justice**
**who is eminently qualified.**
**If he had been kin to the litigants,**
**but then severed the connection [e.g., through death],**
**he is qualified to sit in judgment of them.**
**And in this connection,**
**He states:**
**“Do not wonder why the old days were better than today,**
**for such a question does not proceed from wisdom”** (Ecc. 7:10). ****²⁷⁵ 190.3 appears at *Pisqa’* 153.2.

4. **“Then the justices shall seek *diligently*” (Dt. 19:18).**
**And elsewhere He states:**
**“And it is reported to you, and you have heard it,**
**then you shall seek it out *diligently*” *(*Dt. 17:4).**

5. On what basis do I know that
a witness may admit to perjuring *himself*?
The Teaching states:
“And *the witness* indeed offered false testimony” (Dt. 19:18).
And on what basis do I know that
a witness may charge his *counterpart* with perjury?
The same Teaching states:
“And the *witness* indeed offered false testimony” (Dt. 19:18).
Is it possible to say that
[a charge of perjury can be lodged]
as soon as their testimony
has been investigated by the court?
The Teaching states:
“He has charged his brother *falsely*” (Dt. 19:18).
On this basis²⁷⁹), two rules may be adduced. you may conclude that
[this rule applies]
as long as the court
requires their presence for testimony,
but not as soon as their testimony has
been investigated by the court.
On this basis you might teach that
**a refuted witness may [still be] refuted**
**[for giving another false testimony],**
**even if there are a hundred of them!**²⁸⁰

(דברים יט יט) **וַעֲשִׂיתֶם לוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר זָמַם לַעֲשׂוֹת לְאָחִיו**, אִם מָמוֹן – מָמוֹן; אִם מַכּוֹת – מַכּוֹת; אִם עוֹנָשִׁים – עוֹנָשִׁים.

עֹנֶשׁ שָׁמַעְנוּ, אַזְהָרָה מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר [(שמות כ יג): ״לֹא תַעֲנֶה בְרֵעֲךָ עֵד שָׁקֶר״].

**וַעֲשִׂיתֶם לוֹ**, מִכָּן אָמְרוּ: אֵין עֵדִים זוֹמְמִים נֶהֱרָגִים עַד שֶׁיִּגָּמֵר הַדִּין, שֶׁהֲרֵי צַדּוּקִים אוֹמְרִים: עַד שֶׁיֵּהָרֵג, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים יט כא): ״נֶפֶשׁ בְּנֶפֶשׁ״.

רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר: מַה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר **וַעֲשִׂיתֶם לוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר זָמַם לַעֲשׂוֹת לְאָחִיו**? לְפִי שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּכָל עוֹנָשִׁים שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה, שֶׁהִשְׁוָה מִיתַת הָאִישׁ לְמִיתַת הָאִשָּׁה – וְזוֹמְמֵיהֶם כַּיּוֹצֵא בָהֶם. אֲבָל בַּת כֹּהֵן וּבוֹעֲלָהּ – לֹא הִשְׁוָה מִיתַת הָאִישׁ לְמִיתַת הָאִשָּׁה, אֶלָּא מִיתַת הָאִישׁ בְּחֶנֶק וּמִיתַת הָאִשָּׁה בִּשְׂרֵפָה. אֲבָל זוֹמְמִים, לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ מַה יֵּעָשֶׂה לָהֶם? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וַעֲשִׂיתֶם לוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר זָמַם לַעֲשׂוֹת לְאָחִיו** – כְּמִיתַת אָחִיו מִיתָתוֹ, וְלֹא כְּמִיתַת אֲחוֹתוֹ!


7. R. Yose the Galilean says:
What does the Teaching mean by
“And you shall do to him *as he connived* to do to his brother” (Dt. 19:19)?
For we have found:
among all the executions prescribed in the Torah,
the execution meted out to a man
is the same as that meted out to a woman.
And those who *connive* against them
share in the same.
However, regarding the daughter of a Priest
[“who has begun to fornicate” (Lv. 21:9)],
the execution meted out to the man
is not the same as that meted out to the woman.
For, the execution of the man is by strangulation,
whereas that of the woman is by burning.
But as for the conniving witnesses,
we haven’t heard what is to be done with them!
The Teaching states:
“And you shall do to him *as he connived* to do to *his brother*” (Dt. 19:19)—
his death shall be by *strangulation*, like that of *his brother*,
but not by *burning*, like that of *his sister*.

וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁהַמְבַיֵּשׁ מְשַׁלֵּם מָמוֹן? נֶאֱמַר כָּאן (דברים יט כא) ״לֹא תָחוֹס עֵינֶךָ״ וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן (דברים כה יב) ״לֹא תָחוֹס עֵינֶךָ״, מַה ״לֹא תָחוֹס עֵינֶךָ״ הָאָמוּר לְהַלָּן – מָמוֹן, אַף ״לֹא תָחוֹס עֵינֶךָ״ הָאָמוּר כָּאן – מָמוֹן.


8. On what basis do I know that
one who shames [his companion]
compensates him with wealth?
It is stated here:
“You shall cut off her hand, *show no pity*” (Dt. 25:12),
**and it is stated elsewhere :**
**“You shall *show no pity*: life for life” (Dt. 19:21).**
**Just as *show no pity* stated elsewhere**
**implies monetary compensation [for loss of a limb],**
**so, too, *show no pity* stated here**
**implies monetary compensation [for being shamed].**²⁸³ 8.

רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״יָד וְרֶגֶל״, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן (שמות כא כד) ״יָד וְרֶגֶל״, מַה ״יָד וְרֶגֶל״ הָאָמוּר לְהַלָּן – מָמוֹן, אַף ״יָד וְרֶגֶל״ הָאָמוּר כָּאן – מָמוֹן.

רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא יֵצֵא לַמִּלְחָמָה עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ לוֹ יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם וְעֵינַיִם וְשִׁנַּיִם? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (דברים יט כא-כ א): **לֹא תָחוֹס עֵינֶךָ נֶפֶשׁ בְּנֶפֶשׁ וְג׳ כִּי תֵצֵא לַמִּלְחָמָה**.

a man does not go off to war
unless he has hands, feet, eyes and teeth?

###### Sifrei Devarim 190:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/190:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/190:17)


אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? בְּמִלְחֶמֶת מִצְוָה, אֲבָל בְּמִלְחֶמֶת חוֹבָה הַכֹּל יוֹצְאִים, אֲפִלּוּ (יואל ב טז) ״חָתָן מֵחַדְרוֹ וְכַלָּה מֵחֻפָּתָהּ״. [(דברים כ א) **סוּס וָרֶכֶב**,] כְּשֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂים רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם – כָּל הַגּוֹיִם נַעֲשִׂים לִפְנֵיהֶם כְּסוּס אֶחָד, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמות טו א): ״סוּס וְרֹכְבוֹ רָמָה בַיָּם״. וְכִי סוּס אֶחָד הָיָה כו׳.


9. **Said R. Judah:**
**Under what circumstances**
**does [the exemption from war] apply?**
**If the war is obligatory (*mitzvah*)**²⁸⁶ (“optional”). That is, a war waged to expand the borders of the Land beyond those apportioned by God. Cf. *Pisqa’* 198.2
**[for the defense of the Land].**
**But if the war is imposed *(khovah*)**²⁸⁷ (“obligatory”).
**[as a response to the introduction of a foreign cult],**
**everyone must go—**
**even a bride-groom from his bedroom**
**and a bride from her wedding-canopy.**²⁸⁸ 190, ns.15-17. Cf. the parallel at T. Sotah 7:24.
“**When you go off to war against your enemies,**
**should you see *horse and chariot*” (Dt. 20:1)—**
**when Israel performs**
**the will of the All-Present,**
**all the gentile cavalry**
**is transformed before them**
**into a *single horse*,**²⁸⁹ 158.1 for a different exegesis of the use of “horse” as a collective noun.
**as it is said:**
**“He threw *horse* and rider into the sea” (Ex. 15:1).**²⁹⁰ 2.

²⁸⁷ MSS of M. Sotah 8:7 read: mitzvah
²⁸⁸ //M. Sotah 8:7. For text-critical observations, see F:232, n.1, and H:461, Pisqa’
²⁸⁹ See Pisqa’
²⁹⁰ //Mechilta Ishmael, shirah,


###### Sifrei Devarim 190:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/190:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/190:18)


**כִּי תֵצֵא לַמִּלְחָמָה עַל אוֹיְבֶיךָ** – בְּמִלְחֶמֶת הָרְשׁוּת הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר.


10. **“When you go off to war against *your* enemies” (Dt. 20:1).**
**The verse specifies an optional war (*reshut*).**²⁹¹ 198-199 for a fuller discussion of optional and obligatory warfare.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/190:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/190:19)


**עַל אוֹיְבֶיךָ** – כְּנֶגֶד אוֹיְבֶיךָ אַתָּה נִלְחָם.


**“Against *your* enemies” (Dt. 20:1)—**
**wage war against *your* enemies,**
**[but not a gentile nation’s enemies].**


###### Sifrei Devarim 190:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/190:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/190:20)


**וְרָאִיתָ סוּס וָרֶכֶב**, מָה הֵם יוֹצְאִים עָלֶיךָ בְּסוּס וָרֶכֶב – אַף אַתָּה צֵא עֲלֵיהֶם בְּסוּס וָרֶכֶב. מָה הֵם יוֹצְאִים עָלֶיךָ בְּעַם רַב – אַף אַתָּה צֵא עֲלֵיהֶם בְּעַם רַב.


**“Should you see *horse and chariot*” (Dt. 20:1)—**
**just as they attack you with horse and chariot,**
**you, too, must attack them with horse and chariot.**
**Just as they attack you with a large force,**
**you, too, must attack them with a large force.**


###### Sifrei Devarim 190:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/190:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/190:21)


**לֹא תִירָא מֵהֶם כִּי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ עִמָּךְ הַמַּעַלְךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם**, מִי שֶׁהֶעֱלָךְ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם הוּא עִמָּךְ בְּעֵת צָרָה.


**“Have no fear of them, for HASHEM your *God is with you*,**
***Who brought you up* from the land of Egypt” (Dt. 20:1)—**
**the One who brought you up from the land of Egypt,**
**is the very One Who is with you in times of trouble.**²⁹² 2, s.v. *weki sus ‘akhad hayah*

## Paragraph 191

###### Sifrei Devarim 191:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/191:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/191:1)


(דברים כ ב) **וְהָיָה כְּקָרָבְכֶם אֶל הַמִּלְחָמָה**, יָכוֹל זֶה יוֹם הַקְרִיבָם בּוֹ לַמִּלְחָמָה? כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר (דברים כ ג) ״וְאָמַר אֲלֵיהֶם שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל אַתֶּם קְרֵבִים הַיּוֹם לַמִּלְחָמָה״ הֲרֵי יוֹם הַקְרִיבָם בּוֹ לַמִּלְחָמָה אָמוּר! וּמַה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר **וְהָיָה כְּקָרָבְכֶם אֶל הַמִּלְחָמָה**? כֵּיוָן שֶׁמַּגִּיעִים לַסְּפָר – כֹּהֵן מַתְנֶה עִמָּהֶם כָּל הַתְּנָאִים הָאֵלּוּ וְאוֹמֵר אֲלֵיהֶם ״שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל״.


**Pisqa’ 191**²⁹³
1. “When you draw *close* to battle” (Dt. 20:2).
Is it possible to say that
[the Priest offers his words]
on the very day they join battle?
When Scripture states:
**“Then the Priest shall approach and say: Listen, Israel!**
**This day you are joining the battle” (Dt. 20:3)—**
**it certainly suggests that**
**[the Priest charges the troops]**
**on the very day they join battle.**
**So, what does the Teaching mean by**
**“When you draw *close* to battle” (Dt. 20:2)?**
**When they reach the perimeter**
**[of enemy territory, but before reaching the front lines,]**
**the Priest expounds for them**
**all these exemptions,**
**saying to them: “Listen Israel!” (Dt. 20:2).**²⁹⁴

²⁹³ H:212; JN2: 78.
²⁹⁴ Cf. T. Sotah 7:18.



## Paragraph 192

###### Sifrei Devarim 192:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/192:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/192:1)


(דברים כ ח) ״מִי הָאִישׁ הַיָּרֵא וְרַךְ הַלֵּבָב... וְיָסְפוּ הַשּׁוֹטְרִים״, לָמָּה נֶאֶמְרוּ כָּל הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלּוּ? שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ עָרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נְשַׁמּוֹת, כְּדִבְרֵי רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּי. בּוֹא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה חָס הַמָּקוֹם עַל כְּבוֹד הַבְּרִיּוֹת, מִפְּנֵי הַיָּרֵא וְרַךְ הַלֵּבָב כְּשֶׁהוּא חוֹזֵר, יֹאמְרוּ: שֶׁמָּא בָּנָה בַיִת, שֶׁמָּא נָטַע כֶּרֶם, שֶׁמָּא אֵרַס אִשָּׁה, וְכֻלָּם הָיוּ צְרִיכִים לְהָבִיא עֵדוּתָם – חוּץ מִן הַיָּרֵא וְרַךְ הַלֵּבָב, שֶׁעֵדָיו עִמּוֹ. שָׁמַע קוֹל הֲגָפַת תְּרִיסִים – וְנִבְעַת, קוֹל צַהֲלַת סוּסִים – וּמְרַתֵּת, קוֹל לִעוּז קְרָנִים – וְנִבְהָל, רוֹאֶה שִׁמּוּט סְיָפִים – וּמַיִם יוֹרְדִים בֵּין בִּרְכָּיו.


**Pisqa’ 192**²⁹⁵
1. **“Who is the man, fearful and faint-hearted . . .**
**And the officers shall continue” (Dt. 20:5-8).**
Why do [the officers] go into such detail
[regarding exemptions from war]?
So that the cities of Israel are not abandoned
[for lack of men to inhabit them].
In the words of Rabban Yohanan b. Zakkai:
**Come and see!**
**How the All-Present [is careful]**
**to spare the feelings of His creatures**
**who are fearful and faint-hearted!**
**When [the fearful soldier] is furloughed,**
**the other troops will wonder:**
**Perhaps he has built a new house?**
**Perhaps he has planted a vineyard?**
**Perhaps he has betrothed a woman?**
**Moreover, soldiers had to**
**supply proof [of their circumstances],**
**except for the fearful and faint-hearted,**
**whose proof is his nature.**
**At the sound of clashing shields—he recoils;**
**At the sound of horses neighing—he trembles;**
**At the sound of the trumpets—he panics;**
**he sees swords unsheathed,**
**and he wets himself!** ²⁹⁶

footnotes:
²⁹⁵ H:214-2I5; JN2:79-80. The entirety of 192.1—through “another version”—is missing in most mss and editions (F:232-233, n.11).
²⁹⁶ Cf. M.Sotah 8:5. This material is unevenly attested in the major manuscripts and edition. F:234: n. 16.


###### Sifrei Devarim 192:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/192:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/192:2)


דָּבָר אַחֵר: (דברים כ ג) **וְאָמַר אֲלֵיהֶם שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל אַתֶּם קְרֵבִים הַיּוֹם לַמִּלְחָמָה עַל אֹיְבֵיכֶם**, וְלֹא עַל אֲחֵיכֶם; לֹא יְהוּדָה עַל שִׁמְעוֹן, וְלֹא שִׁמְעוֹן עַל יְהוּדָה, שֶׁאִם תִּפְּלוּ בְּיָדָם יְרַחֲמוּ עֲלֵיכֶם, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שופטים כא ג): ״וַיֹּאמְרוּ לָמָה ה׳ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיְתָה זֹאת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״ וְחָזְרוּ וַיָּשִׁיבוּ אֶת הַשֵּׁבֶט בִּמְקוֹמוֹ. וְלֹא כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברי הימים ב כח ח): ״וַיִּשְׁבּוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאֲחֵיהֶם מָאתַיִם אֶלֶף נָשִׁים בָּנִים וּבָנוֹת, וְשָׁם הָיָה נָבִיא לַה׳ עוֹדֵד שְׁמוֹ, וַיֵּצֵא לִפְנֵי הַצָּבָא הַבָּא לְשֹׁמְרוֹן וַיֹּאמֶר לָהֶם: הִנֵּה בַּחֲמַת ה׳ אֱלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵיכֶם עַל יְהוּדָה נְתָנָם בְּיֶדְכֶם, וַתַּהַרְגוּ בָם בְּזַעַף עַד לַשָּׁמַיִם הִגִּיעַ. וְעַתָּה בְּנֵי יְהוּדָה וּבְנֵי יְרוּשָׁלִַם אַתֶּם אוֹמְרִים לִכְבֹּשׁ לַעֲבָדִים וְלִשְׁפָחוֹת לָכֶם, וְעַתָּה שִׁמְעוּנִי וְהָשִׁיבוּ הַשִּׁבְיָה אֲשֶׁר שְׁבִיתֶם מֵאֲחֵיכֶם״, כְּמָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לְהַלָּן (דברי הימים ב כח טו) ״וַיָּקֻמוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר נִקְּבוּ בְשֵׁמוֹת וַיַּחֲזִיקוּ בַשִּׁבְיָה, וְכָל מַעֲרֻמֵּיהֶם הִלְבִּישׁוּ מִן הַשָּׁלָל, וַיַּלְבִּשׁוּם וַיַּנְעִלוּם וַיַּאֲכִלוּם וַיַּשְׁקוּם וַיְסֻכוּם וַיְנַהֲלוּם בַּחֲמֹרִים לְכָל כּוֹשֵׁל, וַיְבִיאוּם יְרֵחוֹ עִיר הַתְּמָרִים אֵצֶל אֲחֵיהֶם, וַיָּשׁוּבוּ שֹׁמְרוֹן״; עַל אוֹיְבֵיכֶם אַתֶּם הוֹלְכִים, שֶׁאִם תִּפְּלוּ בְּיָדָם אֵין מְרַחֲמִים עֲלֵיכֶם.


2. Another word:
“**And he said to them: Listen Israel!**
**This day you are nearing the battle against your *enemies*” (Dt. 20:3)—**
**but not against your *brothers*!**
**This is not like Judah fighting Shimon,**
**or like Shimon fighting Judah.**
**For if one fell into the hands of the other,**
**he would show him mercy,**
**in line with what is said**
**[regarding the tribe of Benjamin]:**
**“Why, HASHEM God of Israel, has it come to this in Israel?” (Jud. 21:3)—**
**and they relented and returned the tribe**
**to its territory.**
**Now, such mercy was not the rule,**
**as it is stated [regarding the civil war**
**in the reign of King Ahaz]:**
**“And now, you aim to turn he people of Judah and natives of Jerusalem**
**into your slaves and slave-girls!” (2Chron. 28:1).**
**Yet, further on, it is said:**
**“Then the men named above took the captives in hand,**
**and clothed their naked with the spoils.**
**They clothed them, shod them, fed them, gave them drink, anointed them,**
**and provided asses to carry all the crippled,**
**bringing them near to their brothers—**
**to Jericho, the city of date-palms.**
**And then they returned to Samaria” (2Chron. 28:15).**
**But, now, you are going to battle**
**against enemies,**
**who will show you no mercy,**
**should you fall into their hands!**²⁹⁷

footnotes:
²⁹⁷ = M. Sotah 8:1.


###### Sifrei Devarim 192:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/192:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/192:3)


**אַל יֵרַךְ לְבַבְכֶם אַל תִּירְאוּ וְאַל תַּחְפְּזוּ וְאַל תַּעַרְצוּ מִפְּנֵיהֶם**. **אַל יֵרַךְ לְבַבְכֶם** – מִפְּנֵי צַהֲלַת סוּסִים, **אַל תִּירְאוּ** – מִפְּנֵי הֲגָפַת תְּרִיסִים וְשִׁפְעַת עֲקַלְגָּסִים, **וְאַל תַּחְפְּזוּ** – מִקּוֹל הַקְּרָנוֹת, **וְאַל תַּעַרְצוּ** – מִקּוֹל הַצְּוָחָה. כְּנֶגֶד אַרְבָּעָה דְבָרִים שֶׁאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם עוֹשִׂים: מְגִיפִים וּמְרִיעִים וְצוֹוְחִים וְרוֹמְסִים. **כִּי ה׳ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם הַהֹלֵךְ עִמָּכֶם**: הֵם בָּאִים בְּנִצְחוֹנוֹ שֶׁל בָּשָׂר וָדָם, וְאַתֶּם בָּאִים בְּנִצְחוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם.


3. **“Do not grow faint-hearted,do not fear, do not panic, and do not dread them” (Dt. 20:3).**
**“Do not grow faint-hearted”—at the neighing of the horses;**
**“do not fear”—the clashing of the shields**
**or the stamping of their jack-boots;**
**“do not panic”—at the blast of the trumpet;**
**“and do not dread”—the roar of the battle cry.**²⁹⁸
These correspond to the four strategies [of intimidation]
employed by the nations of the world:
clashing of shields; blasting of trumpets; battle cries; and stamping of boots.
**“But HASHEM your God is marching with you” (Dt. 20:4)—**
***they* join the battle**
**trusting in the victory of flesh and blood,**
**but *you* join the battle**
**trusting in the victory of the All-Present.** ²⁹⁹

footnotes:
²⁹⁸ = M. Sotah 8:1; Cf. M. Sotah 8:5.
²⁹⁹ = M. Sotah 8:1.



## Paragraph 193

###### Sifrei Devarim 193:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/193:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/193:1)


(דברים כ ד) **כִּי ה׳ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם הַהֹלֵךְ עִמָּכֶם**, מִי שֶׁהָיָה עִמָּכֶם בַּמִּדְבָּר – הוּא יִהְיֶה עִמָּכֶם בְּעֵת צָרָה, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר (שמות יד יד): ״ה׳ יִלָּחֵם לָכֶם וְאַתֶּם תַּחֲרִישׁוּן״.


**Pisqa’ 193**³⁰⁰
1. “**But *HASHEM your God* is marching *with you*” (Dt. 20:4).**
***The One* who was *with you* in the wasteland**
**is *the very One* who will be *with you***
**in times of trouble.**
**And so He says:**
**“HASHEM will do battle *on your behalf*, so you must be silent” (Ex. 14:14).**

footnotes:
³⁰⁰ H:214:JN2:81.


###### Sifrei Devarim 193:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/193:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/193:2)


**לְהִלָּחֵם לָכֶם עִם אוֹיְבֵיכֶם לְהוֹשִׁיעַ אֶתְכֶם** – מִשְּׂרָפִים וְעַקְרַבִּים וְרוּחוֹת הָרָעִים.


**“To do battle with your *enemies* on your behalf, to *deliver* you” (Dt. 20:4)—**
**[from human enemies, but also]**
**from poisonous snakes,**
**scorpions, and evil spirits.**


###### Sifrei Devarim 193:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/193:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/193:3)


[(דברים כ ה) **וְדִבְּרוּ הַשּׁוֹטְרִים**], עַד כָּאן מְשׁוּחַ מִלְחָמָה מְדַבֵּר. מִכָּן אֵילָךְ – **וְדִבְּרוּ הַשּׁוֹטְרִים**.


**“And the officers shall *speak*” (Dt. 20:5)—**
**till this point, the speaker is the Priest Anointed for War.**
**From this point and on,**
**“And the *officers* shall *continue speaking*” (Dt. 20:8).**


###### Sifrei Devarim 193:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/193:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/193:4)


[(דברים כ ז) אֲשֶׁר נָשָׂא אִשָּׁה –] אֲפִלּוּ אַלְמָנָה, אֲפִלּוּ שׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם, אֲפִלּוּ שָׁמַע שֶׁמֵּת לוֹ אָחִיו בַּמִּלְחָמָה – חוֹזֵר.


**“Who is the man. . .who has betrothed *a woman*” (Dt. 20:7)?**
**Even if he betrothed a widow;**
**even if she is awaiting the levir’s decision**
**[to either marry or release her];**
**even if the levir heard**
**that his [childless] brother**
**was killed in battle**
**[thus releasing her to marry anyone]—**
**all these may return from war.**³⁰¹ 196.1 for a more complete annotation of the levir and the woman awaiting his decision.

footnotes:
³⁰¹ Cf. Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 193:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/193:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/193:5)


[**יֵלֵךְ וְיָשֹׁב לְבֵיתוֹ**,] הַכֹּל שׁוֹמְעִים דִּבְרֵי כֹהֵן מֵעֶרְכֵי הַמִּלְחָמָה וְהֵם חוֹזְרִים, וּמְסַפְּקִים מַיִם וּמָזוֹן לַאֲחֵיהֶם, וּמְתַקְּנִים אֶת הַדְּרָכִים.


**“He shall go and return to his home” (Dt. 20:7)—**
**all heed the words of the Warrior Priest and return home,**
**where they supply their brothers**
**with water and food,**
**and help pave the roads.** ³⁰²

footnotes:
³⁰² // M. Sotah 8:2. The smaller type represents material unevenly attested in mss and early editions. F:234, n.3.


###### Sifrei Devarim 193:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/193:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/193:6)


**וְדִבְּרוּ הַשּׁוֹטְרִים**, יָכוֹל דְּבָרִים אֲחֵרִים? כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר (דברים כ ח) ״וְיָסְפוּ הַשּׁוֹטְרִים לְדַבֵּר אֶל הָעָם״ מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהֵם הַדְּבָרִים. וּמַה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר **וְדִבְּרוּ הַשּׁוֹטְרִים**? כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִתְחִיל שׁוֹטֵר לְדַבֵּר – כֹּהֵן מַשְׁמִיעַ לָהֶם כַּתְּנָאִים הַלָּלוּ.


2. “And the officers shall *continue speaking*” (Dt. 20:8).
Is it possible to say that
the officers used other words?
When He states:
“And the officers shall *continue speaking* to the people” (Dt. 20:8),
this teaches that these are their very words.
So, what does the Teaching add by
“And the officers *shall speak*” (Dt. 20:5)?
When the officer begins his charge,
then the Priest explains the exemptions to them.



## Paragraph 194

###### Sifrei Devarim 194:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/194:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/194:1)


(דברים כ ה) **מִי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר בָּנָה**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בָּנָה. יָרַשׁ, לָקַח, נִתַּן לוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **מִי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר בָּנָה**.


**Pisqa’ 194**³⁰³
1. **“Who is the man who has *built* a new house” (Dt. 20:5)?**
I might infer only that
[this exemption applies to]
one who *built* a house!

footnotes:
³⁰³ H:214-215; JN2:82-83.


###### Sifrei Devarim 194:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/194:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/194:2)


**בַּיִת**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בַּיִת. מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת בּוֹנֶה בֵּית הַתֶּבֶן, וּבֵית הַבָּקָר, וּבֵית הָעֵצִים, וּבֵית הָאוֹצָרוֹת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **אֲשֶׁר בָּנָה**. יָכוֹל אַף הַבּוֹנֶה בֵּית שַׁעַר, אַכְסַדְרָה וּמִרְפֶּסֶת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **בַּיִת** – מָה בַּיִת מְיֻחָד, שֶׁהוּא בֵּית דִּירָה – יָצְאוּ אֵלּוּ, שֶׁאֵינָם בֵּית דִּירָה.


**On what basis do I know to include**
**one who *inherited* a house,**
**one who *purchased* a house,**
**or one who *received it* as a gift?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“Who is the man who has *built*” (Dt. 20:5)—**
**[*building* includes any mode of acquisition].**
**“A *house*” (Dt. 20:5)—**
**I might infer only that**
**[this exemption] applies to a house (*bayit*)!**
**On what basis do I know to include**
**a storage shed for straw (*beit***³⁰⁴ is the construct state of *bayit* (Heb: “house”). The point of the exegesis is to include in the rule items designated for shelter of any kind. ***hateven),***
**a cattle-barn (*beit habaqar*),**
**a wood-shed (*beit ha`eitzim),***
**or a silo (*beit ha-‘otzarot*)*?***
**The Teaching states:**
**“Who has *built*” (Dt. 20:5)—**
**[a *house* includes any form of permanent shelter].**³⁰⁵
**If so, is it possible to say that**
**[this exemption] applies even to**
**the builder of a gate-house (*beit sha`ar*),**
**a portico, or a balcony?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“A *house*” (Dt. 20:5)—**
**Since a house is distinctive**
**in serving as a dwelling-place (*beit dirah*),**
**these structures,**
**which do not primarily serve as a dwelling-place,**
**must be excluded from the exemption.**³⁰⁶

footnotes:
³⁰⁴ Beit
³⁰⁵ //M. Sotah 8:2.
³⁰⁶ Cf. M. Sotah 8:3.


###### Sifrei Devarim 194:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/194:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/194:3)


**וְלֹא חֲנָכוֹ** – פְּרָט לְגַזְלָן.


“And who hasn’t yet dedicated it” (Dt. 20:5)—
this prevents a robber [from claiming an exemption].


###### Sifrei Devarim 194:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/194:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/194:4)


**יֵלֵךְ וְיָשֹׁב לְבֵיתוֹ** – יֵלֵךְ וְיִשְׁמַע דִּבְרֵי כֹהֵן מֵעֶרְכֵי מִלְחָמָה וְיַחֲזֹר.


2. “**He shall go and return to his *home*” (Dt. 20:5)—**
**that is, he shall go and heed**
**the instructions of the Warrior Priest to return.**


###### Sifrei Devarim 194:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/194:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/194:5)


**פֶּן יָמוּת בַּמִּלְחָמָה**, אִם אֵינוֹ שׁוֹמֵעַ לְדִבְרֵי כֹהֵן – לְסוֹף הוּא מֵת בַּמִּלְחָמָה.


**“*Lest* he die in battle” (Dt. 20:5)—**
**failing to heed the instructions of the Warrior Priest,**
**he will eventually die in battle.**³⁰⁷ 195.2.

footnotes:
³⁰⁷ Cf. Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 194:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/194:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/194:6)


**וְאִישׁ אַחֵר יַחְנְכֶנּוּ**, יָכוֹל דּוֹדוֹ וּבֶן דּוֹדוֹ? נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״אַחֵר״ וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן (דברים כ ז) ״אַחֵר״, מָה אַחֵר הָאָמוּר לְהַלָּן נָכְרִי, אַף אַחֵר הָאָמוּר כָּאן נָכְרִי.


**“And *another* man will consecrate it” (Dt. 20:5)—**
**is it possible to say that**
**his uncle or cousin might take the house? Here it is stated:**
**“*Another* man will consecrate it” (Dt. 20:5),**
**and elsewhere it is stated:**
**“*Another* man will take her” (Dt. 20:7; cf. Dt. 28:30)—**
**just as the *other man* discussed elsewhere**
**implies a stranger,**³⁰⁸ commonly denotes a gentile. Here, it refers to an Israelite who has no kinship ties to a particular Israelite family.
**so, too, the *other man* discussed here**
**implies a stranger.**³⁰⁹

³⁰⁸ Heb: nochri;
³⁰⁹ //T. Sotah 7:22.

(דברים כ ו) **וּמִי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר נָטַע**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא נָטַע. יָרַשׁ, לָקַח, נִתַּן לוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וּמִי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר נָטַע**.

**כֶּרֶם**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא כֶּרֶם. מִנַּיִן לְנוֹטֵעַ חֲמִשָּׁה אִילָנֵי מַאֲכָל, וַאֲפִלּוּ מֵחֲמֵשֶׁת הַמִּינִים? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **אֲשֶׁר נָטַע**. יָכוֹל אַף הַנּוֹטֵעַ אַרְבָּעָה אִילָנֵי מַאֲכָל וַחֲמִשָּׁה אִילָנֵי סְרָק? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **כֶּרֶם**.

**[this exemption applies]**

**or five shade trees?**³¹²
**The Teaching states:**
**“A *vineyard*” (Dt. 20:6)—**

## Paragraph 196

###### Sifrei Devarim 196:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/196:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/196:1)


(דברים כ ז) **וּמִי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר אֵרַשׂ אִשָּׁה**, אֶחָד הַמְאָרֵס אֶת הַבְּתוּלָה וְאֶחָד הַמְאָרֵס אֶת הָאַלְמָנָה, וַאֲפִלּוּ שׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם, וַאֲפִלּוּ שָׁמַע שֶׁמֵּת אָחִיו בַּמִּלְחָמָה חוֹזֵר וּבָא לוֹ.


**Pisqa’ 196**³¹⁷
1. **“Who is the man who has betrothed a *woman*” (Dt. 20:7)—**
**the same ruling applies to**
**one who betroths *a young lady*,**³¹⁸, literally, “a virgin.”
**and one who betroths a *widow*,**
**or [a woman] awaiting the levir’s**³¹⁹; “brother-in-law.” In particular, a man designated to marry the wife of his deceased, childless brother, or to release her from this marriage by a rite of “loosening the shoe” (*khalitzah;* Dt. 25:5-11 and *Pisqa’ot* 188-291.) While awaiting the *yavam’s* decision to marry or to release her, the woman occupies the status of *shomeret yevam* (“awaiting the levir”). **decision**
**[to either marry or release her],**
**or even if the levir heard**
**that his childless brother**
**was killed in battle**
**[thus releasing the wife from her obligation to the levir]—**
**all these may return [from war].**³²⁰ 193.1.

footnotes:
³¹⁷ H:216; JN2:86.
³¹⁸ Heb: betulah
³¹⁹ Heb: yavam
³²⁰ //M.Sotah 8:2; cf. T.Sotah 7:19. Cf. the virtually identical formulation at Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 196:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/196:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/196:2)


**וְלֹא לְקָחָהּ** – בְּאִשָּׁה הָרְאוּיָה לוֹ; פְּרָט לְמַחֲזִיר גְּרוּשָׁתוֹ, וְאַלְמָנָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, גְּרוּשָׁה וַחֲלוּצָה לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט, מַמְזֶרֶת וּנְתִינָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל וּבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְנָתִין וּלְמַמְזֵר.


“But he hasn’t yet taken her” (Dt. 20:7)—
the exemption applies only to
one marrying a *suitable* woman.
**This excludes the following prohibited marriages:**
**one who remarries his [divorced] wife;**
**or a widow marrying a High Priest;**
**or a divorcee, or a wife**
**—released by the levir**³²¹; “the released one.”**—**
**who marries a common Priest.**
**Or a woman of impaired lineage,**³²², “a woman born of parents whose marriage is forbidden,” e.g., of close relatives. The male correlate is *mamzer. Mamzerim* (plural) may marry other *mamzerim*, as well as *netinim,* but are prohibited from marrying Israelites of unimpaired lineage.
**or a descendant of outcastes,**³²³ literally, “one predisposed [to servitude].” The term is used as a title for descendents of the people of Gibeon who, according to Josh. 9:17-27, were condemned to serve other Israelites in perpetuity as “drawers of water and hewers of wood.”
**who marries into Israel;**
**or an Israelite daughter**
**who marries a man of impaired lineage**
**or a descendant of outcastes.**

footnotes:
³²¹ Heb: khalutzah
³²² Heb: mamzeret
³²³ Heb: netin;


###### Sifrei Devarim 196:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/196:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/196:3)


**יֵלֵךְ וְיָשֹׁב לְבֵיתוֹ** – יֵלֵךְ וְיִשְׁמַע דִּבְרֵי כֹהֵן מֵעֶרְכֵי מִלְחָמָה וְיַחֲזֹר.


**“He shall go and return to his home” (Dt. 20:7)—**
**that is, he shall go and heed**
**the instructions of the Warrior Priest to return**³²⁴

³²⁴ Cf. M. Sotah 8:3.



## Paragraph 197

###### Sifrei Devarim 197:1

(דברים כ ח) **וְיָסְפוּ הַשֹּׁטְרִים לְדַבֵּר אֶל הָעָם וְאָמְרוּ**, לָמַדְנוּ שֶׁהֵם הַדְּבָרִים.


**Pisqa’ 197**³²⁵
1. **“And the officers shall continue**
**to speak with the people, *saying*:” (Dt. 20:8)—**
**thus, we learn that**
**they should speak exactly those words.**

###### Sifrei Devarim 197:2

**מִי הָאִישׁ הַיָּרֵא וְרַךְ הַלֵּבָב** – שֶׁיֵּשׁ עֲבֵרָה בְּיָדוֹ בַּסֵּתֶר, **יֵלֵךְ וְיָשֹׁב לְבֵיתוֹ**.


**“Who is the man,**
***fearful* and *faint-hearted*” (Dt. 20:8)—**
**this is one who has committed a hidden transgression.**
**“He shall go and return to his home”(Dt. 20:8).**


###### Sifrei Devarim 197:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/197:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/197:3)

2. **R. Akiva says:**
***Fearful* and *faint-hearted***
**means just that! R. Yose the Galilean says:**
***Fearful and faint-hearted***
**implies that he suffers from an infirmity**.³²⁶

###### Sifrei Devarim 197:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/197:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/197:4)


**וְלֹא יִמַּס אֶת לְבַב אֶחָיו כִּלְבָבוֹ**, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאִם הָיָה אֶחָד מֵהֶם מִתְיָרֵא מִן הָעֲבֵרוֹת שֶׁבְּיָדוֹ – כֻּלָּם חוֹזְרִים וּבָאִים.


**“So that the hearts of his brothers not faint away like his” (Dt. 20:8)—**

## Paragraph 198

###### Sifrei Devarim 198:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/198:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/198:1)


(דברים כ ט) **וְהָיָה כְּכַלֹּת הַשֹּׁטְרִים**, בַּעֲקֵבָם שֶׁל עָם מַעֲמִידִים זַקָּפִים מִלִּפְנֵיהֶם וְאַחֲרֵיהֶם, וְכַשִּׁילִים שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל בִּידֵיהֶם, וְכָל הַמְבַקֵּשׁ לַחֲזֹר – הָרְשׁוּת בְּיָדָם לְקַפֵּחַ אֶת שׁוֹקָיו, שֶׁתְּחִלַּת נְפִילָה נִיסָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמואל א ד יז): ״נָס יִשְׂרָאֵל מִפְּנֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים וְגַם מַגֵּפָה גְדוֹלָה הָיְתָה בָעָם״. בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? בְּמִלְחֶמֶת הָרְשׁוּת, אֲבָל בְּמִלְחֶמֶת מִצְוָה הַכֹּל יוֹצְאִים, אֲפִלּוּ (יואל ב טז) חָתָן מֵחַדְרוֹ וְכַלָּה מֵחֻפָּתָהּ!


**Pisqa’ 198**³²⁸
1. **“And when the officers had finished” (Dt. 20:9)—**
**after their charge to the people,**
**they set up guards in the front**
**and rear of the troops,**
**with iron mallets in their hands.**
**And if anyone wanted to leave,**
**the guards had the right to**
**break their shins,**
**for the beginning of defeat is retreat.**
**And, furthermore, it is said:**
**“So Israel retreated from the Philistines**
**and then a great plague afflicted the people” (1Sam. 4:17).**³²⁹
2. **Under what circumstances**
**[do these exemptions from battle apply]?**
**In optional wars.**
**But if it is an obligatory war,**
**[in defense of the borders of the Land],**
**everyone must go—**
**even a bride-groom from his bedroom**
**and a bride from her wedding-canopy**³³⁰ 190.9.

## Paragraph 199

###### Sifrei Devarim 199:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/199:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/199:1)


(דברים כ י) **כִּי תִקְרַב אֶל עִיר**, בְּמִלְחֶמֶת הָרְשׁוּת הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר.


**Pisqa’ 199**³³¹
1. “When you approach a *city*” (Dt. 20:10)—
here the verse speaks of an optional war
[in which there is no mandate to destroy the population].

###### Sifrei Devarim 199:2

**אֶל עִיר** – וְלֹא לִכְרָךְ.


“A *city*” (Dt. 20:10)—but not a town.


###### Sifrei Devarim 199:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/199:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/199:3)


**אֶל עִיר** – וְלֹא לִכְפָר.


“A *city*” (Dt. 20:10)—but not a village.


###### Sifrei Devarim 199:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/199:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/199:4)


**לְהִלָּחֵם עָלֶיהָ** – וְלֹא לְהַרְעִיבָהּ וְלֹא לְהַצְמִיאָהּ, וְלֹא לַהֲמִיתָהּ מִיתַת תַּחֲלוּאִים.


“To engage it *in battle*” (Dt. 20:10)—
but not to starve it out,
or to foul its water,
or to unleash disease within it.


###### Sifrei Devarim 199:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/199:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/199:5)


**וְקָרָאתָ אֵלֶיהָ לְשָׁלוֹם**. גָּדוֹל שָׁלוֹם, שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ מֵתִים צְרִיכִים שָׁלוֹם. גָּדוֹל שָׁלוֹם, שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ בְּמִלְחַמְתָּם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל צְרִיכִים שָׁלוֹם. גָּדוֹל שָׁלוֹם, שֶׁדָּרֵי רוּם צְרִיכִים שָׁלוֹם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (איוב כה ב): ״עוֹשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם בִּמְרוֹמָיו״. גָּדוֹל שָׁלוֹם, שֶׁחוֹתְמִים בּוֹ בִּרְכַּת כֹּהֲנִים. וְאַף מֹשֶׁה הָיָה אוֹהֵב שָׁלוֹם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים ב כו): ״וָאֶשְׁלַח מַלְאָכִים מִמִּדְבַּר קְדֵמוֹת אֶל סִיחוֹן מֶלֶךְ חֶשְׁבּוֹן דִּבְרֵי שָׁלוֹם״.


2. “Then you shall sue it for peace” (Dt. 20:10).
**Great is peace,**
**for even the dead need peace,**
**Great is peace,**
**for even in Israel’s wars they needed peace.**
**Great is peace,**
**for those who dwell on high need peace,**
**as it is said:**
**“He makes peace in His lofty dwelling” (Job 25:2).**
**Great is peace,**
**for the Priestly Blessing concludes with *peace*.**
**And Moses, too, was a lover of peace,**
**as it is said:**
**“Then I sent messengers from the desert of Qadmut. to Sihon, the King of Heshbon,**
**with words of *peace*” (Dt. 2:25**).³³²

footnotes:
³³² Sifre Nu, 42, s.v., gadol hashalom



## Paragraph 200

###### Sifrei Devarim 200:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/200:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/200:1)


(דברים כ יא) **וְהָיָה אִם שָׁלוֹם תַּעַנְךָ**, יָכוֹל אַף מִקְצָתָהּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וּפָתְחָה לָךְ**, כֻּלָּהּ וְלֹא מִקְצָתָהּ.


**Pisqa’ 200**³³³
1. “Now, if *it answers you* with peace” (Dt. 20:11).
Is it possible to say that
even if only part of the populace
[desires peace, peace should be negotiated]?
The Teaching states:
“And opens *itself* to you” (Dt. 20:11)—
implying that the entire populace,
not only part of it,
[has opened the city’s gates].

footnotes:
³³³ H:217-218; JN2:91:92


###### Sifrei Devarim 200:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/200:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/200:2)


**וְהָיָה כָּל הָעָם הַנִּמְצָא בָהּ** – לְרַבּוֹת כְּנַעֲנִים שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ.


“Then *the entire populace* found there” (Dt. 20:11)—
including whatever Canaanites may be within it.


###### Sifrei Devarim 200:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/200:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/200:3)


**יִהְיוּ לְךָ לָמַס וַעֲבָדוּךָ**, אָמְרוּ: ״מְקַבְּלִים אָנוּ עָלֵינוּ מִסִּים וְלֹא שִׁעְבּוּד״, ״שִׁעְבּוּד וְלֹא מִסִּים״ – אֵין שׁוֹמְעִים לָהֶם, עַד שֶׁיְּקַבְּלוּ עֲלֵיהֶם זוֹ וָזוֹ.


“Shall be yours for tribute and servitude” (Dt. 20:11).
If they say:
We accept tribute but not servitude,
Or, we accept servitude, but not tribute,
pay no mind to them,
until they accept both conditions.


###### Sifrei Devarim 200:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/200:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/200:4)


(דברים כ יב) **וְאִם לֹא תַשְׁלִים עִמָּךְ וְעָשְׂתָה עִמְּךָ מִלְחָמָה**, הַכָּתוּב מְבַשֶּׂרְךָ שֶׁאִם אֵינָהּ מַשְׁלֶמֶת עִמְּךָ – לְסוֹף שֶׁהִיא עוֹשָׂה עִמְּךָ מִלְחָמָה.


2. “But, if the city will not make peace with you, *but wages war* against you” (Dt. 20:12)—
this verse announces to you that
if the city does not make peace with you,
it is destined to *wage war* against you.


###### Sifrei Devarim 200:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/200:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/200:5)


**וְצַרְתָּ עָלֶיהָ**, אַף לְהַרְעִיבָהּ, אַף לְהַצְמִיאָהּ, אַף לַהֲמִיתָהּ בְּמִיתַת תַּחֲלוּאִים!


“Then you shall lay siege to it” (Dt. 20:12)—
including starvation, thirst, and death by disease.³³⁴ 199.1.

footnotes:
³³⁴ Cf. Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 200:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/200:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/200:6)


(דברים כ יג) **וּנְתָנָהּ ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּיָדֶךָ**, אִם עָשִׂיתָ אֶת כָּל הָאָמוּר בָּעִנְיָן – לְסוֹף שֶׁה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ נוֹתְנָהּ בְּיָדֶךָ.


“Once HASHEM your God has given it into *your hands*” (Dt. 20:13)—
if you have performed all that is stated here,
in the end, HASHEM your God will deliver it into *your hands*.


###### Sifrei Devarim 200:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/200:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/200:7)


**וְהִכִּיתָ אֶת כָּל זְכוּרָהּ לְפִי חָרֶב**, שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי אַף הַקְּטַנִּים שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (דברים כ יד): **רַק הַנָּשִׁים וְהַטַּף וְהַבְּהֵמָה**. אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא טַף שֶׁל נְקֵבוֹת? אָמַרְתָּ: וּמָה מִדְיָן, שֶׁהֵמִית אֶת הַגְּדוֹלוֹת, הֶחֱיָה אֶת הַקְּטַנּוֹת, כָּאן שֶׁהֶחֱיָה אֶת הַגְּדוֹלוֹת, אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁיְּחַיֶּה אֶת הַקְּטַנּוֹת? הָא אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר כָּאן טַף – אֶלָּא טַף שֶׁל זְכָרִים, מִנַּיִן שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה עִמְּךָ מִלְחָמָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **רַק הַנָּשִׁים וְהַטַּף וְהַבְּהֵמָה וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בָעִיר כָּל שְׁלָלָהּ תָּבֹז לָךְ**, יָכוֹל תְּהֵא בִזָּתָם אֲסוּרָה לָךְ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **תָּבֹז לָךְ וְאָכַלְתָּ אֶת שְׁלַל אוֹיְבֶיךָ**.


“Then you shall strike all its males with the blade of the sword” (Dt. 20:13)—
shall I infer from this that
even the young boys shall be put to the sword?
The Teaching states:
“Only, the women, the babies, and the livestock . . . you may take as booty” (Dt. 20:14)—
[but do not spare even the young boys].
Perhaps, the little girls as well
[shall be put to the sword]?
Take the case of the war against Midian (Nu. 31:17-18):
There they killed the adult women
and permitted the young girls to live,
whereas here (Dt. 20:14),
where they let the adult women live—
isn’t it logical that
they should let the young girls live?
I conclude, therefore, that
here, when *babies* are mentioned,
the reference is to male babies as well!
How do I know that any male combatant
[of whatever age must be put to the sword]?
The Teaching states:
“Only the women, the babies, and the livestock, whatever is in the city, all its spoils,
you may take as booty” (Dt. 20:14)—
[but male combatants must be put to the sword].
Is it possible to say that
their booty should be forbidden to you?
The Teaching states [to the contrary]:
“You may take as booty, and consume the spoils of your enemy
that HASHEM your God has given you” (Dt. 20:14)

**Pisqa’ 201**³³⁵

## Paragraph 203

###### Sifrei Devarim 203:1

[of territorial expansion].³³⁹ 190.8

**אֶל עִיר** – וְלֹא לִכְרָךְ;


“To a *city*” (Dt. 20:19)—but not to a capitol;


###### Sifrei Devarim 203:3

###### Sifrei Devarim 203:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/203:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/203:4)


**יָמִים רַבִּים**, **יָמִים** – שְׁנַיִם, **רַבִּים** – שְׁלֹשָׁה. מִכָּן אָמְרוּ: אֵין צָרִים עַל עִיר שֶׁל גּוֹיִם פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים קֹדֶם לַשַּׁבָּת.


“For many days” (Dt. 20:19):
*Days*—this implies at least two days,
*Many*—adds a third.
On this basis they taught:
**They do not lay siege to a gentile city,**
**Fewer than three days before the Sabbath.**³⁴⁰

**לְהִלָּחֵם עָלֶיהָ לְתָפְשָׂהּ** – וְלֹא לִשְׁבּוֹתָהּ.


“To wage war against it, to seize it” (Dt. 20:19)—
but not merely to take captives.


###### Sifrei Devarim 203:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/203:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/203:6)


**לֹא תַשְׁחִית אֶת עֵצָהּ לִנְדֹּחַ עָלָיו גַּרְזֶן**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא גַּרְזֶן. מִנַּיִן אַף לִמְשֹׁךְ הֵימֶנָּה אַמַּת הַמַּיִם? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **לֹא תַשְׁחִית אֶת עֵצָהּ**, בְּכָל דָּבָר.


2. “You may not destroy a tree, wielding an ax against it” (Dt. 20:19)—

one may not wield an ax.

one may not even divert its irrigation channel?
The Teaching states:
“You may not destroy a tree” (Dt. 20:19)—
by any means.


###### Sifrei Devarim 203:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/203:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/203:7)


דָּבָר אַחֵר: **כִּי תָצוּר אֶל עִיר**, מַגִּיד שֶׁתּוֹבֵעַ שָׁלוֹם שְׁנַיִם שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים, עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִלְחָם בָּהּ. וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר (שמואל ב א א): ״וַיֵּשֶׁב דָּוִד בְּצִקְלַג יָמִים שְׁנַיִם״. וְאֵין צָרִים עַל עִיר בַּתְּחִלָּה בְּשַׁבָּת, אֶלָּא קוֹדֶם לַשַּׁבָּת שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים. וְאִם הִקִּיפוּהָ וְאֵרְעָה שַׁבָּת לִהְיוֹת – אֵין הַשַּׁבָּת מַפְסֶקֶת מִלְחַמְתָּהּ. זֶה אֶחָד מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים שֶׁדָּרַשׁ שַׁמַּי הַזָּקֵן: אֵין מַפְלִיגִים אֶת הַסְּפִינָה לַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל אֶלָּא קוֹדֶם לַשַּׁבָּת שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים. בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? בְּדֶרֶךְ רְחוֹקָה, אֲבָל בְּדֶרֶךְ קְרוֹבָה מַפְלִיגִים אוֹתָהּ.


Another word:
“*If* you lay siege to a city” (Dt. 20:19)—
this explains that you may sue for peace
two or three days before waging war against it.
And, similarly, He says:
“And David stayed at Tziqlag for two days” (2Sam. 1:1).
**They may not initiate a siege against a city on the Sabbath;**
**rather, at least three days before the Sabbath.**
**But if they surround it, and the Sabbath intervenes,**
**Sabbath-observance does not interfere with the war**³⁴¹**.**
This is one of three teachings
expounded by Shammai the Elder:
**A ship does not embark on the Great Sea**
**unless there are three days left till the Sabbath.**³⁴²
Under what circumstances?
If it’s sailing to a distant port.
But if it’s sailing a short distance,
They permit the ship to embark.³⁴³

³⁴² //T.Eruv.3:8.
³⁴³ This material is lacking in many mss copies. See F:239, n.3,

**כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ תֹאכֵל** – מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה; **וְאֹתוֹ לֹא תִכְרֹת** – מִצְוַת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.


3. “For you *must* eat from it” (Dt. 20:19)—
this is a prescription.
“But you may not chop it down” (Dt. 20:19)—

**כִּי הָאָדָם עֵץ הַשָּׂדֶה**, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁחַיָּיו שֶׁל אָדָם אֵינָם אֶלָּא מִן הָאִילָן. רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: מִכָּן חָס הַמָּקוֹם עַל פֵּרוֹת הָאִילָן קַל וָחוֹמֶר מֵאִילָן, וּמָה אִילָן שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה פֵּרוֹת – הִזְהִירְךָ הַכָּתוּב עָלָיו, פֵּרוֹת עַצְמָם – עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה!


“Now, is a tree of the field *like a man*” (Dt. 20:19)—
this teaches that
human life is sustained only by trees.
R. Ishmael says:
On this basis we reason that
since the All-Present notes
the importance of the fruit of trees,
it stands to reason that
He cares for the tree itself.
For just as the verse warns you about the tree,
which yields the fruit,
all the more so should we protect the fruit itself!

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/203:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/203:10)


**לָבוֹא מִפָּנֶיךָ בַּמָּצוֹר**, הָא אִם מְעַכֶּבְךָ לָבוֹא מִפָּנֶיךָ בַּמָּצוֹר – קָצְצֵהוּ!


“That *must be* besieged by you?” (Dt. 20:19)—
well—if the tree is hindering the siege,
you may chop it down.

**כִּי לֹא עֵץ מַאֲכָל הוּא** – זֶה אִילַן סְרָק. אִם סוֹפֵנוּ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת אִילַן מַאֲכָל, מַה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר **עֵץ מַאֲכָל**? מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאִילַן סְרָק קוֹדֵם לְאִילַן מַאֲכָל. יָכוֹל אֲפִלּוּ מְעֻלֶּה בְּדָמִים, וּכְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **אֹתוֹ תַשְׁחִית וְכָרָתָּה**,


“*Useless* for food” (Dt. 20:20)—

Is it possible to say that

“*That* one you may destroy and chop down” (Dt. 20:20)—

using the wood for storage-bins or construction.

by deploying against it various kinds of catapults,

## Paragraph 205

###### Sifrei Devarim 205:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/205:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/205:1)


(דברים כא א) **כִּי יִמָּצֵא** – וְלֹא בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁמָּצוּי. מִכָּן אָמְרוּ (סוטה ט ט): מִשֶּׁרַבּוּ הָרַצְחָנִים בָּטְלָה עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה, מִשֶּׁבָּא אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן דִּינַאי וּתְחִינָה בֶן פְּרִישָׁה. [״בֶּן פְּרִישָׁה״] הָיָה נִקְרָא – חָזְרוּ לִקְרוֹתוֹ ״בֶּן הָרַצְחָן״.


**Pisqa’ 205**³⁴⁵
1. “*Should you find* a murder-victim” (Dt. 21:1)—
but not at a time
when abandoned victims are plentiful.
On this basis they taught:
**When murderers became common,**
**they abolished the rite of the Beheaded Calf**.³⁴⁶
**This was when Elazar b. Dinai showed up,**
**followed by Tekhinah b. Perishah.**
**Known also as “the Boy Wonder,”**
**he became notorious as “the Son of the Murderer.”**³⁴⁷ XX 6.

**R. Akiva says:**
**How do I know that**
**if the court witnessed the murder,**

(דברים כא ב) **וְיָצְאוּ זְקֵנֶיךָ**, **זְקֵנֶיךָ** – שְׁנַיִם, **וְשֹׁפְטֶיךָ** – שְׁנַיִם, אֵין בֵּית דִּין שָׁקוּל – מוֹסִיפִים עֲלֵיהֶם עוֹד אֶחָד, הֲרֵי כָּאן חֲמִשָּׁה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: **זְקֵנֶיךָ וְשֹׁפְטֶיךָ** – שְׁנַיִם, אֵין בֵּית דִּין שָׁקוּל – מוֹסִיפִים עֲלֵיהֶם עוֹד אֶחָד, הֲרֵי כָּאן שְׁלֹשָׁה.


3. **“Then, your *elders* shall go out” (Dt. 21:2)—**
**the plural, *elders*, implies two.**
**“And your *justices*” (Dt. 21:2)—**
**here are two more.**
**Now, a court cannot yield a split decision,**
**so they add one more justice,**
**and now there are five:**
**words of R. Judah.**³⁵²
R. Shimon says:
“Your *elders* and your *justices*” (Dt. 21:2)—
one of each, yielding two.
**Now, a court cannot yield a split decision,**
**so they add one more justice,**
**And now there are three!**³⁵³

**וּמָדְדוּ אֶל הֶעָרִים**, מִן הֶחָלָל אֶל הֶעָרִים, וְלֹא מִן הֶעָרִים אֶל הֶחָלָל. מִכָּן אָמְרוּ: נִמְצָא רֹאשׁוֹ בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד וְגוּפוֹ בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר – מוֹלִיכִים אֶת הָרֹאשׁ אֵצֶל הַגּוּף, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָה אוֹמֵר: הַגּוּף אֵצֶל הָרֹאשׁ. נִמְצָא סָמוּךְ לַסְּפָר, אוֹ לְעִיר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ גּוֹיִם, אוֹ לְעִיר שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ בֵּית דִּין – לֹא הָיוּ מוֹדְדִים. אֵין מוֹדְדִים אֶלָּא לְעִיר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ בֵּית דִּין!


4. “And they measured to the cities” (Dt. 21:2)—
measuring from the victim to the cities,
but not from the cities to the victim.
On this basis they taught:
**If his head was found lying in one place,**
**and his body was found lying in another place,**
**they bring the head to the body:**
**words of R. Eliezer.**
**R. Akiva says:**
**They bring the body to the head!** ³⁵⁴
**If the victim is found close to**
**the border [of a gentile population],**
**or near a city where there are gentiles,**
**or near a city in which there is no [Israelite] court,**
**they would not measure to these cities.**
**They measure only to one**
**In which there is an [Israelite] court.**³⁵⁵

## Paragraph 206

###### Sifrei Devarim 206:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/206:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/206:1)


(דברים כא ג) **וְהָיָה הָעִיר הַקְּרֹבָה** – הַקְּרוֹבָה שֶׁבַּקְּרוֹבוֹת. מִכָּן אָמְרוּ (סוטה ט ב): נִמְצָא מְכֻוָּן בֵּין שְׁתֵּי עֲיָירוֹת – שְׁתֵּיהֶן מְבִיאוֹת שְׁתֵּי עֶגְלוֹת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: עִיר אַחַת מְבִיאָה, וְאֵין שְׁתֵּי עֲיָירוֹת מְבִיאוֹת שְׁתֵּי עֶגְלוֹת, וְאֵין יְרוּשָׁלִַם מְבִיאָה עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה.


**Pisqa’ 206**³⁵⁶
1. “After the city *closest* to the murder victim has been determined” (Dt. 21:3).
This refers to the nearest among the near.
On this basis they taught:
**If the murder victim is found**
**exactly between two cities,**
**each of them brings two calves**
**[one for itself and one for its neighbor].**
**But sages say:**
**One city brings one calf,**
**and two cities do not bring two calves**.³⁵⁷
**But residents of Jerusalem are**
**under no obligation to bring a Beheaded-calf for the rite**
**[because Jerusalem falls within no tribal inheritance].**³⁵⁸

³⁵⁶ H:221; JN2:101-102.
³⁵⁷ =T, Neg.1:13
³⁵⁸ =M. Sotah 9:2.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/206:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/206:2)


**וְלָקְחוּ זִקְנֵי הָעִיר הַהִיא** – וְלֹא זִקְנֵי יְרוּשָׁלִַם.


2. “Then, the elders *of that city* shall purchase” (Dt. 21:3)—
but *not* the elders of Jerusalem.
“A calf of the herd” (Dt. 21:3).
**R. Eliezer says:**


###### Sifrei Devarim 206:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/206:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/206:3)


**עֶגְלַת בָּקָר**, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: עֶגְלָה בַּת שְׁנָתָהּ, וּפָרָה בַּת שְׁתַּיִם. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: עֶגְלָה בַּת שְׁתַּיִם, וּפָרָה בַּת שָׁלֹשׁ וּבַת אַרְבַּע. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **עֶגְלַת בָּקָר** – שֶׁיְּהֵא בָּהּ שְׁנֵי דְרָכִים. הָא כֵּיצַד? בַּת שְׁתַּיִם **עֶגְלַת בָּקָר**.


**A calf qualifies [for the rite] in its *first* year,**
**While a heifer qualifies [for the rite of the Red Heifer**³⁵⁹**] in its *second*.**
**But sages say:**
**A calf qualifies in its second year,**
**While a heifer qualifies in its third or fourth**.³⁶⁰.
Another word:
“A calf of the herd” (Dt. 21:3)—
one that has two distinguishing traits.
And what might these be?
It must be two years old,
And it must be a calf³⁶¹ “heifer.” of the herd.

³⁶¹ So F:242. Pardo emends to parah,


###### Sifrei Devarim 206:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/206:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/206:4)


דָּבָר אַחֵר: רְחִיצָה בַּזְּקֵנִים וְכַפָּרָה בַּכֹּהֲנִים.


Another word:
**Rinsing the hands is the task of elders (Dt. 21:6),**
**while the absolution is the task of Priests (Dt. 21:5-7)**³⁶²

###### Sifrei Devarim 206:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/206:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/206:5)


**אֲשֶׁר לֹא עֻבַּד בָּהּ** – כָּל עֲבוֹדָה. מִנַּיִן בְּעוֹל? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **אֲשֶׁר לֹא מָשְׁכָה בְּעֹל**.


**“Which had never been *worked*” (Dt. 21:3)—**
**Can this mean *any* work at all?**
**How do I know that**
**this refers to bearing a yoke?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“Which has *never* carried a yoke”**³⁶³ (Dt. 21:3)

## Paragraph 207

###### Sifrei Devarim 207:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/207:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/207:1)


(דברים כא ד) **וְהוֹרִידוּ זִקְנֵי הָעִיר הַהִיא** – מִצְוָה בְּזִקְנֵי הָעִיר הַהִיא.


**Pisqa’ 207**³⁶⁴
1. **“Now, *the elders of that city* shall bring the calf down” (Dt. 21:4)—**
**this is the obligation of the *elders of that city*.**

footnotes:
³⁶⁴ H:221-222; JN2:101-102.


###### Sifrei Devarim 207:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/207:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/207:2)


**אֶת הָעֶגְלָה אֶל נַחַל אֵיתָן** – כְּמַשְׁמָעוֹ, קָשֶׁה; וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֵיתָן – כָּשֵׁר.


**“To a river-bed of *rapids*” (Dt. 21:4)—**
**in the sense that it is *difficult* [to navigate].**
**But even if it is not a rapids,**
**the rite is fit.**


###### Sifrei Devarim 207:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/207:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/207:3)


עוֹרְפִים אוֹתָהּ בְּקוֹפִיץ מֵאֲחוֹרֶיהָ, וּמְקוֹמָהּ אָסוּר מִלִּזְרוֹעַ וּמִלַּעֲבוֹד. יָכוֹל יְהֵא אָסוּר לִסְרוֹק שָׁם פִּשְׁתָּן וּלְנַקֵּר שָׁם אֶת הָאֲבָנִים? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **אֲשֶׁר לֹא יֵעָבֵד בּוֹ וְלֹא יִזָּרֵעַ**, זְרִיעָה בִּכְלָל הָיְתָה, וְלָמָּה יָצָאת? לְהַקִּישׁ אֵלֶיהָ – מָה זְרִיעָה מְיֻחֶדֶת שֶׁהִיא עֲבוֹדַת קַרְקַע; יָצְאוּ אֵלּוּ, שֶׁאֵין עֲבוֹדַת קַרְקַע.


**They behead the calf**
**from the back of its neck**
**with a cleaver.**
**And the spot [at which it is killed]**
**is forbidden from being sown or**
**from being worked in any way.** ³⁶⁵
Is it possible to say that
it is forbidden as well to comb flax there
or to chisel stones there?
The Teaching states:
“Which had *never* been worked and had *never* been sown” (Dt. 21:4)—
*sowing* [should be conceived] as an aspect of *working.*
Why, then, is it singled out for special mention?
To facilitate comparative inquiry:
Just as *sowing* is distinctive,
as work connected to the soil,
this excludes from the rule these,
which are not connected to the soil.

footnotes:
³⁶⁵ =M. Sotah9:5.


###### Sifrei Devarim 207:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/207:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/207:4)


**וְעָרְפוּ שָׁם**, נֶאֱמַר כָּאן עֲרִיפָה וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן (שמות יג יג) עֲרִיפָה, מָה עֲרִיפָה הָאֲמוּרָה כָּאן – עוֹרְפָהּ בְּקוֹפִיץ מֵאַחֲרֶיהָ, וְקוֹבְרָהּ, וַאֲסוּרָה בַּהֲנָיָה, אַף עֲרִיפָה הָאֲמוּרָה לְהַלָּן – עוֹרְפָהּ בְּקוֹפִיץ מֵאֲחוֹרֶיהָ, וְקוֹבְרָהּ, וַאֲסוּרָה בַּהֲנָיָה.


2. “And they shall *behead* it there” (Dt. 21:4)—
Here, *beheading* is mentioned, and
elsewhere [in connection with the Firstling of an ass] (Ex 13:13) *beheading* is mentioned. Just as the *beheading* mentioned here (Dt. 21:4)
requires beheading at the neck,
and requires beheading with a cleaver,
and requires beheading from behind,
and requires burial of the carcass,
and is forbidden for any benefit—
So, too, the *beheading* mentioned elsewhere,
requires beheading at the neck,
and requires beheading with a cleaver,
and requires beheading from behind,
and requires burial of the carcass,
and is forbidden for any benefit.


###### Sifrei Devarim 207:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/207:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/207:5)


**בַּנָּחַל** – אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֵיתָן.


“In the river-bed” (Dt. 21:4)—
even if it is not *a rapids*.



## Paragraph 208

###### Sifrei Devarim 208:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/208:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/208:1)


(דברים כא ה) **וְנִגְּשׁוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים בְּנֵי לֵוִי**, מִכְּלָל שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים יח ז) ״וְשֵׁרֵת בְּשֵׁם ה׳ אֱלֹהָיו״, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא תְמִימִים, בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִים מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר **בְּנֵי לֵוִי**. **כִּי בָם בָּחַר ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ [לְשָׁרְתוֹ וּלְבָרֵךְ בִּשְׁמוֹ]**, מַגִּיד שֶׁאֵין בִּרְכַּת כֹּהֲנִים כְּשֵׁרָה בְּבַעֲלֵי מוּמִים.


**Pisqa’ 208**³⁶⁶
1. “Then the Priests, the sons of Levi, shall approach” (Dt. 21:5).
inferring from what is stated—
“And he shall serve in the name of HASHEM his God” (Dt. 18:7)—
I only know that
unblemished [Priests] may conduct the rite.
How do I know that
*disfigured* Priests are qualified as well?³⁶⁷ 208, n.2).
The Teaching states:
“The sons of *Levi*” (Dt. 21:5)—
[whether unblemished or disfigured].

footnotes:
³⁶⁶ H:222-223; JN2:103-104.
³⁶⁷ See M. Meg.4: 7, which excludes priests with disfigured hands.from lifting them in blessing. Cf. H:464 (pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 208:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/208:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/208:2)


**לְשָׁרְתוֹ וּלְבָרֵךְ בְּשֵׁם ה׳**, מַקִּישׁ בְּרָכָה לְשֵׁרוּת: מַה שֵּׁרוּת בַּעֲמִידָה – אַף בְּרָכָה בַּעֲמִידָה.


2. “For HASHEM your God has chosen from among them to serve Him
and to *give blessing* in His Name” (Dt. 21:5)—
the conjoining of *to serve* and *to bless* implies that
the *blessing* of the *Priest* is invalid if he is disfigured.
“To *serve* Him and to *give blessing* in His Name” (Dt. 21:5)—
Let us draw out the comparative implications:
Just as *serving* requires *standing*,
*blessing* also requires *standing*.


###### Sifrei Devarim 208:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/208:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/208:3)


**וְעַל פִּיהֶם יִהְיֶה כָּל רִיב וְכָל נָגַע**, מַקִּישׁ רִיבִים לִנְגָעִים: מַה נְּגָעִים בַּיּוֹם – אַף רִיבִים בַּיּוֹם, מַה רִיבִים שֶׁלֹּא בִּקְרוֹבִים – אַף נְגָעִים שֶׁלֹּא בִּקְרוֹבִים.


3. “And their instructions (*`al pihem*) shall resolve every *dispute* and the status of every *plague-sign* (Dt. 21:5)—
the verse suggests a comparison
between civil *disputes* and *plague-signs*:
Just as plague-signs are examined during the day,
so, too, civil disputes are judged during the day;
just as civil disputes are not
judged by relatives,
so, too, plague-signs are not
examined by relatives.


###### Sifrei Devarim 208:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/208:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/208:4)


אוֹ, מָה רִיבִים בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה אַף נְגָעִים בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה? וְדִין הוּא, אִם מָמוֹנוֹ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה גּוּפוֹ לֹא יְהֵא בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (ויקרא יג ב): ״אוֹ אֶל אַחַד מִבָּנָיו הַכֹּהֲנִים״, לְלַמֶּדְךָ שֶׁכֹּהֵן אֶחָד רוֹאֶה אֶת הַנְּגָעִים!


Or [may we argue that]:
Just as civil disputes are
judged by courts of three,
so, too, the status of plague-signs is
examined by three Priests?
Now, this is only reasonable!
If a matter affecting one’s wealth
is judged by three [judges],
shouldn’t a matter affecting one’s body
be judged by three [Priests]?
[Nevertheless,] the Teaching states:
“Now, when there appears, on the skin of his flesh. . . something akin to an unclean eruption, then he should be brought before Aaron the Priest,
or *one* of his priestly sons” (Lv. 13:2)—
This teaches you that only one Priest need examine plague-signs.



## Paragraph 209

###### Sifrei Devarim 209:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/209:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/209:1)


(דברים כא ו) **וְכֹל זִקְנֵי הָעִיר הַהִיא**, וַאֲפִלּוּ הֵם מֵאָה. לְפִי שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ לְהַלָּן שְׁלֹשָׁה וַחֲמִשָּׁה, יָכוֹל אַף כָּאן כֵּן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר **וְכֹל זִקְנֵי הָעִיר הַהִיא**, וַאֲפִלּוּ הֵם מֵאָה.


**Pisqa’ 209**³⁶⁸
1. “Then, all the elders of that city” (Dt. 21:6)—
even if there are a hundred!
Since we have taught elsewhere:³⁶⁹):
**Three elders or five elders—**
Is it possible to say that
The same applies here?
The Teaching states:
“All the elders of that city” (Dt .21:6)—
Even if there are a hundred!

footnotes:
³⁶⁸ H:223; JN2:195-106.
³⁶⁹ M.Sot.9:5 cited at Pisqa’ 205.3


###### Sifrei Devarim 209:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/209:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/209:2)


**יִרְחֲצוּ אֶת יְדֵיהֶם עַל הָעֶגְלָה הָעֲרוּפָה בַּנָּחַל**, עַל מְקוֹם עֲרִיפָתָהּ שֶׁל עֶגְלָה. יָכוֹל יַעֲלוּ מִן הַנַּחַל וְיֹאמְרוּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **בַּנָּחַל**, שֶׁתְּהֵא עֲנִיָּתָם וַאֲמִירָתָם בַּנַּחַל.


2. “They shall wash their hands over the beheaded calf, in the river-bed” (Dt. 21:6)—
over the place of the calf’s beheading.
Is it possible to say that
they should ascend from the river-bed
before reciting [the formula of denial]?
The Teaching states:
“In the river-bed” (Dt. 21:6)—
let all their recitals and responses come from the river-bed.



## Paragraph 210

###### Sifrei Devarim 210:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/210:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/210:1)


(דברים כא ז) **וְעָנוּ וְאָמְרוּ**, בִּלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ.


**Pisqa’ 210**³⁷⁰
1. **“And they shall respond, *saying*:” (Dt. 21:7)—**
**in the Holy Tongue.**³⁷¹ Mech.ISH, *bakhodesh*, par.2, s.v.*, koh bileshon haqodesh..*

footnotes:
³⁷⁰ H:223;JN2:108.
³⁷¹ //Sifre Nu, 39, s.v., bileshon haqodesh;


###### Sifrei Devarim 210:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/210:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/210:2)


**יָדֵינוּ לֹא שָׁפְכָה**, וְכִי עָלָת עַל לִבֵּנוּ שֶׁזִּקְנֵי בֵּית דִּין שׁוֹפְכֵי דָמִים הֵם? אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא בָא לְיָדֵינוּ וּפְטַרְנוּהוּ בְּלֹא מְזוֹנוֹת, וְלֹא רְאִינוּהוּ וְהִנַּחְנוּהוּ בְּלֹא לְוָיָה.


**“Our hands have not spilled this blood” (Dt. 21:7)—**
**now, who could imagine that**
**elders of the court might be murderers?**
**Rather, their point is:**
**Never did he approach us,**
**that we sent him off [without provisions],**³⁷²
**And never did we see him,**
**That we left him [to travel unaccompanied]!**

footnotes:
³⁷² The clauses. “without provisions” and ‘to travel unaccompanied” appear to be scribal interpolations based upon the text of M. Sot.9:6.


###### Sifrei Devarim 210:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/210:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/210:3)


(דברים כא ח) הַכֹּהֲנִים אוֹמְרִים: **כַּפֵּר לְעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל**.


**The Priests then say:**
**“Grant absolution to Your people, Israel!” (Dt. 21:8).**³⁷³

footnotes:
³⁷³ //M. Sotah 9:6.


###### Sifrei Devarim 210:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/210:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/210:4)


כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר **אֲשֶׁר פָּדִיתָ ה׳**, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכַּפָּרָה זוֹ מְכַפֶּרֶת עַל יוֹצְאֵי מִצְרַיִם.


**When He continues:**
**“Whom You have redeemed, HASHEM” (Dt. 21:8)—**
**this teaches that the formula of absolution**
**even absolves the blood-guilt of those [unwitting killers]**
**who left Egypt [but died before the rite was**
**taught to Moses].**³⁷⁴

footnotes:
³⁷⁴ Cf. T. Sotah 9:2.


###### Sifrei Devarim 210:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/210:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/210:5)


**כַּפֵּר לְעַמְּךָ** – אֵלּוּ הַחַיִּים;


2. “Grant absolution to Your people” (Dt. 21:8)—
this refers to the living.


###### Sifrei Devarim 210:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/210:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/210:6)


**אֲשֶׁר פָּדִיתָ** – אֵלּוּ הַמֵּתִים, מַגִּיד שֶׁהַמֵּתִים צְרִיכִים כַּפָּרָה. נִמְצִינוּ לְמֵדִים שֶׁשּׁוֹפֵךְ דָּמִים חוֹטֵא עַד יוֹצְאֵי מִצְרַיִם.


“Whom You have redeemed” (Dt. 21:8)—
referring to the dead.
This explains that
even the dead need absolution.
We turn out to learn that
The blood-spiller’s sin even
affects those who left Egypt!


###### Sifrei Devarim 210:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/210:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/210:7)


**אֲשֶׁר פָּדִיתָ** – עַל מְנָת כֵּן פְּדִיתָנוּ, שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ בֵּינֵינוּ שׁוֹפְכֵי דָמִים. דָּבָר אַחֵר: עַל מְנָת כֵּן פְּדִיתָנוּ, שֶׁאִם נֶחֱטָא – אַתָּה מְכַפֵּר עָלֵינוּ.


“Whom you have redeemed” (Dt. 21:8)—
for this reason did You redeem us,
so that there not be among us anyone
guilty of spilling innocent blood!
Another word:
**For this reason did You redeem us,**
**so that when we sin, You can absolve us!**


###### Sifrei Devarim 210:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/210:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/210:8)


וְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ אוֹמֶרֶת: כָּל זְמַן שֶׁתַּעֲשׂוּ כָּכָה – הַדָּם מִתְכַּפֵּר לָכֶם.


**And the Holy Spirit says:**
**Whenever you perform this rite,**
**the blood of the calf will grant you absolution!** ³⁷⁵

³⁷⁵ //M. Sotah 9:6. See F:244, n.4.


###### Sifrei Devarim 210:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/210:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/210:9)


(דברים כא ט) **וְאַתָּה תְּבַעֵר** – בַּעֵר עוֹשֵׂי הָרָעוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל!


“And may you expunge the innocent blood
From your midst” (Dt. 21:9)—
**that is, expunge the evil-doers from Israel**!³⁷⁶ (“expunge”) appears widely scattered throughout Sifre. See *Pisqa’ot* 151.1, 155.1, 187.3, 220, 240, 241

## Paragraph 211

###### Sifrei Devarim 211:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/211:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/211:1)


(דברים כא י) **כִּי תֵצֵא לַמִּלְחָמָה** – בְּמִלְחֶמֶת הָרְשׁוּת הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר.


**Pisqa’ 211**¹
1. “When you go out to battle” (Dt. 21:10)—
the verse speaks of an optional war.² 190.4, 198.2

footnotes:
¹ H:224; JN2:111-112.
² For the various terms for divinely sanctioned war, see Pisqa’ot


###### Sifrei Devarim 211:2
