**עַל אֹיְבֶיךָ** – כְּנֶגֶד אוֹיְבֶיךָ.


“*Upon* your enemies” (Dt. 21:10)—
that is, *against* your enemies,
[but *not* in an alliance *with* them].


###### Sifrei Devarim 211:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/211:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/211:3)


**וּנְתָנוֹ ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּיָדֶךָ**, אִם עָשִׂיתָ כָּל הָאָמוּר בָּעִנְיָן – סוֹף שֶׁה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ נוֹתְנוֹ בְּיָדֶךָ.


“And HASHEM your God *has delivered* him into your hands” (Dt. 21:10)—
if you have performed all that is stated here,
in the end, HASHEM your God *will deliver* him
into your hands!


###### Sifrei Devarim 211:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/211:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/211:4)


**וְשָׁבִיתָ שִׁבְיוֹ** – לְרַבּוֹת כְּנַעֲנִים שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ.


2. “And you take *him* captive” (Dt. 21:10)—
including any Canaanites that might be within.


###### Sifrei Devarim 211:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/211:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/211:5)


(דברים כא יא) **וְרָאִיתָ בַּשִּׁבְיָה** – בִּשְׁעַת שִׁבְיָה.


“And you see *among* the captured” (Dt. 21:11)—
that is, *during* her captivity.


###### Sifrei Devarim 211:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/211:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/211:6)


**אֵשֶׁת** – וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִיא אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ.


“A woman” (Dt. 21:11)—
even though she is a married woman.


###### Sifrei Devarim 211:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/211:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/211:7)


**יְפַת תֹּאַר**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִיא נָאָה, מִנַּיִן אֲפִילּוּ הִיא כְּעוּרָה? – תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וְחָשַׁקְתָּ בָהּ**, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָהּ יְפַת תֹּאַר.


“In fine shape” (Dt. 21:11)—
I infer from this only that
she may be taken [as a war-bride]
only as long as she is a beauty.
How do I know that
she may be taken even if she is ugly?
The Teaching states:
“And you *desire* her” (Dt. 21:11)—
even though she’s not in fine shape.


###### Sifrei Devarim 211:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/211:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/211:8)


**וְלָקַחְתָּ לְךָ לְאִשָּׁה**, שֶׁלֹּא תֹּאמַר ׳הֲרֵי זוֹ לְאַבָּה׳, ׳הֲרֵי זוֹ לְאָחִי׳.


“Then you may take her as *your wife*” (Dt. 21:11)—
lest you say:
this one’s for my father, and that one’s for my brother!



## Paragraph 212

###### Sifrei Devarim 212:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/212:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/212:1)


(דברים כא יב) **וַהֲבֵאתָהּ אֶל תּוֹךְ בֵּיתֶךָ** – וְלֹא לְבַיִת אַחֵר.


**Pisqa’ 212**³
1. “And you may bring her into the inner-most chamber of *your* house” (Dt. 21:12)
but not *anyone else’s* house.

footnotes:
³ H:224; JN2:113.


###### Sifrei Devarim 212:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/212:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/212:2)


**וְגִלְּחָה אֶת רֹאשָׁהּ וְעָשְׂתָה אֶת צִפָּרְנֶיהָ**, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: תָּקוֹץ. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָה אוֹמֵר: תְּגַדֵּל.


2. “Where she shall *shave* her head and *do* her nails” (Dt. 21:12)—
R. Eliezer says:
She *trims* her nails.
R. Akiva says:
She *grows* them long.


###### Sifrei Devarim 212:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/212:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/212:3)


אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: נֶאֶמְרָה עֲשִׂיָּה בָּרֹאשׁ וְנֶאֶמְרָה עֲשִׂיָּה בַּצִּפָּרְנַיִם, מָה עֲשִׂיָּה הָאֲמוּרָה בָּרֹאשׁ – הַעֲבָרָה, אַף עֲשִׂיָּה הָאֲמוּרָה בַּצִּפָּרְנַיִם – הַעֲבָרָה!


Said R. Eliezer:
*Doing* applies to what she does to her head,
and *doing* applies to what she does to her nails—
just as the term applied to her head implies *trimming*,
so, too, the term applied to her nails implies *trimming*.


###### Sifrei Devarim 212:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/212:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/212:4)


רַבִּי עֲקִיבָה אוֹמֵר: נֶאֶמְרָה עֲשִׂיָּה בָּרֹאשׁ וְנֶאֶמְרָה עֲשִׂיָּה בַּצִּפָּרְנַיִם, מָה עֲשִׂיָּה הָאֲמוּרָה בָּרֹאשׁ – נִוּוּל, אַף עֲשִׂיָּה הָאֲמוּרָה בַּצִּפָּרְנַיִם – נִוּוּל. וּרְאָיָה לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר (שמואל ב יט כה): ״וּמְפִיבֹשֶׁת בֶּן שָׁאוּל יָרַד לִקְרַאת הַמֶּלֶךְ לֹא עָשָׂה רַגְלָיו וְלֹא עָשָׂה שְׂפָמוֹ״.


R. Akiva says:
*Doing*, applied to her head, indicates she has been disgraced;
*doing*, applied to her nails, indicates that she has been disgraced.
And there is proof for R. Eliezer’s view:
“And Mefiboshet, the son of Saul, went down to the king,
without having *done* his feet or his moustache” (2Sam. 19:28)—
[Thus, *doing*, implies an act
of trimming that marks one as being in disgrace.]



## Paragraph 213

###### Sifrei Devarim 213:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/213:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/213:1)


(דברים כא יג) **וְהֵסִירָה אֶת שִׂמְלַת שִׁבְיָהּ מֵעָלֶיהָ**, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁמַּעֲבִיר מִמֶּנָּה בְּגָדִים נָאִים וּמַלְבִּישָׁהּ בִּגְדֵי אַלְמְנוּת, שֶׁהַגּוֹיִם, אֲרוּרִים הֵם, בְּנוֹתֵיהֶם מִתְקַשְּׁטוֹת בַּמִּלְחָמָה בִּשְׁבִיל לְהַזְנוֹת אֲחֵרִים אַחֲרֵיהֶן.


**Pisqa’ 213**⁴
1. “And she shall remove from herself the *garment* of her captivity” (Dt. 21:13).
This teaches that
they remove from her any fine clothing,
and dress her in widow’s garb.
For the gentiles
—curse them!—
prettify their daughters during battles
so that others will whore after them.

footnotes:
⁴ H:224-225; JN2:114.


###### Sifrei Devarim 213:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/213:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/213:2)


**וְיָשְׁבָה בְּבֵיתֶךָ** – בְּבַיִת שֶׁמִּשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בּוֹ; נִתְקָל בָּהּ וְנִכְנָס, נִתְקָל בָּהּ וְיוֹצֵא; דּוֹמָה לְקֵרוּיָה וְרוֹאֶה בְּנִוּוּלָהּ.


“And she will stay in *your* house” (Dt. 21:13)—
in the house he *normally uses,*
so that he will trip over her upon entering,
and he will trip over her upon leaving,
like an old piece of pumpkin.
And he will notice her disgrace.


###### Sifrei Devarim 213:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/213:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/213:3)


**וּבָכְתָה אֶת אָבִיהָ וְאֶת אִמָּהּ יֶרַח יָמִים** – אָבִיהָ וְאִמָּהּ מַמָּשׁ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין אָבִיהָ וְאִמָּהּ אֶלָּא עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ירמיהו ב כז): ״אוֹמְרִים לָעֵץ אָבִי אַתָּה״.


2. “Then she shall weep for her *father* and *mother* for a month of days” (Dt. 21:13)—
this refers to her actual father and mother:
words of R. Eliezer.
R. Akiva says:
Actually, her father and mother [represent]
images in a foreign cult,
As it is said:
“They say to a piece of wood: You are my father!” (Jer. 2:27)
**“For a month of days” (Dt. 21:13)—**
**for thirty days.**⁵

footnotes:
⁵ Cf. T. Yev. 6:7 regarding the proper time delay between the death of a childless husband and his widow’s marriage to the levir. For textual discussion, see F:246, n.


###### Sifrei Devarim 213:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/213:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/213:4)


**יֶרַח יָמִים** – שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **יֶרַח** – אֶחָד, **יָמִים** – שְׁנַיִם, הֲרֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים כְּדֵי בִּגְדֵי נוֹיָהּ שֶׁהָיוּ עָלֶיהָ וַחֲמָדָהּ, וְתִקּוּן הַוָּלָד, כְּדִבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָה, בֵּין זֶרַע רִאשׁוֹן לְזֶרַע שֵׁנִי.


3. Another word:
“A month”—that’s one;
“Of days”—the plural indicates two more months,
Yielding a total of three months.
This is enough time for
lavish clothing to wear out,
and to establish the paternity of
any fetus she may be already carrying.
[Three months is sufficient time]
to determine if the fetus [is the offspring]
of the first husband or of the second:
in accord with the words of R. Akiva.


###### Sifrei Devarim 213:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/213:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/213:5)


רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: **יֶרַח יָמִים** כְּמַשְׁמָעוֹ, וְכָל כָּךְ לָמָּה? שֶׁתְּהֵא בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל שְׂמֵחָה וְזוֹ בּוֹכָה, בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִתְקַשֶּׁטֶת וְזוֹ מִתְנַוֶּלֶת.


R. Eliezer says:
“A month of days” (Dt. 21:13)—
It means just that!
Now, why [do we put her through] all this?
So that Israelite daughters may rejoice
[in anticipation of marriage],
while *this* one weeps;
so that Israelite daughters
may luxuriate [in preparation for marriage],
while *this* one is degraded.


###### Sifrei Devarim 213:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/213:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/213:6)


**וְאַחַר כֵּן תָּבוֹא אֵלֶיהָ וּבְעַלְתָּהּ**, הָא אִם לֹא עָשָׂה בָּהּ אֶת כָּל הַמַּעֲשִׂים הָאֵלּוּ, וּבָא עָלֶיהָ – הֲרֵי זוֹ בְּעִילַת זְנוּת.


4. “And afterwards you may consort with her and mount her” (Dt. 21:13)—
indeed, if he doesn’t impose these procedures upon her
and nevertheless mounts her,
this is considered a lustful mounting!⁶

footnotes:
⁶ These paragraphs are unevenly attested in mss. and editions. See F:246, n.10.


###### Sifrei Devarim 213:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/213:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/213:7)


**וְאַחַר כֵּן תָּבוֹא אֵלֶיהָ וּבְעַלְתָּהּ**, אֵין לְךָ בָּהּ אֶלָּא מִצְוַת בְּעִילָה.


“And afterwards you may consort with her and mount her” (Dt. 21:13)—
there’s nothing left to do
but [to fulfill] the commandment to mount her!


###### Sifrei Devarim 213:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/213:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/213:8)


**וְהָיְתָה לְךָ לְאִשָּׁה**, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמות כא י): ״שְׁאֵרָהּ כְּסוּתָהּ וְעוֹנָתָהּ לֹא יִגְרָע״.


“And she shall be your wife” (Dt. 21:13)—
as it is said on this theme:
“He may not limit her meat, her wardrobe, or her pleasure” (Ex. 21:10).



## Paragraph 214

###### Sifrei Devarim 214:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/214:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/214:1)


(דברים כא יד) **וְהָיָה אִם לֹא חָפַצְתָּ בָּהּ**, הַכָּתוּב מְבַשֶּׂרְךָ שֶׁאַתָּה עָתִיד לִשְׂנאוֹתָהּ.


**Pisqa’ 214**⁷
1. “Should you no longer *desire* her” (Dt. 21:14).
The verse announces to you that
you will eventually come to *reject* her.

footnotes:
⁷ H:225-226; JN2:115.


###### Sifrei Devarim 214:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/214:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/214:2)


**וְשִׁלַּחְתָּהּ לְנַפְשָׁהּ** – וְלֹא לְבֵית אֱלֹהֶיהָ.


“And you shall send her off *on her own*” (Dt. 21:14)—
But not back to her god’s house.⁸ Other versions read: *liveit ‘aviha* (“to her father’s house).

footnotes:
⁸ Heb: liveit ‘eloheiha.


###### Sifrei Devarim 214:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/214:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/214:3)


**וְשִׁלַּחְתָּהּ** – בְּגֵט, כְּדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן; וְאִם הָיְתָה חוֹלָה – יַמְתִּין לָהּ עַד שֶׁתַּבְרִיא, קַל וָחוֹמֶר לִבְנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהֵן קְדוֹשׁוֹת וּטְהוֹרוֹת.


“And you shall *send her* off” (Dt. 21:14)—
with a document of divorce,
as in the opinion of R. Jonathan.
And if she were ill,
he should give her time to recover.
[If such consideration is extended
to a gentile war-bride,]
it is simply logical that it applies to
Israelite daughters, who are holy and pure.⁹

footnotes:
⁹ This material is considered spurious, due to spotty mss evidence. See F:247. n. 6.


###### Sifrei Devarim 214:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/214:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/214:4)


וּמָכוֹר לֹא תִמְכְּרֶנָּה בַּכָּסֶף, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא יִמְכְּרֶנָּה בְּכֶסֶף, מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא יִתְּנֶנָּה בְּמַתָּנָה, וְלֹא יַעֲשֶׂה בָּהּ טוֹבָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר **וּמָכֹר לֹא תִמְכְּרֶנָּה בַּכָּסֶף**.


2. “And you shall surely not sell her for *money*” (Dt. 21:14).
I might infer only that
one may not sell her for money.
On what basis do I know that
he may not offer her either as a gift,
or [even temporarily,] as a favor?
The Teaching states:
“And you shall surely not sell her *for money*” (Dt. 21:14)—
[or in any way treat her like a commodity].


###### Sifrei Devarim 214:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/214:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/214:5)


**לֹא תִתְעַמֵּר בָּהּ** – שֶׁלֹּא תִּשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהּ. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **לֹא תִתְעַמֵּר בָּהּ** – כְּדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן. דָּבָר אַחֵר: הֲרֵי זוֹ אַזְהָרָה לְבֵית דִּין.


3. “You shall not enslave her” (Dt. 21:14)—
that is, you may not abuse her.
Another word:
“You shall not enslave her” (Dt. 21:14)—
as in the opinion of R. Jonathan.
Another word:
Indeed, this is a warning to the court.¹⁰

footnotes:
¹⁰ See F:247, n.10.


###### Sifrei Devarim 214:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/214:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/214:6)


**תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר עִנִּיתָהּ**, אֲפִלּוּ לְאַחַר מַעֲשֶׂה יְחִידִי.


“In light of the way you’ve *demeaned* her” (Dt. 21:14)—
even after *a single* sexual encounter.



## Paragraph 215

###### Sifrei Devarim 215:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:1)


(דברים כא טו) **כִּי תִהְיֶיןָ לְאִישׁ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים** – שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם הֲוָיָה. יָצְאוּ שִׁפְחָה וְנָכְרִית שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם הֲוָיָה. מַשְׁמָע מוֹצִיא אֶת אֵלּוּ וּמוֹצִיא אֶת הַיְבָמָה וּמוֹצִיא אֶת הָאֲרוּסָה, שֶׁאֵין לָהֶן הֲוָיָה, [תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים**].


**Pisqa’ 215**¹¹
1. “Should a man have two *wives*” (Dt. 21:15)—
*wives* implies that
the marriages are legitimate.
Excluded are marriages to
a slave-girl or a gentile,
for such marriages are not legitimate.
Does this mean that
we exclude [the marriages of] these two?
Then let us also exclude
—from the category of *wife*—
the childless widow of a deceased brother,¹². She must marry her brother-in-law unless he releases her to marry another man. See Dt. 25:5-11, *Pisqa’* 291.
and a betrothed woman
[as yet unmarried, but who requires a document of divorce]?
The Teaching states:
“*Two* wives” (Dt. 21:15)—
[both marriages must be in good standing
in order to fall under the present rule of inheritance].

footnotes:
¹¹ H:225-226;JN2:116-118.
¹² Heb; yevamah


###### Sifrei Devarim 215:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:2)


רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר, מַגִּיד שֶׁסּוֹפוֹ לִהְיוֹת שׂוֹנֵא אוֹתָהּ וְאוֹהֵב אַחֶרֶת.


R. Ishmael says:
The verse describes the way things are.
It explains that, in the end,
[the man taking a second wife]
will hate her and love another!


###### Sifrei Devarim 215:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:3)


**וְיָלְדוּ לוֹ בָנִים**, לְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַסָּפֵק בֶּן תִּשְׁעָה לָרִאשׁוֹן בֶּן שִׁבְעָה לָאַחֲרוֹן.


2. “And they bear him *children*” (Dt. 21:15)—
The [birth-dates] will resolve any doubts about
a nine-month child of the first marriage
or a seven-month child of the second marriage.


###### Sifrei Devarim 215:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:4)


אֵין לִי אֶלָּא הַיּוֹצֵא מִמְּקוֹם הַלֵּידָה. יוֹצֵא דֹפֶן מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וְיָלְדוּ לוֹ**, מִכָּל מָקוֹם.


I might infer only that
the verse speaks of a child born from the birth canal.
On what basis do I know about
a child born from its mother’s side?
The Teaching states:
“And they *bear* him children” (Dt. 21:15)—
by *any* kind of birth.


###### Sifrei Devarim 215:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:5)


דָּבָר אַחֵר: **כִּי תִהְיֶיןָ לְאִישׁ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵן שְׁתַּיִם. מִנַּיִן אֲפִלּוּ הֵן מְרֻבּוֹת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **נָשִׁים**.


Another word:¹³ 215.1-2 is unevenly represented in textual witnesses. See F:247, n.12.
“Should a man have two wives” (Dt. 21:15).
I might infer only that
this rule applies when there are only two wives.
How do I know that it applies as well to more?
The Teaching states:
“*Wives*” (Dt. 21:15)—
[*at least* two].

footnotes:
¹³ The material from Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 215:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:6)


אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן מְרֻבּוֹת, וּמִקְצָתָן אֲהוּבוֹת וּמִקְצָתָן שְׂנוּאוֹת, מִנַּיִן אֲפִלּוּ כֻּלָּן אֲהוּבוֹת, כֻּלָּן שְׂנוּאוֹת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **אֲהוּבָה – הָאֲהוּבָה**, **שְׂנוּאָה – הַשְּׂנוּאָה**, רִבָּה הַכָּתוּב.


I might infer only that
this rule applies when there are many wives,
but *some* of them are favored,
and *some* of them are rejected.
How do I know that it applies as well
when *all* of them are favored
or when *all* of them are rejected?
The Teaching states:
“*One* is favored” and “The *favored* one” (Dt. 21:15);
“*One* is rejected” and “The *rejected* one” (Dt. 21:15)—
this redundancy permits expansion of the rule
[to include many wives in varying degrees of favor].


###### Sifrei Devarim 215:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:7)


אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן מְרֻבּוֹת, וְכֻלָּן אֲהוּבוֹת אוֹ כֻלָּן שְׂנוּאוֹת, מִנַּיִן אֲפִלּוּ הֵן שְׁתַּיִם? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים**.


But I still might infer only that
this rule applies when there are *many* wives
*all* of whom are favored,
or *all* of whom are rejected.
How do I know that it applies as well
even when there are *two* wives?
The Teaching states:
*two wives* (Dt. 21:15).


###### Sifrei Devarim 215:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:8)


אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן **שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים**, **אַחַת אֲהוּבָה וְאַחַת שְׂנוּאָה**, מִנַּיִן אֲפִלּוּ אַחַת וְהִיא אֲהוּבָה, אֲפִלּוּ אַחַת וְהִיא שְׂנוּאָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **אֲהוּבָה** – **אֲהוּבָה**, **שְׂנוּאָה** – **שְׂנוּאָה**; רִבָּה הַכָּתוּב.


But I still might infer only that
this rule applies when there are *two* wives,
*one* of whom is favored
and *one* of whom is rejected?
And how do I know that it applies as well
even if there is only *one* wife and she is favored,
or there is only *one* wife and she is rejected?
The Teaching states:
*Favored* and the *favored* (Dt. 21:15),
*rejected* and the *rejected*—
the redundancy of the verse permits expansion of the rule
[to include many wives
in various degrees of favor].


###### Sifrei Devarim 215:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:9)


אֵיזוֹ הִיא **אֲהוּבָה**? אֲהוּבָה לִפְנֵי הַמָּקוֹם; **שְׂנוּאָה**? שְׂנוּאָה לִפְנֵי הַמָּקוֹם. יָכוֹל אֵין לִי אֶלָּא אֲנוּסָה וּמְפֻתָּה, שֶׁאֵינָן לוֹ כְּדֶרֶךְ כָּל הַנָּשִׁים, מִנַּיִן אַלְמָנָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, גְּרוּשָׁה וַחֲלוּצָה לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **שְׂנוּאָה** – **שְׂנוּאָה**; רִבָּה אֶת הָעֲרָיוֹת שֶׁהֵן בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.


3. Which is the *favored*?
One who is favored in the eyes of
the All-Present [for her virtues].
And the *rejected*?
One who is rejected in the eyes of
The All-Present [for her vices].
Is it possible to say that
[at issue is the love of the All-Present]? I might infer only that
[at issue is] a woman who has been raped
or one who has been seduced,
since a husband’s way with her
is different than it is with other women.
On what basis do I know that
[marriages between] a widow and a High Priest,
or between a divorcee or a Shoe-loosener¹⁴. This is a widow whose levir has refused to marry her. She must perform the “Shoe-loosening rite” (*khalitzah*) before re-marrying. See *Pisqa’* 288-291 and a common Priest
are legitimate?
The Teaching states:
“Favored”¹⁵ and with the direct article, *ha’ahuvah;* literally, “beloved.” and “the favored” (Dt. 21:15);
“Rejected”¹⁶ and with the direct article, *hasenu’ah;* literally, “hated.” and “the rejected”—
this redundancy permits expansion of the rule
[to include the wives of Priests who
should not have married into priestly families].

¹⁴ Heb: khalutzah
¹⁵ Heb: ‘ahuvah
¹⁶ Heb: senu’ah


###### Sifrei Devarim 215:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:10)


וַעֲדַיִן לֹא אֲרַבֶּה אֶת הָעֲרָיוֹת שֶׁחַיָּבִין עֲלֵיהֶן כָּרֵת בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **שְׂנוּאָה** – **שְׂנוּאָה**, רִבָּה אֶת הָעֲרָיוֹת שֶׁחַיָּבִים עֲלֵיהֶן כָּרֵת בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם; וַעֲדַיִן לֹא אֲרַבֶּה אֶת הָעֲרָיוֹת שֶׁחַיָּבִים עֲלֵיהֶן מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **שְׂנוּאָה** – **שְׂנוּאָה**, רִבָּה.


4. Now, should I include proscribed marriages
between close relatives,
[for which the Torah itself provides no penalty,]
but not include marriages between close relatives
for which the penalty is heavenly excision?
The Teaching states:
“Rejected” and “the rejected” (Dt. 21:15)—
Does this redundancy permit expansion of the rule
to include marriages between close relatives
for which the penalty is *heavenly excision*,
but *not* include marriages between close relatives
for which the penalty is *judicial execution*?
The Teaching states:
“Rejected” and “the rejected” (Dt. 21:15)—
this redundancy permits expansion of the rule
[to include all marriages that are illegitimate].


###### Sifrei Devarim 215:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:11)


יָכוֹל אֲפִלּוּ שִׁפְחָה, אֲפִלּוּ נָכְרִית? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **כִּי תִהְיֶיןָ לְאִישׁ**, מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בָּהֶן הֲוָיָה; יָצְאוּ אֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן הֲוָיָה.


Is it possible to say, then, that
this rule applies even to a slave-girl, and even to a gentile?
The Teaching states:
“Should a man have two *wives*” (Dt. 21:15)—
this refers to a man who is legitimately married to the women.
But it excludes these two,
[namely, the slave-girl and the gentile,]
for their marriages are not legitimate.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:12)


**וְיָלְדוּ לוֹ בָנִים**, מִי שֶׁהַוְּלָדוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ; יָצְאוּ אֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין הַוְּלָדוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ.


5. “And they bear *him* children” (Dt. 21:15)—
the children must be his,
thereby excluding the children of these two,
who [under the rules of inheritance] are not considered his.


###### Sifrei Devarim 215:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/215:13)


דָּבָר אַחֵר: **וְיָלְדוּ לוֹ בָנִים** – הַבָּנִים בַּתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת, וְאֵין הַבָּנוֹת בַּתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת. לְפִי שֶׁמָּצִינוּ שֶׁהַבָּנוֹת נִכְנָסוֹת לְנַחֲלָה תַּחַת הָאַחִים, לַחֲלוֹק בְּשָׁוֶה, יָכוֹל תְּהֵא בְּכוֹרָה נוֹהֶגֶת בָּהֶן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וְיָלְדוּ לוֹ בָנִים**, הַבָּנִים בַּתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת וְאֵין הַבָּנוֹת בַּתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת.


Another word:
**“And they bear him *children*”**¹⁷ can mean “male children” or children of either sex. **(Dt. 21:15)—**
**sons are covered by this Teaching,**
**but daughters**¹⁸. **are *not* covered by this Teaching.**
Yet we find that
**daughters may claim their inheritance**
**in place of their dead brothers,**
**to take an equal share**
**[with relatives yet living]** ¹⁹ (Nu. 27:1-12).
Is it possible to say that
the right of the First-born son applies to them?
The Teaching states:
**“And they bear him *children*” (Dt. 21:15)—**
**sons are covered by this Teaching,**
**but daughters are not covered by this Teaching.**

“Then, the *son*” (Dt. 21:15)—
but not a child of undetermined sex,²⁰
or one with male and female sexual organs²¹.

“Born *first*” (Dt. 21:15)—
but not one [whose birth-order] is in doubt.

“Is *assigned to* the rejected wife” (Dt. 21:15)—
the verse announces to you that
the First-born son, [who is your principal heir,]
*belongs to* the rejected wife!



## Paragraph 216

###### Sifrei Devarim 216:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/216:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/216:1)


(דברים כא טז) **וְהָיָה בְּיוֹם הַנְחִילוֹ אֶת בָּנָיו**, בַּיּוֹם מַפִּילִים נַחֲלוֹת וְאֵין מַפִּילִים נַחֲלוֹת בַּלַּיְלָה.


**Pisqa’ 216**²²
1. “So when *the day* comes to bequeath to his sons” (Dt. 21:16).
Bequests are distributed by day,
but they are not distributed by night.

footnotes:
²² H:227-228; JN2:119.


###### Sifrei Devarim 216:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/216:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/216:2)


**אֵת אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה לוֹ**, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהַבֵּן נוֹטֵל בָּרָאוּי כְּבַמֻּחְזָק.


“That which *is to be his*” (Dt. 21:16)—
***is to be his*, teaches that the son takes,**
**as his inheritance from his father’s estate,**
**both its anticipated income and its current holdings**.²³ 217.4.

footnotes:
²³ Cf. M. Bech.8:9 and Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 216:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/216:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/216:3)


**לֹא יוּכַל לְבַכֵּר**, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁי לְבַכֵּר. יָכוֹל לֹא יְבַכֵּר, וְאִם בִּכֵּר – יְהֵא מְבֻכָּר? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **לֹא יוּכַל לְבַכֵּר**, הָא אִם בִּכֵּר – אֵינוֹ מְבֻכָּר.


2. “He is unable to transfer the *right* of the First-born” (Dt. 21:16)—
this teaches that the father has
no right to transfer *the status* of the First-born
[to another son by a different wife].
Is it possible to say that,
while the father has no *right* to transfer the status of the First-born,
if he does so, it is done?
The Teaching states:
“He is unable to transfer the *right* of the First-born” (Dt. 21:16)—
thus, if the father *does* transfer this status,
it is not [effectively] done.


###### Sifrei Devarim 216:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/216:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/216:4)


**אֶת בֶּן הָאֲהוּבָה**, כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּצָא רֹאשׁוֹ וְרֻבּוֹ בַּחַיִּים – פּוֹטֵר אֶת הַבָּא אַחֲרָיו מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה.


“To *the son* of the favored wife” (Dt. 21:16)—
as soon as the First-born’s head
and most of his body emerge alive,
he exempts any brother born after him
[even of a different mother]
from [exercising the right of] the First-born.


###### Sifrei Devarim 216:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/216:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/216:5)


**עַל פְּנֵי בֶן הַשְּׂנוּאָה הַבְּכֹר** – אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבֵּן הַבְּכוֹר לַשְּׂנוּאָה.


“Instead of to *the son* of the rejected wife, the rightful First-born” (Dt. 21:16)—
even though the First-born son belongs to the rejected wife,
[his father cannot transfer First-born status to his son by a favored wife].



## Paragraph 217

###### Sifrei Devarim 217:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/217:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/217:1)


(דברים כא יז) **כִּי אֶת הַבְּכֹר בֶּן הַשְּׂנוּאָה יַכִּיר** – יַכִּירֶנּוּ לַאֲחֵרִים, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁנֶּאֱמָן אָדָם לוֹמַר ׳זֶה בְּנִי בְּכוֹר׳. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁנֶּאֱמָן אָדָם לוֹמַר ׳זֶה בְּנִי בְּכוֹר׳, כָּךְ נֶאֱמָן לוֹמַר ׳זֶה בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה וְזֶה בֶּן חֲלוּצָה׳, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן.


**Pisqa’ 217**²⁴
1. “Rather, he must *recognize* the First-born son of the rejected wife” (Dt. 21:17).
*Recognition* implies that
[the father] should make known to others
[his son’s First-born status].
This teaches that
a person can be relied upon when he says:
Meet my First-born son!
R. Judah says:
Just as a person can be relied upon [to be truthful]
when he says:
Meet my First-born son
[who is entitled to inherit twice the sum due his brothers],
so, too, can [a Priest] be relied upon [to be truthful]
when he says:
Meet the son of the divorcee
[whom I later married]!
Or: Meet the son of my sister-in-law,
the Shoe-loosener²⁵, see Dt. 25:5-11. Cf. *Pisqa’ot* 288-291.
[whom I later married]!²⁶ Cf. Rashi, B. Qid. 78b, s.v., *l’a mib`ay’a ‘eihu*
But sages say:
He cannot be relied upon [to disadvantage his son].

footnotes:
²⁴ H:228-229; JN2:120-121.
²⁵ On levirat marriage and the rite of khalitzah
²⁶ A son sired by a Priest and a divorcee, or a Shoe-loosener, is disqualified from serving in the sacrificial service. The priest is assumed to be truthful in such a grave genealogical matter. I follow RH ad loc.


###### Sifrei Devarim 217:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/217:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/217:2)


**לָתֶת לוֹ פִּי שְׁנַיִם** – פִּי שְׁנַיִם בּוֹ. אוֹ פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּכָל הַנְּכָסִים? הֲרֵי אַתָּה דָן: הוֹאִיל וְנוֹחֵל עִם אֶחָד וְנוֹחֵל עִם חֲמִשָּׁה, מַה מָּצִינוּ כְּשֶׁנּוֹחֵל עִם אֶחָד – פִּי שְׁנַיִם בּוֹ, אַף כְּשֶׁנּוֹחֵל עִם חֲמִשָּׁה – פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּאֶחָד מֵהֶם.


2. “By giving him *two times as much* from all his property” (Dt. 21:17).
Does this mean that the First-born receives
twice as much as any one share
[e.g., forty percent]?²⁷
Or [does he receive] twice as much as
the sum of all property [set aside for the heirs by the estate
[e.g., fifty per cent of the whole]?²⁸
Look—
You can reason it out this way.
Whereas [the First-born is either] sharing the estate
with one other heir, or sharing it with five—
since we find that,
when he shares with one heir,
he takes twice as much as that heir
[that is, forty per cent, to his brother’s twenty per cent],
so, too, when he shares with five heirs,
[namely, himself and four brothers,]
he takes twice as much property
[at fifty percent of the whole]
as any one of their shares
[each of which amounts to twenty five percent].

###### Sifrei Devarim 217:3

אוֹ כַּלֵּךְ לְדֶרֶךְ זוֹ: הוֹאִיל וְנוֹחֵל עִם אֶחָד וְנוֹחֵל עִם חֲמִשָּׁה, מַה מָּצִינוּ כְּשֶׁנּוֹחֵל עִם אֶחָד – פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּכָל הַנְּכָסִים, אַף כְּשֶׁנּוֹחֵל עִם חֲמִשָּׁה – פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּכָל הַנְּכָסִים! תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְהָיָה בְּיוֹם הַנְחִילוֹ אֶת בָּנָיו״, רִבָּה נַחֲלָה לַבָּנִים.


Perhaps we can try another approach?
Whereas the First-born is [either] sharing the estate
with one other heir, or with five other heirs—
since we find that,
when he shares with one heir,
he takes twice as much property as any one of them,
[forty percent as opposed to twenty percent,]
so, too, when he shares with five heirs,
he should take twice as much property as all of them
[fifty percent as opposed to twenty percent].3. The Teaching states:
“So when the day comes to *bequeath* to his sons” (Dt. 21:16)—
this includes the *release* of the heirs’ inheritance
[of the assets of the estate].

4. And, similarly, he [Jacob] says [to Joseph]:
“And I have given you a single portion more than your brothers” (Gn. 48:22)—
[this is the right of the First-born, transferred from Reuben].
And He says [of Reuben and Joseph]:
“And my son, Reuben, first-born of Israel! He is, indeed, the First-born! Yet, for desecrating his father’s couch, his right of the First-born was given to the sons of
Joseph b. Israel, so he is no longer mentioned as the First-born” (1Chron. 5:1-2).
And He says:
“For Judah dominated his brothers, and royalty proceeded from his line,
but the right of the First-born went to Joseph” (1Chron. 5:2).

Now that we have learned to
include the sons’ inheritance [in the total estate],

Whereas [the first-born] can share

or he can share it with five heirs—
just as we have found that,
when he shares with one heir,
he takes twice as much property as this one,

is a double share of any one of them.

(דברים כא כב) ״כִּי יִהְיֶה בְאִישׁ חֵטְא מִשְׁפַּט מָוֶת וְהוּמָת״ – לֹא בְּשַׁבָּת וְלֹא בְּיָמִים טוֹבִים.


Another word:
Simply because this guy
consumes his father’s wealth,
do you claim that the
stubbornly incorrigible son
must be put to death?
No!
**He is condemned because of**
**what he will become.**
**Better he should die innocently now,**
**Rather than later as a sinner!**³⁶
This guy’s father desired
a certain fine-looking captive (cf. Dt. 21:10-14).
So, he brought Satan into his home.
As a result, the son became stub bornly incorrigible,
and brought upon his father an early death.
[Accordingly, the Torah immediately teaches:]
“When a man commits a sin worthy of death, he shall be *put to death*” (Dt. 21:22)—
[This son, then, is punished for the death of his father,]
but he is not executed on the Sabbath or on Feast Days.

Another word:

critical of his father’s teachings.
“Incorrigible” (Dt. 21:18)—
in criticism of his mother’s teachings.
“Who is stubbornly”—
critical of the teachings of the Torah.
“Incorrigible”—
in his criticism of the teachings of the Prophets.
“Who is stubbornly”—
critical of the testimony of witnesses.
“Incorrigible”—
in criticism of the rulings of judges.

Zeira told me three traditions
in the name of
the leading figures of Jerusalem:

[Second,] regarding the stubbornly incorrigible son—

4. “He *heeds neither* the voice of his father *nor* the voice of his mother” (Dt. 21:18)—
Is it possible to say that
[he stands liable]
even if they told him to light the lamp, and he refused?
The Teaching [twice] states:
“He *heeds neither*” (Dt. 21:18),
“He *will not heed*” (Dt. 21:20)—
[thus, anticipating more serious acts of defiance].
[The repetition also]
permits an analogical inference:
Just as *he will not heed*,
mentioned elsewhere (Dt. 21:20), applies only to drunken gluttony—
so, too, *he heeds neither*
mentioned here (Dt. 21:18)
applies only to drunken gluttony.
Furthermore:
**Just as *he will not heed*,”**
**mentioned elsewhere (Dt. 21:20),**
**[does not apply] until he steals**
**from his father and from his mother**
**[in order to pay for his meat and wine]—**
**so, too, *heeds neither* mentioned here (Dt. 21:18),**
**[does not apply] until he steals**
**from his father and from his mother.**³⁸

###### Sifrei Devarim 219:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/219:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/219:1)


(דברים כא יט) **וְתָפְשׂוּ בוֹ אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ** – מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאֵינוֹ חַיָּב עַד שֶׁיִּהְיוּ לוֹ אָב וָאֵם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם לֹא הָיְתָה אִמּוֹ רְאוּיָה לְאָבִיו – אֵינוֹ נַעֲשֶׂה בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה.


**Pisqa’ 219**³⁹
1. “Then his *father and mother* shall seize him” (Dt. 21:19).
This teaches that
he can only be liable for punishment
while he has a [living] *father and mother*:
words of R. Meir.
R. Judah says:
**If his mother was unsuited [by improper lineage]**⁴⁰ and the father was of unimpaired lineage. See *Pisqa’* 196.1. **to marry his father,**
**the son cannot be held liable**
**for punishment as a persistently incorrigible son.** ⁴¹

footnotes:
³⁹ H:230-231; JN2:124-125.
⁴⁰ That is, his mother was disqualified from marrying into the priesthood, and his father was a priest, or if the mother was a mamzeret
⁴¹ //M. San.8:4.


###### Sifrei Devarim 219:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/219:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/219:2)


**וְהוֹצִיאוּ אֹתוֹ אֶל זִקְנֵי עִירוֹ וְאֶל שַׁעַר מְקֹמוֹ** – מִצְוָה בְּזִקְנֵי עִירוֹ וּבְשַׁעַר מְקוֹמוֹ.


2. “And they shall take him to the *elders* of his city, and to the *gate* of his place” (Dt. 21:19)—
it is essential that the *elders* of his city
[bear witness] at the *gate* of his home.


###### Sifrei Devarim 219:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/219:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/219:3)


(דברים כא כ) **וְאָמְרוּ אֶל זִקְנֵי עִירוֹ בְּנֵנוּ זֶה** – זֶהוּ שֶׁלָּקָה בִּפְנֵיכֶם, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאִם מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶם אֵינוֹ נִסְקָל.


“And they shall say to the elders of his city: *This* son of *ours*” (Dt. 21:20)—
“*this one*,” who has recently been beaten before you.
The phrase*, ours*, teaches that
if one parent has died, the son is not stoned.


###### Sifrei Devarim 219:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/219:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/219:4)


הָיָה אֶחָד מֵהֶם גִּדֵּם אוֹ חִגֵּר אוֹ אִלֵּם אוֹ סוּמָה אוֹ חֵרֵשׁ – אֵינוֹ נַעֲשֶׂה בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְתָפְשׂוּ בוֹ״ – וְלֹא גִדְּמִים, ״וְהוֹצִיאוּ אוֹתוֹ״ – וְלֹא חִגְּרִים, **וְאָמְרוּ** – וְלֹא אִלְּמִים, **בְּנֵנוּ זֶה** – וְלֹא סוּמִים, **אֵינֶנּוּ שֹׁמֵעַ בְּקֹלֵנוּ** – וְלֹא חֵרְשִׁים. מַתְרִים בּוֹ בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה וּמַלְקִים אוֹתוֹ; חָזַר וְקִלְקֵל – נִדּוֹן בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְשָׁלֹשׁ, וְאֵינוֹ נִסְקָל עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ שָׁם שְׁלֹשָׁה הָרִאשׁוֹנִים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: **בְּנֵנוּ זֶה** – זֶהוּ שֶׁלָּקָה בִּפְנֵיכֶם. **זוֹלֵל וְסֹבֵא** – זוֹלֵל בְּבָשָׂר וְסוֹבֵא בְּיַיִן, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר – זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר (משלי כג כ): ״אַל תְּהִי בְסֹבְאֵי יָיִן בְּזֹלְלֵי בָשָׂר לָמוֹ״, וְאוֹמֵר (משלי כג כא): ״כִּי זוֹלֵל וְסֹבֵא יִוָּרֵשׁ, וּקְרָעִים תַּלְבִּישׁ נוּמָה״.


**If one of them is an *amputee*, or *lame*, or *mute*, or *blind*, or *deaf*,**
**he cannot be held liable for punishment**
**as a stubbornly incorrigible son,**
**for it is said:**
**“They shall *seize* him” (Dt. 21:19)—**
**so they cannot be *amputees*.**
**“*Bring* him out to the gate” (Dt. 21:19)—**
**so they cannot be *lame*.**
**“And they shall *declare*” (Dt. 21:19)—**
**so they cannot be *mute*.**
**“*This* son of ours” (Dt. 21:19)—**
**[since *this* implies gesturing towards the son,]**
**they cannot be blind.**
**“Does not *heed* our voice” (Dt. 21:19)—**
**[since they observe that he doesn’t *heed*,]**
**they cannot be deaf!**
**The elders then warn him,**
**before three witnesses,**
**[of the consequences of his acts,]**
**and administer a beating.**
**If he repeated his offenses,**
**he is brought to a Court of Twenty-Three.**
**But he is not stoned unless**
**three of the *original* elders are in session,**
**as it is said:**
**“*This* son of ours” (Dt. 21:20)—**
***this one* who has recently been beaten before you.**
**“Is a *gluttonous drunkard*” (Dt. 21:20)—**
**stuffing himself with meat**
**and swilling wine.**⁴²
3. Now, even though
**[the Torah contains] no clear proscription**
**against drunken gluttony**,⁴³
the Prophets⁴⁴ suggest as much:
“Don’t be among the wine-swillers or the meat-bingers!” (Prov. 23:20).
And He says:
“For *the wine-swiller* and *meat-binger* will know want,
and their stupor will clothe them in tatters!” (Prov. 23:21)

footnotes:
⁴² //M. San. 8:4.
⁴³ Cf. T. San.11:6.
⁴⁴ This is not a reference to the scriptural canon of the Prophet in general, or to any book in that canon. Rather, the “prophet” in question is King Solomon, reputed compiler of Proverbs.



## Paragraph 220

###### Sifrei Devarim 220:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/220:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/220:1)


(דברים כא כא) **וּרְגָמֻהוּ כָּל אַנְשֵׁי עִירוֹ**, וְכִי כָּל אַנְשֵׁי עִירוֹ רוֹגְמִים אוֹתוֹ? אֶלָּא בְּמַעֲמַד כָּל אַנְשֵׁי עִירוֹ.


**Pisqa’ 220**⁴⁵
1. **“Then *all* the populace of his city shall pummel**⁴⁶; root: *r-g-m.* Dt. 22:22, in similar context uses the root: *s-q-l*, with identical meaning. **him” (Dt. 21:21)—**
**Now, can the *entire* populace of his city**
**actually pummel him?**
**Rather, [they appoint] a deputation.**

footnotes:
⁴⁵ H:231; JN2:126.
⁴⁶ Heb: regemuhu


###### Sifrei Devarim 220:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/220:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/220:2)


**בָאֲבָנִים**, יָכוֹל בַּאֲבָנִים מְרֻבּוֹת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (ויקרא כ ב): ״בָּאֶבֶן״. יָכוֹל בְּאֶבֶן אַחַת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **בָאֲבָנִים**, אֱמֹר מֵעַתָּה: לֹא מֵת בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה – יָמוּת בַּשְּׁנִיָּה.


**“With *stone*s” (Dt. 21:21)—**
**Is it possible to say that**
***many* stones are used?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“With *stone*” (Lv. 20:2).**
**Is it possible to say, then, that**
**only *one* stone is used?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“With *stones*” (Dt. 21:21)!**
**From this you may conclude that**
**if he doesn’t die from the first stone,**
**let him die from the second!**⁴⁷Sifra, *qedoshim,* par. 10:4 . Cf. *Pisqa’* 149.1, 240.1, 242.1 for parallels within Sifre.

footnotes:
⁴⁷ // Sifre Nu., 114; //


###### Sifrei Devarim 220:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/220:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/220:3)


אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וְכִי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָכַל זֶה תַּרְטִימַר בָּשָׂר וְשָׁתָה חֲצִי לוֹג יַיִן הוּא נִסְקָל? אֶלָּא הִגִּיעָה תּוֹרָה לְסוֹף עִנְיָנוֹ שֶׁל זֶה, וְאָמְרָה יָמוּת זַכַּי וְאַל יָמוּת חַיָּב. שֶׁמִּיתָתָם שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים – הֲנָיָה לָהֶם וַהֲנָיָה לָעוֹלָם, וְשֶׁל צַדִּיקִים – רַע לָהֶם וְרַע לָעוֹלָם. יַיִן וְשֵׁנָה לָרְשָׁעִים – הֲנָיָה לָהֶם וַהֲנָיָה לָעוֹלָם, וְלַצַּדִּיקִים – רַע לָהֶם וְרַע לָעוֹלָם. שֶׁקֶט לָרְשָׁעִים – רַע לָהֶם וְרַע לָעוֹלָם, וְלַצַּדִּיקִים – הֲנָיָה לָהֶם וַהֲנָאָה לָעוֹלָם.


2. Said R. Yose:
Does this guy get a stoning
for eating a single serving⁴⁸. Roughly three ounces. of meat
and drinking a half measure⁴⁹Roughly .32 liters, of wine?
Not at all!
The Torah has plumbed the depths
of this guy’s character,
and taught:
**Better he should die innocently now**
**rather than later as a sinner!** ⁵⁰ 218.2.
**For the death of the Wicked**
**is as beneficial to them**
**as it is to the world**
**[since their death forestalls further sins].**
**But the death of the Righteous**
**is as bad for them**
**as it is for the world,**
**[since they may no longer acquire merit through righteous deeds,**
**nor does the world benefit from their righteous deeds]!**
**Wine and a good nap**
**bring the Wicked pleasure,**
**as they bring the world pleasure.**
**But to the Righteous,**
**these are as bad for them**
**as they are for the world!**
**Peace of mind, to the Wicked,**
**is as bad for them**
**as it is for the world.**
**But to the Righteous,**
**it is as beneficial to them**
**as it is for the world!**

⁴⁸ Heb./Lat.: tartimor
⁴⁹ Heb: log .
⁵⁰ =M. San.8:5. Cf. Pisqa’

**וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע** – בַּעֵר עוֹשֵׂי הָרָעוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל!


**“And you shall expunge the evil from your midst” (Dt. 21:21)—**
**That is, expunge the evil-doers from Israel!**⁵¹ 151, 155, 187, etc.

## Paragraph 221

###### Sifrei Devarim 221:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:1)


(דברים כא כב) **וְכִי יִהְיֶה בְאִישׁ חֵטְא מִשְׁפַּט מָוֶת וְהוּמָת**, הָאִישׁ נִתְלֶה, וְאֵין הָאִשָּׁה נִתְלֵית. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אַף הָאִשָּׁה נִתְלֵית.


**Pisqa’ 221**⁵²
1. “Now, *if a man* commits a sin worthy of the sentence of death,
then *he* shall be *put to death*” (Dt. 21:22)—
**A man is hanged,**
**but a woman cannot be hanged.**

footnotes:
⁵² H:231-233; JN2:127-129.


###### Sifrei Devarim 221:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:2)


אָמַר לָהֶם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: וַהֲלֹא שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטָח תָּלָה נָשִׁים בְּאַשְׁקְלוֹן! אָמְרוּ לוֹ: שְׁמוֹנִים נָשִׁים תָּלָה, וְאֵין דָּנִים שְׁנַיִם בְּיוֹם אֶחָד! אֶלָּא שֶׁהַשָּׁעָה צְרִיכָה, לְלַמֵּד בָּהּ אֶת אֲחֵרִים.


**R. Eliezer says:**
**Even a woman can be hanged. Said R. Eliezer to them:**
**Didn’t Shimon b. Shatach hang women in Ashkelon**
**[on charges of witchraft]?**
**They said to him:**
**He hung eighty women, and didn’t sentence two**
**on a single day!**⁵³
Actually, that was an extreme measure,
designed to instruct others,
[but it is not a legal precedent]!

footnotes:
⁵³ // M. San.6:4.


###### Sifrei Devarim 221:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:3)


**וְתָלִיתָ אוֹתוֹ**, יָכוֹל יְהוּ כָל הַנִּסְקָלִים נִתְלִים? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (דברים כא כג): ״כִּי קִלְלַת אֱלֹהִים תָּלוּי״ – אַחַר שֶׁרִבָּה הַכָּתוּב מִיעֵט! הֲרֵי אָנוּ לְמֵדִים אוֹתוֹ מִן הַמְגַדֵּף: מָה מְגַדֵּף מְיֻחָד, שֶׁפָּשַׁט יָדוֹ בָּעִקָּר, וַהֲרֵי הוּא נִתְלֶה – כָּךְ כָּל הַפּוֹשֵׁט יָדוֹ בָּעִקָּר הֲרֵי הוּא נִתְלֶה! רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מָה מְגַדֵּף מְיֻחָד, שֶׁהוּא נִסְקָל וַהֲרֵי הוּא נִתְלֶה – כָּךְ כָּל הַנִּסְקָלִים נִתְלִים. יָכוֹל יְהוּ תּוֹלִים אוֹתוֹ חַי כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁהַמַּלְכוּת עוֹשָׂה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וְהוּמָת וְתָלִיתָ אֹתוֹ עַל עֵץ**.


2. “And you *shall hang* him” (Dt. 21:22)—
**is it possible to say that**
***all* who are stoned should be hanged?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“For the hanged one is an *affront* to God” (Dt. 21:22)—**
after an inclusive clause,
[“you *shall hang* him”],
the verse limits the rule
[calling it “*an affront*”]?
**Look—we learn this from the case of the *reviler***⁵⁴ literally, “blasphemer.” **(e.g., Nu. 15:30).**
**Just as the reviler is distinctive,**
**in attacking a fundamental principle [e.g., divine justice]**
**and is hanged,**
**shouldn’t anyone attacking a fundamental principle,**
**also be hanged?**
**R. Eliezer says:**
**Just as the reviler is distinctive,**
**in being stoned and then hanged,**
**shouldn’t all who are stoned**
**likewise be hanged**?⁵⁵
Is it possible to say that
He should be hanged alive—Imperial-style?⁵⁶
The Teaching states:
“Then he shall be put to death, and you shall hang *him* from a wood” (Dt. 21:22)—
[the hanging, unlike a Roman crucifixion, is not a form of torture].

footnotes:
⁵⁴ Heb: hamegadeif;
⁵⁵ // M. San. 6:4.
⁵⁶ That is, crucified.


###### Sifrei Devarim 221:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:4)


**אֹתוֹ** – וְלֹא אֶת כֵּלָיו; **אֹתוֹ** – וְלֹא אֶת עֵדָיו; **אֹתוֹ** – וְלֹא אֶת זוֹמְמָיו; **אֹתוֹ** – וְלֹא שְׁנַיִם בְּיוֹם אֶחָד!


*Him*—
implying that his clothes are not hung [with the body].
*Him*—
implying that witnesses
[who testified falsely against him]
are not hanged [after their execution].
*Him*—
implying that colluding witnesses
[who have been exposed as such]
are not hanged [after their execution].
*Him*—
And *not two* on a single day!


###### Sifrei Devarim 221:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:5)


**עַל עֵץ**, יָכוֹל בְּעֵץ הַתָּלוּשׁ. אוֹ בְּעֵץ הַמְחֻבָּר? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (דברים כא כג): ״כִּי קָבוֹר תִּקְבְּרֶנּוּ״ – בְּעֵץ שֶׁנִּקְבָּר עִמּוֹ, אֱמֹר מֵעַתָּה: בְּעֵץ הַתָּלוּשׁ וְלֹא בְּעֵץ הַמְחֻבָּר.


“From a *wood*” (Dt. 21:22)—
Is it possible that *wood*
can refer either to an uprooted tree
or to a tree still attached to the earth?
The Teaching states:
“You shall *quickly bury* it” (Dt. 21:23)—
the tree is buried with him.
On this basis you can teach:
[He is hanged] on an uprooted tree,
but not to one still attached to the earth.


###### Sifrei Devarim 221:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:6)


מִנַּיִן לַמֵּלִין אֶת מֵתוֹ שֶׁהוּא עוֹבֵר בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **לֹא תָלִין נִבְלָתוֹ עַל הָעֵץ**. הֱלִינוֹ לִכְבוֹדוֹ, לְהָבִיא לוֹ אָרוֹן וְתַכְרִיכִים, יָכוֹל יְהֵא עוֹבֵר עָלָיו? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **עַל הָעֵץ** – מָה עֵץ מְיֻחָד, שֶׁהוּא נִוּוּל לוֹ – אַף כָּל שֶׁהוּא נִוּוּל לוֹ. יָצָא הַמֵּלִין לִכְבוֹדוֹ, שֶׁאֵין נִוּוּל לוֹ.


3. On what basis do I know that
if you permit his body to hang until morning,
you transgress a proscription?
The Teaching states:
“Do not permit his corpse *to over-night* on the *wood*” (Dt. 21:23).
If you delay burial till morning, for the sake of his dignity
—to bring him a coffin or shroud—
is it possible that
you transgress a proscription?
The Teaching states:
“On the *wood*” (Dt. 21:22)—
just as wood is distinctive,
in that it is an element of his disgrace,
so, too, anything that
disgraces him [should be proscribed].
This excludes delaying burial till morning
for the sake of his dignity,
since this is not an element of his disgrace
[but an effort to handle the corpse with respect].


###### Sifrei Devarim 221:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:7)


**לֹא תָלִין נִבְלָתוֹ עַל הָעֵץ** – מִצְוַת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה. **כִּי קָבוֹר תִּקְבְּרֶנּוּ** – מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה. כֵּיצַד עוֹשִׂים לוֹ? מַמְתִּינִים לוֹ עַד חֲשֵׁכָה, וְתוֹלִים לוֹ – וּמַתִּירִים אוֹתוֹ, וְאִם לָן – עוֹבְרִים עָלָיו בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: **לֹא תָלִין נִבְלָתוֹ עַל הָעֵץ**.


4. “*Do not* permit his corpse to over-night on the wood” (Dt. 21:23)—
this is a proscriptive commandment.
“*You shall* quickly bury it” (Dt. 21:23)—
This is a prescriptive commandment.
So, how do they treat the corpse
[in obedience to both
the prescription and proscription]?
They wait until night-fall and hang him
[thus fulfilling the proscription].
Then they immediately untie [and bury] him,
[in fulfillment of the prescription.]
But were the corpse to over-night there,
they would be transgressing a proscription.
For it is said:
“*Do not* permit his corpse to over-night on the wood” (Dt. 21:23).


###### Sifrei Devarim 221:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:8)


**כִּי קִלְלַת אֱלֹהִים תָּלוּי**, כְּלוֹמַר: מִפְּנֵי מָה זֶה תָּלוּי? מִפְּנֵי שֶׁקִּלֵּל אֶת הַשֵּׁם, וְנִמְצָא שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם מִתְחַלֵּל.


**“For the hanged one is an affront to *God*” (Dt. 21:22)—**
**bystanders will see him and say:**
**Why is this guy hanging there?**
**Because he reviled the [Holy] Name!**
**And thus, [preservation of the reviler’s memory]**
**profanes the Name of Heaven.**⁵⁷

###### Sifrei Devarim 221:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:9)


הָאִישׁ נִסְקָל עָרוֹם, וְאֵין הָאִשָּׁה נִסְקֶלֶת עֲרוּמָה. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֶחָד הָאִישׁ וְאֶחָד הָאִשָּׁה, אֶלָּא שֶׁהָאִישׁ – תּוֹלִים אוֹתוֹ וּפָנָיו כְּלַפֵּי הָעָם וַאֲחוֹרָיו כְּלַפֵּי הָעֵץ, וְהָאִשָּׁה – פָּנֶיהָ כְּלַפֵּי הָעֵץ וַאֲחוֹרֶיהָ כְּלַפֵּי הָעָם. הָאִישׁ – סֶרֶט אֶחָד מִלְּפָנָיו, וְהָאִשָּׁה – שְׁנֵי סְרָטִים: אֶחָד מִלְּפָנֶיהָ וְאֶחָד מֵאַחֲרֶיהָ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁכֻּלָּהּ עֶרְוָה.


5. **A man is stoned naked,**
**but a woman is not stoned naked.**
**R. Judah says:**
**It is the same for a man and a woman,**
**except that they hang a man**
**facing toward the people**
**with his back towards the wood.**
**But a woman faces the wood,**
**while her back is towards the people.**⁵⁸
**A man holds a single cloth**
**in front of himself,**
**while a woman holds two cloths—**
**one in front of herself,**
**and one from behind, .**⁵⁹
**For her entire body is**
**an enticement to sin.**⁶⁰ 221.5 is lacking in several mss. Cf. F:254-255, n.16.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/221:10)


**וְלֹא תְטַמֵּא אֶת אַדְמָתְךָ אֲשֶׁר ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ נוֹתֵן לְךָ נַחֲלָה** – לְהַזְהִיר בֵּית דִּין עַל כָּךְ.


7. “And don’t pollute the soil which HASHEM your God is giving you for an inheritance” (Dt. 21:23)—

## Paragraph 222

###### Sifrei Devarim 222:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/222:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/222:1)


(שמות כג ה) ״כִּי תִרְאֶה״, יָכוֹל אֲפִלּוּ רָחוֹק מִמֶּנּוּ מְלֹא מִיל? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (שמות כג ד): ״כִּי תִפְגַּע״. אִי ״כִּי תִפְגַּע״, שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי כְּמַשְׁמָעוֹ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״כִּי תִרְאֶה״. הָא כֵּיצַד? שִׁעֲרוּ חֲכָמִים אֶחָד מִשִּׁבְעָה וּמֶחֱצָה בַּמִּיל, שֶׁהוּא רִיס.


**Pisqa’ 222**⁶²
1. “**When you *see***⁶³ root: *r-‘-h.* **your rival’s ass crouching beneath its burden,**
**and you refrain from aiding him—**
**you must exert yourself to aid him” (Ex. 23:5).**
**Is it possible to say that**
**the rule applies even if you are a full *mil*,**⁶⁴ **away?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“When you *encounter***⁶⁵ root: *n-g-`,* “to strike against.” **your enemy’s ox or ass” (Ex. 23:4).**
**The verse specifies *encounter*—**
**should I infer that**
**the usual sense of the term is meant?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“*When* you *see*” (Ex. 23:5)—**
**[suggesting a distant sighting].**
**So, how do we understand this?**
**Sages defined the distance as a *ris***⁶⁶***—***
**equivalent to one-seventh of a *mil***
**and then some*.***⁶⁷
**[One can “see” the animal from the distance of a *ris;* an “encounter”**
**requires only a few cubits].**⁶⁸’, 20.

footnotes:
⁶² H:233-234;JN2:130-131.
⁶³ Heb: tir’eh;
⁶⁴ Roughly equivalent to 1200 yards.
⁶⁵ Heb: tifg`a;
⁶⁶ Roughly 150 yards.
⁶⁷ //T. BM.2:25.
⁶⁸ // Mechilta Ishmael, kaspa


###### Sifrei Devarim 222:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/222:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/222:2)


[״וְחָדַלְתָּ מֵעֲזֹב לוֹ עָזֹב תַּעֲזֹב עִמּוֹ״,] נִמְצֵינוּ לְמֵדִים שֶׁהוּא עוֹבֵר עַל מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה וְעַל מִצְוַת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.


2. **“When you encounter your enemy’s ox or ass gone astray,**
**make every effort to return him” (Ex. 23:4).**
**We turn out to learn about transgressing both**
**a prescriptive commandment and a proscriptive commandment.**


###### Sifrei Devarim 222:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/222:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/222:3)


עָזוֹב תַּעֲזֹב עִמּוֹ – זוֹ פְּרִיקָה; **הָקֵם תָּקִים עִמּוֹ** – זוֹ טְעִינָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶן בְּתֵירָה.


**“*You must* exert yourself to aid him” (Ex. 23:5)—**
**[The prescription is to] help unburden the ass.**
**“You *shall not* see your brother’s ass fallen in the road, while you ignore him.**
**You must labor to get him on his feet” (Dt. 22:4)—**
**[The proscription is against] over-loading the beast:**
**Words of R. Judah b. Bethyra.**⁶⁹

footnotes:
⁶⁹ F:255. n.3, observes that this unit is based upon Ex. 23:5 and is closely paralleled in Mechilta-Ishmael. In his view, the passage, which is also unattested in many versions of Sifre, is foreign to the original work.


###### Sifrei Devarim 222:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/222:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/222:4)


(דברים כב א) **לֹא תִרְאֶה אֶת שׁוֹר אָחִיךָ** – מִצְוַת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה, וּלְהַלָּן הוּא אוֹמֵר (שמות כג ד) ״כִּי תִפְגַּע״ – מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה.


“You *shall not* see your brother’s ox” (Dt. 22:1)—
this is a proscriptive commandment.
Yet, elsewhere He states:
“*When* you encounter your enemy’s ox or ass” (Ex. 23:4)—
This is a prescriptive commandment.


###### Sifrei Devarim 222:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/222:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/222:5)


**שׁוֹר אָחִיךָ**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שׁוֹר אָחִיךָ; שׁוֹר אוֹיִבְךָ מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (שמות כג ד): ״אוֹיִבְךָ״, מִכָּל מָקוֹם. אִם כֵּן לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר **אָחִיךָ**? אֶלָּא מְלַמֵּד שֶׁלֹּא דִבְּרָה תוֹרָה אֶלָּא כְּנֶגֶד הַיֵּצֶר.


“Your *brother’s* ox” (Dt. 22:1)—
I might infer only that
the rule applies to your *brother’s* ox!
On what basis to I include
even your *enemy’s* ox?
The Teaching states:
“Your *enemy’s* ox” (Ex. 23:4)—
[help the animal] no matter who owns it!
**If so, why does it specify “your brother?”**
**Actually, it teaches that**
**the point of the Torah is**
**to defeat the rebellious urge**
**[which can even challenge brotherly love]!**⁷⁰ 225.1.

footnotes:
⁷⁰ So, too, Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 222:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/222:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/222:6)


**אוֹ אֶת שֵׂיוֹ נִדָּחִים** – כְּדֶרֶךְ הַדָּחָתָם. מִכָּן אַתָּה אוֹמֵר (ב״מ פ״ב מ״ט): אֵיזוֹ הִיא אֲבֵדָה? מָצָא חֲמוֹר אוֹ פָּרָה רוֹעִים בַּדֶּרֶךְ – אֵין זוֹ אֲבֵדָה. חֲמוֹר וְכֵלָיו הֲפוּכִים, פָּרָה וְרָצָה בֵּין הַכְּרָמִים – הֲרֵי זוֹ אֲבֵדָה.


3. “Or his sheep driven off” (Dt. 22:1)—
however they might have been scattered.
On this basis you can teach:
**How is a lost object defined?**
**If he found an ass or a cow**
**grazing in a path, that’s no lost object!**
**But an ass with its burden in disaray,**
**or a cow running through a vineyard—**
**Now, that’s a lost object!** ⁷¹

⁷¹ =M. BM.2:9.


###### Sifrei Devarim 222:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/222:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/222:7)


**וְהִתְעַלַּמְתָּ מֵהֶם** – פְּעָמִים שֶׁאַתָּה מִתְעַלֵּם וּפְעָמִים שֶׁאֵין אַתָּה מִתְעַלֵּם. כֵּיצַד? הָיָה כֹהֵן – וְהִיא בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת, אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה זָקֵן – וְאֵינָהּ לְפִי כְבוֹדוֹ, אוֹ שֶׁהָיְתָה שֶׁלּוֹ מְרֻבָּה מִשֶּׁל חֲבֵרוֹ – פָּטוּר! לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר: **וְהִתְעַלַּמְתָּ** – פְּעָמִים שֶׁאַתָּה מִתְעַלֵּם וּפְעָמִים שֶׁאֵין אַתָּה מִתְעַלֵּם.


4. “**While you turn a *blind eye* to them” (Dt. 22:1)—**
**sometimes you do turn a blind eye,**
**and sometimes you don’t turn a blind eye**.⁷² 20.
**For example?**
**If the passer-by was a Priest**
**and the cow was in a graveyard**
**[which Priests may not enter, lest they contract**
**the uncleanness of corpses];**
**or, if the passer-by was old,**
**and chasing cows is beneath his dignity;**
**or, if the cost to the passer-by [of retrieval] is greater than**
**[the value of the cow] to its owner—**
**[in all these cases,] the passer-by**
**is exempt from the rule.**
**This is why the verse states:**
**“You turn a blind eye *to them*” (Dt. 22:1)—**
***sometimes* you turn a blind eye,**
**and *sometimes* you don’t turn a blind eye,**
**[one’s obligation depends upon the facts of the case].**⁷³’, 20 and *Pisqa’* 225.3.

⁷² Cf. Mechilta Ishmael, kaspa’,
⁷³ Cf. Mechilta Ishmael, kaspa


###### Sifrei Devarim 222:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/222:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/222:8)


**הָשֵׁב תְּשִׁיבֵם**, הֶחֱזִירָהּ וּבָרְחָה הֶחֱזִירָהּ וּבָרְחָה, אֲפִלּוּ חָמֵשׁ פְּעָמִים – חַיָּב, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: **הָשֵׁב תְּשִׁיבֵם**; הֶחֱזִירָהּ לְמָקוֹם שֶׁרָאוּהָ אֲחֵרִים, לֹא יִטַּפְּלוּ בָהּ. נִגְנְבָה אוֹ אָבְדָה – חַיָּב בְּאַחֲרָיוּתָהּ. לְעוֹלָם חַיָּב בְּאַחֲרָיוּתָהּ, עַד שֶׁיַּכְנִיסֶנָּה לִרְשׁוּתוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: **הָשֵׁב תְּשִׁיבֵם לְאָחִיךָ**.


5. **“Make every effort to return them” (Dt. 22:1).**
**If he returned the sheep, and she escaped;**
**he returned her again, and again she escaped**
**—even five times!—**
**he is obliged to return her,**
**for it is said:**
**“Make *every effort* to return them to your brother” (Dt. 22:1)—**
**[including multiple efforts].**⁷⁴
**Now, if he returned her to a spot where**
**others could look after her,**
**he needn’t attend her needs any further.**
**But, if she was stolen**
**or lost under his care,**
**he would be obliged to replace her.**
**In fact, the passer-by is obliged**
**to replace the [lost] beast until she**
**actually enters her owner’s property,** ⁷⁵
as it is said:
“Make *every effort* to return them” (Dt. 22:1)—
[until they have in fact been successfully returned].

⁷⁵ //T. BM. 2:23.



## Paragraph 223

###### Sifrei Devarim 223:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/223:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/223:1)


(דברים כב ב) **וְאִם לֹא קָרוֹב אָחִיךָ**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא קָרוֹב. רָחוֹק מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וְלֹא יְדַעְתּוֹ**.


**Pisqa’ 223**⁷⁶
1. “But if your brother *does not* live *near you*” (Dt. 22:2)—
I might infer only that the rule applies
if he *does not* live *nearby.*
How do I know that
it surely applies if he lives far away?
The Teaching states:
“And you don’t *know* him well” (Dt. 22:2)—
[as a result of the distance between you].

footnotes:
⁷⁶ H:234; JN2:132.


###### Sifrei Devarim 223:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/223:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/223:2)


**וַאֲסַפְתּוֹ אֶל תּוֹךְ בֵּיתֶךָ** – וְלֹא לְבַיִת אַחֵר.


2. “Then you shall gather it *into your* household” (Dt. 22:2)—
but *not* into *another* household,
[expecting its residents to care for it].


###### Sifrei Devarim 223:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/223:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/223:3)


**וְהָיָה עִמְּךָ עַד דְּרֹשׁ אָחִיךָ אֹתוֹ**, וְכִי עָלְתָה עַל דַּעְתְּךָ שֶׁאַתָּה נוֹתֵן לוֹ עַד שֶׁלֹּא יִתֵּן סִימָנִים? אִם כֵּן לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר **עַד דְּרֹשׁ אָחִיךָ אֹתוֹ**? עַד שֶׁתִּדְרֹשׁ אֶת אָחִיךָ אִם רַמַּי הוּא אִם אֵינוֹ רַמַּי.


“Where it shall remain with you *until* your brother *inquires* after it” (Dt. 22:2).
Now can you possibly imagine that
you would return it to him
before he specified its markings?
If so, why is it stated:
**“*Until* your brother *inquires* after it” (Dt. 22:2)—**
**[that is, even without specifying its markings.**
**[You needn’t return the animal]**
**until *you inquire* [and confirm] that**
**your brother is not a cheat.** ⁷⁷

footnotes:
⁷⁷ = M. BM. 2:7


###### Sifrei Devarim 223:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/223:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/223:4)


**וַהֲשֵׁבֹתוֹ לוֹ** – אַף אֶת עַצְמוֹ אַתָּה מֵשִׁיב לוֹ!


**“And then *return* it to *him*” (Dt. 22:2)—**
**[Furthermore,] if [your brother] himself is lost,**
**you should guide him home.**⁷⁸

footnotes:
⁷⁸ //T.BM.2:28.



## Paragraph 224

###### Sifrei Devarim 224:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/224:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/224:1)


(דברים כב ג) **וְכֵן תַּעֲשֶׂה לַחֲמוֹרוֹ**, הָיְתָה חֲמוֹר – עוֹשָׂה וְאוֹכֶלֶת;


**Pisqa’ 224**⁷⁹
1. “Thus shall you treat his ass, as well as his *garment*,
as well as any of your brother’s lost property, *which he has lost*” (Dt. 22:3).
**If it was an ass [that he lost],**
**it works [for the finder] and eats [at the finder’s expense].**⁸⁰

footnotes:
⁷⁹ H:234-235;JN2:133.
⁸⁰ Cf. M. BM. 2:7.


###### Sifrei Devarim 224:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/224:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/224:2)


כְּסוּת – מְנַעֲרָהּ אַחַת לִשְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, שׁוֹטְחָהּ לְצָרְכָהּ אֲבָל לֹא לִכְבוֹדוֹ;


**A [simple] cloak—**
**the finder must shake it out once every thirty days.**
**And he may air it out for its own maintenance,**
**but not to enhance his wardrobe.**


###### Sifrei Devarim 224:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/224:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/224:3)


כְּלֵי כֶסֶף וּכְלֵי נְחֹשֶׁת – מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶם לְצָרְכָּם, אֲבָל לֹא לְשָׁחֳקָם;


**Silver or bronze pots—**
**the finder may use them for their own maintenance,**
**but not to wear them out.**


###### Sifrei Devarim 224:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/224:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/224:4)


כְּלֵי עֵץ – מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶם כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יֵרָקְבוּ.


**Wooden utensils—**
**the finder may use them to prevent dry-rot.**⁸¹

footnotes:
⁸¹ =M. BM.2:8.


###### Sifrei Devarim 224:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/224:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/224:5)


אַף הַשִּׂמְלָה הָיְתָה בִּכְלַל כָּל אֵלּוּ, וְלָמָּה יָצָאת? לְהַקִּישׁ אֵלֶיהָ – מָה שִׂמְלָה מְיֻחֶדֶת, שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ סִימָנִים וְיֵשׁ לָהּ תוֹבְעִים – כָּךְ כָּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ סִימָנִים וְיֵשׁ לוֹ תוֹבְעִים. אֵין לִי אֶלָּא אֵלּוּ בִּלְבַד, שְׁאָר אֲבֵדָה מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **לְכָל אֲבֵדַת אָחִיךָ**.


2. Now, a [fine] *garment* should be included
within the category of lost property—
so, why does the verse single it out for special mention?
In order to draw out a comparison
with other lost property!
Just as a [fine] garment is distinctive,
in that it bears unique markings
and has claimants [who can identify them],
so, too, we apply the category of lost property
to any object
that bears unique markings
and has claimants [who can identify them].
Now, I might infer only that
these objects alone—
[i.e., livestock, garments, utensils]—
are included within the rule.
On what basis do I include
other sorts of lost objects
[such as gold and glassware]?⁸²
The Teaching states:
“As well as any of your brother’s *lost* property” (Dt. 22:3).

footnotes:
⁸² Such items are included in the list at M. BM. 2:8.


###### Sifrei Devarim 224:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/224:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/224:6)


**אֲשֶׁר תֹּאבַד מִמֶּנּוּ** – פְּרָט לְפָחוֹת מִשָּׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: **וּמְצָאתָ[הּ]** – לְרַבּוֹת פָּחוֹת מִשָּׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה!


“*which he has lost*” (Dt. 22:3)—
except for an object worth less than a *perutah*.⁸³
R. Judah says:
“And which you have *found*” (Dt. 22:3)—
the rule includes an object worth *even* less than a *perutah!*

⁸³ A copper coin, a “penny.”


###### Sifrei Devarim 224:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/224:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/224:7)


**לֹא תוּכַל לְהִתְעַלֵּם** – לִתֵּן עָלָיו בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.


“You *may not* turn a blind eye” (Dt. 22:3)—
this phrase treats the rule as a proscription.



## Paragraph 225

###### Sifrei Devarim 225:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/225:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/225:1)


(דברים כב ד) **לֹא תִרְאֶה** – מִצְוַת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה; וּלְהַלָּן הוּא אוֹמֵר (שמות כג ה): ״כִּי תִרְאֶה״ – מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה.


**Pisqa’ 225**⁸⁴
1. “You *shall not see* your *brother’s* ox” (Dt. 22:4)—
This is a proscriptive commandment.
Now, elsewhere, he says:
“*When* you see your *rival’s* ass” (Ex. 23:5)—
this is a prescriptive commandment.

footnotes:
⁸⁴ H;235-236;JN2:134:135:


###### Sifrei Devarim 225:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/225:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/225:2)


**חֲמוֹר אָחִיךָ**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא חֲמוֹר אָחִיךָ; חֲמוֹר שׂוֹנַאֲךָ מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (שמות כג ה): ״חֲמוֹר שֹׂנַאֲךָ״ מִכָּל מָקוֹם. אִם כֵּן לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר **אָחִיךָ**? מְלַמֵּד שֶׁלֹּא דִבְּרָה תוֹרָה אֶלָּא כְּנֶגֶד הַיֵּצֶר.


I might infer only that
this rule applies to your *brother’s* ass.
How do I know that it also applies
to your *rival’s* ass?
The Teaching states:
“Your *rival’s* ass” (Ex. 23:5)—
[thus, anyone’s animal is included in the rule].
**If so, why does it specify *your brother*?**
**Actually, it teaches that**
**the point of the Torah is**
**to defeat the rebellious urge**
**[which can even overcome brotherly love]!**⁸⁵ 222.2 on the same theme and in the same words.

footnotes:
⁸⁵ Cf. Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 225:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/225:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/225:3)


**נֹפְלִים** – וְלֹא עוֹמְדִים.


2. “Or his ox has *fallen*” (Dt. 22:4)—
without getting up.


###### Sifrei Devarim 225:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/225:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/225:4)


**בַּדֶּרֶךְ** – וְלֹא בָּרֶפֶת. מִכָּן אָמְרוּ (בבא מציעא פ״ב מ״י): מְצָאָהּ בָּרֶפֶת אֵין חַיָּב בָּהּ, בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים חַיָּב בָּהּ.


“In the *road*” (Dt. 22:4)—
but not in the barn.
On this basis they taught:
**If he found her in the barn,**
**he us under no obligation,**
**But if he found her in the public domain,**
**he is obliged to help her up.**⁸⁶

footnotes:
⁸⁶ //M, BM.2:10.


###### Sifrei Devarim 225:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/225:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/225:5)


**וְהִתְעַלַּמְתָּ** – פְּעָמִים שֶׁאַתָּה מִתְעַלֵּם וּפְעָמִים שֶׁאֵין אַתָּה מִתְעַלֵּם. כֵּיצַד? הָיָה כֹהֵן – וְהֵם בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת; אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה זָקֵן – וְאֵינוֹ לְפִי כְבוֹדוֹ, אוֹ שֶׁהָיְתָה אֲבֵדָה שֶׁלּוֹ מְרֻבָּה מִשֶּׁל חֲבֵרוֹ – פָּטוּר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: **וְהִתְעַלַּמְתָּ**, פְּעָמִים שֶׁאַתָּה מִתְעַלֵּם וּפְעָמִים שֶׁאֵין אַתָּה מִתְעַלֵּם.


3. **“And you turn a *blind eye*” (Dt. 22:4)—**
**Sometimes you *do* turn a blind eye,**
**And sometimes you *don’t* turn a blind eye.**
**For example?**
**If the passer-by is a Priest**
**and the cows are in a graveyard**
**[which Priests may not enter, lest they contract**
**the uncleanness of corpses];**
**or, if the passer-by is old,**
**and chasing cows is beneath his dignity;**
**or, if the cost to the passer-by [of retrieval] is greater than**
**the value of the cow to its owner—**
**the passer-by is exempt from the rule.**
**This is why the verse states:**
**“You turn a *blind eye* to them” (Dt. 22:1)—**
**Sometimes you turn a *blind eye*,**
**And sometimes you don’t turn a *blind eye*,**
**[for your obligation varies with the situation].**⁸⁷ 222.4.

footnotes:
⁸⁷ Cf. M. BM 2:9. Virtually identical with Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 225:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/225:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/225:6)


**הָקֵם תָּקִים עִמּוֹ**, הֶעֱמִידָהּ – וְנָפְלָה, הֶעֱמִידָהּ – וְנָפְלָה, אֲפִלּוּ חָמֵשׁ פְּעָמִים – חַיָּב, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: **הָקֵם תָּקִים עִמּוֹ**. הָלַךְ וְיָשַׁב לוֹ, וְאָמַר לוֹ: הוֹאִיל וְעָלֶיךָ מִצְוָה, אִם רָצִיתָ לְהָקִים – תָּקִים – פָּטוּר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: **הָקֵם תָּקִים עִמּוֹ**. יָכוֹל אֲפִלּוּ זָקֵן, וַאֲפִלּוּ חוֹלֶה, וַאֲפִלּוּ מֻכֵּה שְׁחִין? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **הָקֵם תָּקִים עִמּוֹ**.


4. **“You must labor *with him* to get it *on its feet*” (Dt. 22:4)—**
**If he helped it up, and it fell;**
**he helped it up again, and again it fell**
**—even five times!—**
**he is obliged to help it up again,**
**for it is said:**
**“You must labor *with him* to get it *on its feet*” (Dt. 22:4)—**
**If the owner sat himself down,**
**telling the [helpful passer-by]:**
**Look! This is *your* commandment!**
**If you want to fulfill it, be my guest!—**
**[the passer-by] is relieved of his obligation.**
**For it is said:**
**“You must labor *with him* to get it on its feet” (Dt. 22:4)—**
**[but you needn’t do all the work]!**⁸⁸
Is it possible to say that
even if [the passer-by] is old,
even if he is sick,
or even if he is stricken with boils—
[he is required to assist the owner]?
The Teaching states:
“*You* must labor *with him* to get him on his feet” (Dt. 22:4).

⁸⁸ // M. BM 2:10.



## Paragraph 226

###### Sifrei Devarim 226:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/226:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/226:1)


(דברים כב ה) **לֹא יִהְיֶה כְלִי גֶבֶר עַל אִשָּׁה**, וְכִי מָה בָּא הַכָּתוּב לְלַמְּדֵנוּ, שֶׁלֹּא תִּלְבַּשׁ אִשָּׁה כְּלֵי לְבָנִים וְהָאִישׁ לֹא יִתְכַּסֶּה צִבְעוֹנִים? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **תּוֹעֵבָה**, דָּבָר הַבָּא לִידֵי תּוֹעֵבָה. זֶהוּ כְּלָלוֹ שֶׁל דָּבָר: שֶׁלֹּא תִּלְבַּשׁ אִשָּׁה כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁהָאִישׁ לוֹבֵשׁ וְתֵלֵךְ לְבֵין הָאֲנָשִׁים, וְהָאִישׁ לֹא יִתְקַשֵּׁט בְּתַכְשִׁיטֵי נָשִׁים וְיֵלֵךְ לְבֵין הַנָּשִׁים.


**Pisqa’ 226**⁸⁹
1. “A woman must not don a *man’s gear*;
nor may a man dress-up in *feminine costume*” (Dt. 22:5).
Now, what is the verse coming to teach us—
that a woman should not be dressed in *white* garments,
while a man should not cover himself with *colorful* garments?
[No, for] the Teaching states:
“It is *abominable*” (Dt. 22:5)—
[the reference is to] a matter of habituation to abominable acts.
This is the principle of the matter:
A woman should not be dressed *as a man* dresses,
in order to circulate among men.
And a man should not adorn himself *in feminine adornments*
in order to circulate among women.

footnotes:
⁸⁹ H:236;JN2:136.


###### Sifrei Devarim 226:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/226:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/226:2)


רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא תִלְבַּשׁ אִשָּׁה כְּלִי זַיִן וְתֵצֵא לַמִּלְחָמָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **לֹא יִהְיֶה כְלִי גֶבֶר עַל אִשָּׁה**. וְהָאִישׁ לֹא יִתְקַשֵּׁט בְּתַכְשִׁיטֵי נָשִׁים? – תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וְלֹא יִלְבַּשׁ גֶּבֶר שִׂמְלַת אִשָּׁה**.


2. R. Eliezer b. Jacob says:
On what basis do I know that
a woman should not be garbed in *weapons* and go off to war?
The Teaching states:
“A woman must not don a *man’s gear*” (Dt. 22:5).
And [how do I know] that
a man should not adorn himself in *feminine adornments*?
The Teaching states:
“And a man shall not dress himself in *feminine costume*” (Dt. 22:5).


###### Sifrei Devarim 226:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/226:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/226:3)


**כִּי תוֹעֲבַת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ כָּל עֹשֵׂה אֵלֶּה**, קָרוּי חֲמִשָּׁה שֵׁמוֹת: חֵרֶם, תּוֹעֵבָה, שָׂנאוּי, מְשֻׁקָּץ, וְעַוָּל.


3. **“For *all who do so* are abominable to HASHEM your God.” (Dt. 22:5)—**
**he is called by five epithets:**
**Condemned; Abominated; Hateful; Disgusting; and Perverted.**⁹⁰, per.4:1; cf. *Pisqa’* 148.4.

footnotes:
⁹⁰ // Sifra, qedoshim



## Paragraph 227

###### Sifrei Devarim 227:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/227:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/227:1)


(דברים כב ו) **כִּי יִקָּרֵא** – פְּרָט לַמְזֻמָּן.


**Pisqa’ 227**⁹¹
1. **“If you *happen across* a bird’s nest” (Dt. 22:6)—**
**this excludes from the rule**
**birds that are ready at hand**
**[as opposed to wild birds].**⁹²

footnotes:
⁹¹ H:236-237; JN2:137-138.
⁹² Cf. M. Hul. 12:1.


###### Sifrei Devarim 227:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/227:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/227:2)

**The minimum number intended**
**by the plural, “fledglings” (Dt. 22:6), is two,**

**How do I know that**
**even if there is but one fledgling or one egg,**

**a nest with any number of young**.⁹⁴

## Paragraph 228

###### Sifrei Devarim 228:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/228:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/228:1)


(דברים כב ז) **שַׁלֵּחַ תְּשַׁלַּח** – מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה. שִׁלְּחָהּ וְחָזְרָה, שִׁלְּחָהּ וְחָזְרָה, אֲפִלּוּ חָמֵשׁ פְּעָמִים – חַיָּב לְשַׁלֵּחַ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: **שַׁלֵּחַ תְּשַׁלַּח**.


**Pisqa’ 228**¹⁰³
1. *“You must* definitely *send away* the dam” (Dt. 22:7)—
This is a prescriptive commandment.
**If he sent her away and she returned,**
**and he sent her away and she returned**
**—even five times—**
**is he still under obligation to send her away?** ¹⁰⁴
As it is said:.
“You *must* definitely *send away* the dam” (Dt. 22:7).

footnotes:
¹⁰³ H:237-238; JN2:139.
¹⁰⁴ Cf. M. Hul.12:3.


###### Sifrei Devarim 228:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/228:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/228:2)


הָאַוָּזִים וְתַרְנְגוֹלִים שֶׁמָּרְדוּ וְשֶׁקִּנְּנוּ בַּפַּרְדֵּס – חַיָּב לְשַׁלֵּחַ; בַּבַּיִת – פָּטוּר מִלְּשַׁלֵּחַ.


2. **Ducks or chickens that got loose**
**and nested in an orchard—**
**one is under obligation to send the dam away.**
**If the birds are nesting in the house—**
**he need not send the dam away.**


###### Sifrei Devarim 228:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/228:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/228:3)


(דברים כב ו) **אֶפְרוֹחִים אוֹ בֵיצִים**, מָה אֶפְרוֹחִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּם צוֹרֶךְ – יָצְאוּ מֵתִים שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם צוֹרֶךְ, אַף בֵּיצִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם צוֹרֶךְ – יָצְאוּ בֵּיצִים מוּזָרוֹת שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם צוֹרֶךְ. מִעוּט אֶפְרוֹחִים שְׁנַיִם, מִעוּט בֵּיצִים שְׁנַיִם, וַאֲפִלּוּ אֵין שָׁם אֶלָּא בֵּיצָה אַחַת אוֹ אֶפְרוֹחַ אֶחָד – חַיָּב לְשַׁלֵּחַ. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **כִּי יִקָּרֵא קַן צִפּוֹר לְפָנֶיךָ** מִכָּל מָקוֹם.


**“The fledglings or the eggs” (Dt. 22:6)—**
**fledglings are useful as food.**
**Therefore we exclude from the rule**
**dead fledglings, which are useless.**
**Similarly, eggs are useful as food.**
**Therefore we exclude from the rule**
**abnormal eggs, which are useless.**
**The minimum number intended**
**by the plural, *fledglings*, is two.**
**and the minimum of *eggs* is two.**¹⁰⁵ 227.2.
**Even if there is but one fledgling or one egg,**
**he is obliged to send off the dam.**
3. **Another word:**
**“If you happen across a bird’s nest” (Dt. 22:6)—**
**any place.**

footnotes:
¹⁰⁵ Cf. Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 228:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/228:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/228:4)


**בַּדֶּרֶךְ בְּכָל עֵץ אוֹ עַל הָאָרֶץ**, מַה דֶּרֶךְ רְשׁוּת – יָצְאוּ מְקֻשָּׁרִים שֶׁהֵן בִּרְשׁוּת אַחֵר.


**“*In the path*, in any tree, or upon the ground” (Dt. 22:6)—**
**just as the term, *in the path*,**
**implies that the birds are free-ranging,**
**we exclude from the rule**
**birds that are tied together,**
**for they obviously have limited range.**


###### Sifrei Devarim 228:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/228:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/228:5)


דָּבָר אַחֵר: (דברים כב ז) **שַׁלֵּחַ תְּשַׁלַּח** בִּטְהוֹרָה הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר; אוֹ אַף בִּטְמֵאָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״כָּל צִפּוֹר טְהוֹרָה תֹּאכֵלוּ״ זֶה בִּנְיַן אָב, כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר **צִפּוֹר** – בִּטְהוֹרָה הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר, כְּדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה, הָא אִם שִׁלְּחָהּ וְהֶחְזִיר בַּדֶּרֶךְ אֶת פָּנָיו – פָּטוּר מִלְּשַׁלֵּחַ.


**Another word:**
**“You *must* definitely *send* away the *dam*” (Dt. 22:7)—**
**the verse discusses a *clean* bird.**
**Or, [perhaps,] is it also**
**[discussing] an unclean bird?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“Every *clean* bird shall you eat” (Dt. 14:11).**
**This permits us to recognize**
**a family resemblance among scriptural verses,**¹⁰⁶. A hermeneutical principle whereby usage of a word in a primary context clarifies secondary usages.
**Thus, wherever the term, “bird,” is used**
**[as in Dt. 22:7, where “dam” appears],**
**the verse is referring to the *clean* bird**
**[indicated at Dt. 14:11]—**
**as in the words of R. Josiah.**
**Indeed, if he sent her away and returned to his journey,**
**he is under no obligation to repeatedly send her away.**

footnotes:
¹⁰⁶ Heb: binyan ‘ av


###### Sifrei Devarim 228:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/228:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/228:6)


**שַׁלֵּחַ תְּשַׁלַּח** – בַּנְּקֵבוֹת הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר וְלֹא בַּזְּכָרִים.


**“You must definitely send away the *dam*” (Dt. 22:7)—**
**The verse is discussing females, not males.**¹⁰⁷

footnotes:
¹⁰⁷ The material of 228.2-3 appears to be a condensed reprise of 227.2-4, It is not well-attested in mss and early editions. See F:260, n.3, RH who includes the text in parentheses, and Pardo, ad loc.


###### Sifrei Devarim 228:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/228:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/228:7)


קוֹרֵא זָכָר – רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְחַיֵּב בְּשִׁלּוּחַ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: **שַׁלֵּחַ תְּשַׁלַּח**, וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹטְרִים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: **הָאֵם** – פְּרָט לְקוֹרֵא זָכָר.


4. **Regarding the male partridge,**
**R. Eliezer holds that he is under the rule**
**[and must be sent off before taking the young],**
**for it is said:**
**“You *must* definitely *send away* the *dam*”—**
**[That is, any bird *functioning as* the dam].**
**But sages release him from obligation,**
**as it is said:**
**“The *dam*” (Dt. 22:7)—**
**but not a male partridge.**¹⁰⁸

¹⁰⁸ //M. Hul. 12:2.


###### Sifrei Devarim 228:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/228:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/228:8)


הַנּוֹטֵל אֵם מֵעַל הַבָּנִים, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לוֹקֶה וְאֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּחַ, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים מְשַׁלֵּחַ וְאֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה וְכוּ׳ מַתְנִי׳ עַד מִצְווֹת חֲמוּרוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה.


5. **One who takes the dam from the young—**
**R. Judah says:**
**He receives a judicial beating**
**[for violating the proscription of *sending off the dam*],**
**yet needn’t then send off the dam.**
**But sages say:**
**He must send off the dam,**
**yet does not receive a judicial beating.**
**{This is the general principle:**
**Any proscriptive commandment**
**which entails getting up and acting—**
**they do not administer stripes to the transgressor.** ¹⁰⁹
**A person must not take the dam from the young**
**even to cleanse a victim of Scale-disease.**
**Now, if, regarding a simple commandment—**
**costing at most an *issar***¹¹⁰ (Roman *denarius*).**—**
**the Torah promises:**
**“So that you should be well, and extend your days” (Dt. 22:7),**
**shouldn’t it follow that the same promise applies**
**to any of the Torah’s more arduous commandments?}**¹¹¹

¹⁰⁹ = M. Hul.12:4.
