## Paragraph 229

###### Sifrei Devarim 229:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:1)


(דברים כב ח) **כִּי תִבְנֶה בַּיִת חָדָשׁ**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בּוֹנֶה. לָקַח, יָרַשׁ, וְנִתַּן לוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **בַּיִת**, מִכָּל מָקוֹם.


**Pisqa’ 229**¹¹²
1. “When you *build* a new house” (Dt. 22:8)—
**I might infer only that this rule**
**applies to one who *builds* a house.**
**How do I know that it applies as well to**
**one who buys, one who inherits**
**or one who receives it as a gift?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“A *house*” (Dt. 22:8)—**
**However [you may have acquired it].**¹¹³ 194.1.

footnotes:
¹¹² H:238-240; JN2:140-141.
¹¹³ Cf. Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 229:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:2)


**לֹא תָשִׂים דָּמִים בְּבֵיתֶךָ**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בַּיִת. מִנַּיִן לְבוֹנֶה בֵּית הַתֶּבֶן, בֵּית הַבָּקָר, בֵּית הָעֵצִים, בֵּית הָאוֹצָרוֹת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וְלֹא תָשִׂים דָּמִים בְּבֵיתֶךָ**.


“Do not pour blood on your *house*” (Dt. 22:8)—
**I might infer only that this rule**
**applies specifically to a *residence* (*bayit*).**
**How do I know that it applies as well to**
**a storage shed for straw (*beit hateven),***
**a cattle-barn (*beit habaqar*), a wood-shed (*bet ha`eitzim),***
**or a silo (*bet ha‘otzarot*)*?***
**The Teaching states:**¹¹⁴ 194.1
“Do not pour blood on your *house*” (Dt. 22:8)—
[on whatever is sturdy enough to be called a “house”].

footnotes:
¹¹⁴ Continues Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 229:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:3)


יָכוֹל אַף הַבּוֹנֶה בֵּית שַׁעַר אַכְסַדְרָה וּמִרְפֶּסֶת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **בַּיִת**, מָה בַּיִת מְיֻחָד, שֶׁהוּא בֵּית דִּירָה – יָצְאוּ אֵלּוּ, שֶׁאֵינָם בֵּית דִּירָה.


**Well, is it possible to say that**
**this rule applies as well to one who builds**
**A gate house (*beit sha`ar*),**
**or an open-air portico, or a balcony?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“*House*” (Dt. 22:8)—**
**And just as a house is distinctive,**
**in being a residential space (*bet dirah*),**
**all these other structures are excluded,**
**for they have no residential space**.¹¹⁵

footnotes:
¹¹⁵ Continues to parallel 194.1 as above.


###### Sifrei Devarim 229:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:4)


**וְעָשִׂיתָ מַעֲקֶה לְגַגֶּךָ**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא גַּג. מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת בּוֹרוֹת, שִׁיחִים, וּמְעָרוֹת, חֲרִיצִים וּנְעִיצִים? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וְלֹא תָשִׂים דָּמִים בְּבֵיתֶךָ**. אִם כֵּן לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר **גַּג**? פְּרָט לְכֶבֶשׁ. **בַּיִת** – לְרַבּוֹת הֵיכָל. **גַּג** – פְּרָט לָאוּלָם.


2. “Then you shall build a railing for your *roof*” (Dt. 22:8)—
I might only infer that
this rule applies to the roof.
How do I know that
it includes as well [a requirement] to cordon off
cisterns, pits, cave-springs, crevasses and ditches?
The Teaching states:
“Do not pour blood on *your house*” (Dt. 22:8)—
[or any thing on your property].
If so, why does the verse specify the *roof*?
To exclude from this requirement
the Altar Ramp [which, at ten cubits in height, had no railing].¹¹⁶
And why does the verse specify a *house*? —
This is to include the Sanctuary under this rule.¹¹⁷) is called the Holy Abode (*beit hamiqdash*), i.e., a “house.”
*Roof*—
To exclude the Forecourt [adjacent to the Sanctuary].¹¹⁸

footnotes:
¹¹⁶ So M. Mid. 3:5.
¹¹⁷ So M. Mid.4:6. Thus the Sanctuary (heichal
¹¹⁸ So Mid. 4:7.


###### Sifrei Devarim 229:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:5)


**חָדָשׁ**, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: מִשְּׁעַת חִדּוּשׁוֹ עֲשֵׂה לוֹ מַעֲקֶה. כַּמָּה הוּא מַעֲקֶה? מַעְגִּילוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים, בֵּית דָּרְסוֹ עֲשָׂרָה.


3. “A *new* house” (Dt. 22:8)—
Rabbi says:
while the house is still new, build a railing for it.
Now, what are the dimensions of the railing?
Where the roofers spread pitch,¹¹⁹
the height is a minimum of three handbreadths,
but along the walkway,
the height is at least ten handbreadths.

footnotes:
¹¹⁹ Cf. M. Mak. 2:1..


###### Sifrei Devarim 229:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:6)


**וְעָשִׂיתָ מַעֲקֶה לְגַגֶּךָ** – מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה. **וְלֹא תָשִׂים דָּמִים בְּבֵיתֶךָ** – מִצְוַת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.


“Then you *shall build* a railing for your roof” (Dt. 22:8)—
this is a prescriptive commandment.
“*Do not* pour blood on your house” (Dt. 22:8)—
this is a proscriptive commandment.


###### Sifrei Devarim 229:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:7)


**כִּי יִפֹּל הַנֹּפֵל מִמֶּנּוּ**, רָאוּי זֶה שֶׁיִּפּוֹל! אֶלָּא מְגַלְגְּלִים זְכוּת עַל יְדֵי זַכַּי וְחוֹבָה עַל יְדֵי חַיָּב.


4. **“When the one *prone to falling* indeed falls *from it*” (Dt. 22:8)—**
**this guy must heave deserved a fall!**
**Actually, they ascribe merit**
**according to the deeds of the meritorious,**
**and guilt according to the deeds of the guilty.**¹²⁰

footnotes:
¹²⁰ //T. YK. 5:12. Cf. Sifre Nu., 114.


###### Sifrei Devarim 229:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:8)


**מִמֶּנּוּ** – וְלֹא לְתוֹכוֹ; שֶׁאִם הָיָה רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים גָּבוֹהַּ מִמֶּנּוּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים וְנָפַל מִמֶּנּוּ לְתוֹכוֹ – פָּטוּר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: **מִמֶּנּוּ** וְלֹא לְתוֹכוֹ.


“*From* it” (Dt. 22:8)—
[he fell *from* the roof, *downward* to the ground,]
but not *onto* the roof *from above* it.
For if a public domain was higher
than the roof by ten handbreadths,
and someone fell from there onto the roof—
the householder is exempt
from compensating the victim.
As it is said:
“*From* the roof” (Dt. 22:8)—
but not *onto it* from a space above it.


###### Sifrei Devarim 229:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:9)


דָּבָר אַחֵר: **כִּי תִבְנֶה**, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: בָּא הַכָּתוּב לְלַמֶּדְךָ שֶׁאֵין אָדָם יוֹדֵעַ כֵּיצַד הוּא נִדּוֹן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (קהלת ט יב): ״כִּי לֹא יֵדַע הָאָדָם אֶת עִתּוֹ, כַּדָּגִים שֶׁנֶּאֱחָזִים בִּמְצוֹדָה״.


5. Another word:
“*When* you build a new house” (Dt. 22:8).
R, Ishmael says:
The verse comes to teach you that
A person *never knows* how he will be judged.
As it is said:
“For a man *does not know* his allotted time, like a fish trapped in a net” (Ecc. 9:12).


###### Sifrei Devarim 229:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/229:10)


**בַּיִת** מִכָּן אָמְרוּ: בַּיִת שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַרְבַּע עַל אַרְבַּע – פָּטוּר מִן הַמַּעֲקֶה וּמִן הַמְּזוּזָה וּמִן הָעֵרוּב, וְאֵין עוֹשִׂים אוֹתוֹ עִבּוּר לָעִיר, וְלֹא טִבּוּל לַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, וְאֵין נוֹתְנִים לוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת לְפִתְחוֹ; הַנּוֹדֵר מִן הַבַּיִת מֻתָּר לֵישֵׁב בּוֹ; וְאֵין מִטַּמֵּא בִּנְגָעִים, וְאֵין צָמִית בַּיּוֹבֵל, וְאֵין חוֹזְרִים עָלָיו מֵעֶרְכֵי הַמִּלְחָמָה.


“A house” (Dt. 22:8)—
On this basis they taught:
A house that is not at least four cubits square
is exempt from the roof-railing,
and from the doorpost amulet,¹²¹ See Dt. 6:10.
and from [participation in] the blending of private domains.¹²²; literally, “the mixture of domains” that enables carrying between Jewish households in a shared courtyard on the Sabbath. Cf. M. Eruv.6:1ff.
And they do not use it
[to mark] an expansion of a city’s borders,¹²³
or to impose [upon produce] liability to the Tithe.¹²⁴
And they don’t consider the four cubits of its entrance
[as part of the contained space of the house].
Finally, one disavowing the comforts of home
is permitted to live within
[a house less than four cubits square].
But it does not contract uncleanness from plague-signs,¹²⁵
and it does not revert [to ancestral property] at the Jubilee year.¹²⁶
and warriors may not return to their homes on its account.¹²⁷

footnotes:
¹²¹ Heb: mezuzah.
¹²² Heb: ha`eruv
¹²³ The process of extending a city’s borders from a house beyond the established border is described in M. Eruv. 5:1-5.
¹²⁴ The role of the house or courtyard in establishing obligation to remove the Tithe from produce brought into t hat space is detailed at M. Maas.3:1, 5.
¹²⁵ Plague-signs in homes are discussed at Lv. 14:33ff. and M. Neg. 13:1-3.
¹²⁶ See Lv. 25:13-17.
¹²⁷ The material at 229.5 is lacking in several mss and editions. See F:262, n.5.



## Paragraph 230

###### Sifrei Devarim 230:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:1)


(דברים כב ט) **לֹא תִזְרַע כַּרְמְךָ כִּלְאָיִם**, מָה אֲנִי צָרִיךְ? וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר (ויקרא יט יט) ״שָׂדְךָ לֹא תִזְרַע כִּלְאָיִם״! מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכָּל הַמְקַיֵּם כִּלְאַיִם בַּכֶּרֶם עוֹבֵר בִּשְׁנֵי לָאוִים.


**Pisqa’ 230**¹²⁸
1. “**You *may not* sow your *vineyard* with incompatible species**
**lest you prohibit**¹²⁹ In this context, the root *q-d-sh* has the sense of “taboo” and refers to produce the use of which is forbidden until it is deconsecrated. **the whole” (Dt. 22:9).**
**Do I need to know this?**
**Isn’t it already stated:**
**“Your *field* you *may not* sow**
**with incompatible species” (Lv. 19:19)?**
**[The redundancy] teaches that**
**whoever maintains a vineyard**
**with incompatible species**
**transgresses two proscriptions:**
**[One concerning a *vineyard* (Dt. 22:9)**
**and one concerning a *field* (Lv. 19:19)].**¹³⁰ per. 4:16

footnotes:
¹²⁸ H:240-241; JN2:142-143.
¹²⁹ Heb: tiqdash.
¹³⁰ Cf. Sifra, qedoshim,


###### Sifrei Devarim 230:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:2)


אֵין לִי אֶלָּא כֶּרֶם שָׁלֵם. מִנַּיִן אֲפִלּוּ גֶּפֶן יְחִידִי וְעוֹשֶׂה פֵּרוֹת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר **כֶּרֶם**, מִכָּל מָקוֹם.


2. Now, I might infer only that
this rule applies when the *entire* vineyard is sown
with incompatible species!
**But, how do I know that**
**[the prohibition applies to]**
**even a *single* fruit-bearing vine**
**[sown, say, in a wheat field]?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“A *vineyard*” (Dt. 22:9)—**
**[containing] any number [of vines].**¹³¹

footnotes:
¹³¹ Cf. M. Kil. 4:6.


###### Sifrei Devarim 230:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:3)


מִנַּיִן לְכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם שֶׁאֲסוּרִים בַּהֲנָיָה? נֶאֱמַר כָּאן **תִּקְדַּשׁ**, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן (ויקרא ה טו) ״קֹדֶשׁ״ – מָה קֹדֶשׁ הָאָמוּר לְהַלָּן אָסוּר בַּהֲנָיָה, אַף קֹדֶשׁ הָאָמוּר כָּאן אָסוּר בַּהֲנָיָה.


How, furthermore, do I know that
grapes of a vineyard sown with incompatible species
are prohibited for benefit?
The term, *prohibited*, appears here (Dt. 22:9),
and the term, *prohibited,* appears elsewhere (Lv. 5:15).
Just as [the grapes] *prohibited* elsewhere
are forbidden for benefit,
do, too, [the grapes] *prohibited* here
are [prohibited] for benefit.


###### Sifrei Devarim 230:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:4)


**פֶּן תִּקְדַּשׁ הַמְלֵאָה הַזֶּרַע**, מֵאֵימָתַי הַמְלֵאָה הַזֶּרַע מִתְקַדֶּשֶׁת? – מִשֶּׁתַּשְׁרִישׁ, וַעֲנָבִים? – מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשׂוּ כְּפוֹל לָבָן.


3. **“Lest you prohibit *the whole* of the seed you have sown” (Dt. 22:9).**
**At what point [in its growth] is**
***the whole* of the seed prohibited? When it strikes root.**
**[This criterion holds for grain or greens,]**
**but as for grapes—**
**when they are the size of white beans.**¹³²

footnotes:
¹³² = M. Kil.7:7.


###### Sifrei Devarim 230:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:5)


**הַזֶּרַע** – פְּרָט לְזֶרַע שֶׁיָּצָא עִם הַזְּבָלִים אוֹ עִם הַמַּיִם, הַזּוֹרֵעַ וְהָרוּחַ מְסַעַרְתּוֹ. יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מוֹצִיא הַזּוֹרֵעַ וְהָרוּחַ מְסַיַּעְתּוֹ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **אֲשֶׁר תִּזְרָע**.


“*Of* the seed” (Dt. 22:9)—
excluding from the rule seed [sown inadvertently]
in manure or by watering the field.
**If one was sowing seed [in one field],**
**and it was blown down-wind [to another]—**
**[what is the application of the rule]?** ¹³³
Is it possible for me to exempt from the rule
the case of one who was sowing seed,
and it was blown down-wind?
The Teaching states:
“Of the seed *you* have sown” (Dt. 22:9)—
[The rule is limited to fields intentionally sown
in violation of the rule].

footnotes:
¹³³ Cf. M. Kil. 5:7.


###### Sifrei Devarim 230:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:6)


הַמְקַיֵּם קוֹצִים בַּכֶּרֶם, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: קָדַשׁ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר **אֲשֶׁר תִּזְרָע**, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: **זֶרַע** פְּרָט לַמְקַיֵּם קוֹצִים בַּכֶּרֶם.


**As for one who maintains thorns in a vineyard—**
**R. Eliezer says:**
**He has placed it under prohibition,**
**for it is said:**
**“Of the *seed* you have *sown*” (Dt. 22:9)—**
**[and maintaining the thorns is like sowing them].**
**But sages say:**
**“Of the seed you *have sown*” (Dt. 22:9)—**
**this excludes the case of**
**one who maintains thorns in a vineyard**
**[since the thorns are neither seed nor are they sown].** ¹³⁴

footnotes:
¹³⁴ // M. Kil. 5:8.


###### Sifrei Devarim 230:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:7)


**וּתְבוּאַת הַכָּרֶם**, מֵאֵימָתַי הַתְּבוּאָה מִתְקַדֶּשֶׁת? מִשֶּׁתַּשְׁרִישׁ, וַעֲנָבִים מִשֶּׁיַּעֲלוּ כְּפוֹל לָבָן.


4. **“Lest you prohibit the whole of the seed you have sown, *and the yield*” (Dt. 22:9).**
**At what point in its growth is *the yield* prohibited? When it strikes root.**
**[This holds for grain and greens,]**
**But as for grapes—**
**When they are the size of white beans**.¹³⁵ 230.3.

footnotes:
¹³⁵ = M. Kil. 7:7 and Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 230:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:8)


אֵין לִי אֶלָּא כֶּרֶם שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה פֵּרוֹת, כֶּרֶם שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה פֵּרוֹת מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **כֶּרֶם**, מִכָּל מָקוֹם. אֵין לִי אֶלָּא כֶּרֶם שֶׁלְּךָ, כֶּרֶם שֶׁל אֲחֵרִים מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **לֹא תִזְרַע כַּרְמְךָ כִּלְאָיִם**, מִכָּל מָקוֹם.


I might infer that
the rule only applies to a vineyard that is actually productive.
How do I know that it may also apply
to a vineyard that is barren?
The Teaching states:
“A *vineyard*” (Dt. 22:9)—
of any sort.
I might infer that
the rule only applies to your *own* [Israelite] field.
How do I know that it may also apply
to fields owned by [gentile] others?
The Teaching states:
“You *may not sow* . . . with incompatible species’ (Dt. 22:9)—
in *any* [field, owned by anyone].


###### Sifrei Devarim 230:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:9)


הַמּוֹתֵחַ זְמוֹרָה שֶׁל גֶּפֶן עַל גַּבֵּי זְרָעִים, אֲפִלּוּ מֵאָה אַמָּה – הַגֶּפֶן אֲסוּרָה וּפֵירוֹתֶיהָ.


**One who extends the tendril of a grape vine**
**over seed of an incompatible species—**
**even [if the extension covers] a distance of a hundred cubits—**
**the vine and its fruit are prohibited under the rule**.¹³⁶

###### Sifrei Devarim 230:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:10)


[(דברים כב י) **לֹא תַחֲרֹשׁ בְּשׁוֹר וַחֲמֹר** –] יָכוֹל לֹא יַחֲרֹשׁ עַל זֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, וְעַל זֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **יַחְדָּו**. אֲבָל זֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וְזֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ – מֻתָּר.


5. “You may not plow with an ox and an ass *as one*” (Dt. 22:10)—
is it possible to say that
you can’t plow with *this one* on its own,
and then with *that one* on its own?
The Teaching states:
“As *one*” (Dt. 22:10)—
however, plowing with *this one* on its own,
and then with *that one* on its own is permitted.


###### Sifrei Devarim 230:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:11)


דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״כִּלְאַיִם״ – לְחַיֵּב מִשּׁוּם כֶּרֶם וּמִשּׁוּם שָׂדֶה.


Another word:
“Incompatible *species*” (Dt. 22:9)—
[*species* implies a minimum of two].
This places a vineyard under the rule
as well as a field [of wheat or greens].


###### Sifrei Devarim 230:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:12)


דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״פֶּן תִּקְדַּשׁ הַמְלֵאָה״ – פֶּן תֵּאָסֵר הַמְלֵאָה, כְּדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה.


Another word:
“Lest you *prohibit* the whole of the seed you have sown” (Dt. 22:9)—
lest you impose a prohibition *upon all* of it:
As was explained by R. Josiah.


###### Sifrei Devarim 230:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/230:13)


**אֲשֶׁר תִּזְרַע**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁזָּרַע הוּא. זָרַע חֲבֵירוֹ וְרָצָה לְקַיְּמוֹ מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **תִּזְרַע**, מִכָּל מָקוֹם.


6. “Of the seed *you* have sown” (Dt. 22:9)—
I might assume that the rule only applies
to seed *sown by him*.
How do I know that
the rule applies as well where his *companion* has done the sowing,
but the *owner* of the field desires to maintain it?
The Teaching states:
“*You* have sown” (Dt. 22:9)—
by anyone, [acceptable to both parties].¹³⁷

## Paragraph 231

###### Sifrei Devarim 231:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/231:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/231:1)


(דברים כב י) **לֹא תַחֲרֹשׁ בְּשׁוֹר וַחֲמוֹר יַחְדָּו**, יָכוֹל לְעוֹלָם? כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר (שמות כג יב) ״לְמַעַן יָנוּחַ שׁוֹרְךָ וַחֲמֹרֶךָ״ – כְּבָר שׁוֹר וַחֲמוֹר עוֹשִׂים מְלָאכָה! אִם כֵּן לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר **לֹא תַחֲרֹשׁ בְּשׁוֹר וַחֲמוֹר**? זֶה עִם זֶה. שׁוֹר וַחֲמוֹר, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שׁוֹר וַחֲמוֹר; מִנַּיִן לַעֲשׂוֹת שְׁאָר בְּהֵמָה וְחַיָּה וָעוֹף כְּיוֹצֵא בְּשׁוֹר וַחֲמוֹר? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **לֹא תַחֲרֹשׁ**, מִכָּל מָקוֹם. אִם כֵּן לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר **בְּשׁוֹר וַחֲמוֹר**? – בְּשׁוֹר וַחֲמוֹר אִי אַתָּה חוֹרֵשׁ, אֲבָל אַתָּה חוֹרֵשׁ בְּאָדָם וּבַחֲמוֹר!


**Pisqa’ 231**¹³⁸
1. “You *may not* plow with an ox and an ass as one” (Dt. 22:10)—
is it possible to say that this means “never?”
Yet, when he says:
“So that your ox and ass *may rest*” (Ex. 23:12),
[it seems that] the ox and ass
have already been worked [together]!
If so, why is it stated:
“You may not plow with an ox and an ass *as one*” (Dt. 22:10)—
that is, [yoked together] side by side.2. “An *ox* and an *ass*” (Dt. 22:10)—
I might infer only that
[the rule applies to] *an ox and an ass*.
**How do I know to treat**
**other cattle, wild animals, and fowl**
**in the same way as the ox and the ass?** ¹³⁹
The Teaching states:
“You may *not plow*” (Dt. 22:10)—
With any [combination of
incompatible work-animals]
If so, why does the verse specify:
“With an ox and an ass” (Dt. 22:10)?
**You may not plow with**
***an ox* and an ass [as one],**
**But you may certainly plow with**
***a man* and an ass!**¹⁴⁰

footnotes:
¹³⁸ H:241; JN2:144-145.
¹³⁹ Cf. M. Kil. 8:2.
¹⁴⁰ Cf. M. Kil.8:6.


###### Sifrei Devarim 231:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/231:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/231:2)


**לֹא תַחֲרֹשׁ**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא חוֹרֵשׁ; מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת הַדָּשׁ וְהַיּוֹשֵׁב וְהַמַּנְהִיג? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **יַחְדָּו**, מִכָּל מָקוֹם. רַבִּי מֵאִיר פּוֹטֵר בַּיּוֹשֵׁב.


3. “You may not *plow*” (Dt. 22:9)—
I might infer only that
*plowing* is covered by the rule.
How do I know to include
one threshing grain,
or sitting [in a wagon]¹⁴¹ and driving a team?
The Teaching states:
“As *one*” (Dt. 22:9)—
[this refers to] any labor
[associated with the animal’s work].
R. Meir exempts from the rule
the one sitting [in a wagon].

¹⁴¹ RH adds the clause, “in a wagon.”


###### Sifrei Devarim 231:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/231:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/231:3)


**יַחְדָּו** – פְּרָט לְרָמָךְ. **יַחְדָּו** – פְּרָט לְקוֹשֵׁר אֶת הַסּוּס לְצִדֵּי הַקָּרוֹן אוֹ לְאַחַר הַקָּרוֹן, וְאֶת הַלַּבְדְּקָס לַגְּמַלִּים.


“An ox and an *ass* as one” (Dt. 22:9)—
this excludes the *mule*.
“An *ox* and an *ass* as one” (Dt. 22:9)—
**this excludes**
**one who ties his horse**
**to the side of a wagon**
**or behind a wagon [pulled by an ox],**
**and a Libyan ass,**
**[pulling a load] with camels**.¹⁴²

## Paragraph 232

###### Sifrei Devarim 232:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/232:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/232:1)


(דברים כב יא) **לֹא תִלְבַּשׁ שַׁעַטְנֵז**, יָכוֹל לֹא יִלְבַּשׁ גִּיזֵּי צֶמֶר וַאֲנִיצֵי פִשְׁתָּן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **שַׁעַטְנֵז**, דָּבָר שֶׁשּׁוּעַ טָווּי וְנוּז. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: נָלוֹז וּמֵלִיז הוּא אֶת אָבִיו שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם עָלָיו.


**Pisqa’ 232**¹⁴³
*1*
**“Do not wear wool and linen fibers mingled**¹⁴⁴ **as one”(Dt. 22:11)—**
**is it possible to say that**
**[the prohibition includes] shorn wool and linen shreds**
**[that have yet to be woven together]?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“Fibers *mingled*” (Dt. 22:11)—**¹⁴⁵ per.4:18.
**this specifies any garment which is**
**combed (*shu`a*), spun (*tavui*), and woven (*nuz*).**¹⁴⁶) of other words or phrases.
**R. Shimon b. Elazar says:**
**[“Mingled”-wearers] are twisted,**¹⁴⁷ Note the word play with *nuz,* “woven.”.
**forcing their Heavenly Father**
**to deal with them in a twisted way.**¹⁴⁸ per.4:18.

footnotes:
¹⁴³ H:241-242;JN2:232.
¹⁴⁴ Heb: sh`atnez.
¹⁴⁵ =Sifra, qedoshim,
¹⁴⁶ This is an example of a derivation of the meaning of one word from the initial letters (notarikon
¹⁴⁷ Heb: naluz.
¹⁴⁸ //M. Kil.9:8;. Sifra, qedoshim,


###### Sifrei Devarim 232:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/232:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/232:2)


**לֹא תִלְבַּשׁ**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא יִלְבַּשׁ; מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא יִתְכַּסֶּה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (ויקרא יט יט): ״לֹא יַעֲלֶה עָלֶיךָ״. יָכוֹל לֹא יַפְשִׁילֶנּוּ בְּקוּפָּה לְאַחֲרָיו? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **לֹא תִלְבַּשׁ**, לְבִישָׁה בִּכְלָל הָיְתָה, וְלָמָּה יָצָאת? לְהַקִּישׁ אֵלֶיהָ וְלוֹמַר לְךָ: מַה לְּבִישָׁה מְיֻחֶדֶת, שֶׁהִיא הֲנָיַת הַגּוּף – אַף כָּל שֶׁהוּא הֲנָיַת הַגּוּף.


2. “Do not *wear*” (Dt. 22:11)—
I might infer only that
you shouldn’t *wear* [mingled garments].
How do I know that the rule applies as well
to merely *covering up* with them?
The Teaching states:
“And a garment of mingled incompatible fibers shall *not be placed upon* you” (Lv. 19:19)—
[even placing them on the body is forbidden].
Is it possible to say that
he may not *strap* a pack
of such garments on his back?
The Teaching states:
“Do not *wear*” (Dt. 22:11)—
[and *carrying* is distinct from *wearing*].
Now, *wearing* should have been included
in the general statement of the rule.
Why, then, is it singled out for emphasis?
In order to make a comparative observation
and inform you that
just as *wearing* is distinctive,
in that it benefits the body,
only [a mingled fabric] that benefits the body,
[is considered to be worn as a garment].


###### Sifrei Devarim 232:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/232:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/232:3)


**יַחְדָּו**, יָכוֹל לֹא יִלְבַּשׁ חָלוּק שֶׁל צֶמֶר עַל גַּבֵּי חָלוּק שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן וְחָלוּק שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן עַל גַּבֵּי חָלוּק שֶׁל צֶמֶר? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **יַחְדָּו**.


3. “As *one*” (Dt. 22:11)—
is it possible to say that
one should not wear
a wool shirt over a linen shirt,
or a linen shirt over a wool shirt?
The Teaching states:
“As *one*” (Dt. 22:11)—
[the rule applies only to *one* garment
woven of two mingled threads].


###### Sifrei Devarim 232:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/232:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/232:4)


רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא יִקְשֹׁר סֶרֶט שֶׁל צֶמֶר בְּשֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן, לַחְגּוֹר בּוֹ אֶת מָתְנָיו, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָרְצוּעָה בָּאֶמְצַע? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **יַחְדָּו**, מִכָּל מָקוֹם. כְּשֶׁתִּמְצָא אוֹמֵר: הַשַּׂק וְהַקֻּפָּה מְצָרְפִים אֶת הַכִּלְאַיִם.


**R. Hananiah b. Gamliel says**:
How do I know that
**one shouldn’t knot a strip of wool fabric**
**to one of linen fabric**
**and tie it around his waist,**
**even though a leather strap interposes?**¹⁴⁹
The Teaching states:
“As *one*” (Dt. 22:11)—
any arrangement
[of the fabrics into a single article stands under the rule].
**Thus you can argue that**
**sack-cloth [containing wool]**
**and a basket [containing linen]**
**combine [when bound together]**
**to produce an incompatible mixture**
**[that may not be carried on the shoulders].**¹⁵⁰

footnotes:
¹⁴⁹ //T. Kil. 5:22.
¹⁵⁰ // M. Kil.9:10.


###### Sifrei Devarim 232:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/232:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/232:5)


**צֶמֶר וּפִשְׁתִּים יַחְדָּו**, אֲבָל זֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וְזֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ מֻתָּר. הַלְּבָדִים אֲסוּרִים מִשּׁוּם כִּלְאַיִם; אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם מִשּׁוּם אָרִיג, יֵשׁ בָּהֶם מִשּׁוּם שׁוּעַ.


**“Wool and linen fibers mingled as one” (Dt. 22:11)—**
**but a garment of either one on its own is permitted**
**[to be worn with a garment of the other fabric].**
**Articles of felt are prohibited**
**as incompatible mixtures,**
**for even though they are**
**not weaves of woolen thread,**
**they are combed-wool mattings**
**[That may contain fibers of linen]**.¹⁵¹

¹⁵¹ //M. Kil.9:9. This material is missing in several source. See F:265, n. 11.



## Paragraph 233

###### Sifrei Devarim 233:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/233:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/233:1)


(דברים כב יא-יב) **לֹא תִלְבַּשׁ שַׁעַטְנֵז... גְּדִלִים תַּעֲשֶׂה לָּךְ** – שְׁנֵיהֶם נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּדִבּוּר אֶחָד. (שמות כ ח) ״זָכוֹר״ (דברים ה יב) וְ״שָׁמוֹר״ – שְׁנֵיהֶם נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּדִבּוּר אֶחָד.


**Pisqa’ 233**¹⁵²
1. “Do not wear garments of wool and linen fibers *mingled as one* . . .
*Tassels* shall you make for yourself” (Dt. 22:11-12)—
[If one may not mingle fibers how can one make tassels]?
Both of these commandments were given in a single utterance.
**[So, too,] “*Remember* the Sabbath Day” (Ex. 20:8)**
**and “*Preserve* the Sabbath Day” (Dt. 5:12)**
**were both given in a single utterance.**¹⁵³ 7.

(שמות לא יד) ״מְחַלְלֶיהָ מוֹת יוּמָת״, (במדבר כח ט) ״וּבְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת שְׁנֵי כְבָשִׂים בְּנֵי שָׁנָה״ – שְׁנֵיהֶם נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּדִבּוּר אֶחָד.


“Who *defiles it* will quickly be put to death” (Ex. 31:14) and “On *the Sabbath Day*, two yearling lambs” (Nu. 28:9)
were both given in a single utterance.

מַה שֶּׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְבָשָׂר וָדָם לוֹמַר שְׁנֵי דְבָרִים כְּאַחַת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (תהלים סב יב): ״אַחַת דִּבֶּר אֱלֹהִים, שְׁתַּיִם זוּ שָׁמָעְנוּ״.


[Now this proves that the Torah is from Heaven,]
for it is clearly impossible for flesh and blood
to say two things with a single utterance.

## Paragraph 234

###### Sifrei Devarim 234:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/234:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/234:1)


(דברים כב יב) **גְּדִלִים תַּעֲשֶׂה לָּךְ**, לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר? לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (במדבר טו לח) ״וְעָשׂוּ לָהֶם צִיצִית״, שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי: יַעֲשֶׂה חוּט אֶחָד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **גְּדִלִים**.


**Pisqa’ 234**¹⁵⁶
*1*
**“*Tassels***¹⁵⁷ **shall you make for yourself” (Dt. 22:12).**
**Why must this be stated?**
**Because it is also stated:**
**“They shall make for themselves *fringes*”**¹⁵⁸ **(Nu,15:38).**
**Now, do I understand from this that**
**a person should prepare one *thread***¹⁵⁹. The distinctions between a *khut, tzitzit,* and *gedilim* are unclear. **on its own?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“Tassels” (Dt. 22:12)—**
**[Thus, more than one must be made].**

footnotes:
¹⁵⁶ H:243; JN2:149-150
¹⁵⁷ Heb: gedilim.
¹⁵⁸ Heb: tzitzit.
¹⁵⁹ Heb: khut


###### Sifrei Devarim 234:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/234:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/234:2)


כַּמָּה **גְדִלִים** נַעֲשִׂים? אֵין פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה חוּטִים, כְּדִבְרֵי בֵית הִלֵּל. בֵּית שַׁמַּיי אוֹמְרִים: מֵאַרְבָּעָה חוּטִים שֶׁל תְּכֵלֶת וְאַרְבָּעָה חוּטִים שֶׁל לָבָן, שֶׁל אַרְבַּע אַרְבַּע אֶצְבָּעוֹת.


**So how many tassels should be made?**
**No fewer than three threads [per tassel]:**
**According to the words of the circle of Hillel.**
**The circle of Shammai, however, say:**
**At least four threads of azure**¹⁶⁰ a dye extracted from a type of snail (*khilazon*).
**and four threads of white—**
**also, they should each be four fingers long.**

¹⁶⁰ Heb: techeilet,

וַהֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּיי. בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? בַּתְּחִלָּה; אֲבָל בִּשְׁיָרֶיהָ וּבְגַרְדוּמֶּיהָ – כָּל שֶׁהוּא.


**And the customary practice [concerning length]**
**conforms to the words of the circle of Shammai.**
**Now, under what circumstances?**
**When [the tassel] is first made.**
**But its remnants and shreds are**
**suitable at any length.**


###### Sifrei Devarim 234:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/234:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/234:4)


**עַל אַרְבַּע** – יָצְאוּ בַּעֲלֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה וּבַעֲלֵי חָמֵשׁ וּבַעַל שֵׁשׁ וּבַעַל שֶׁבַע וּבַעֲלֵי שְׁמוֹנֶה. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **גְּדִלִים תַּעֲשֶׂה לָּךְ** – זֶה לָבָן. מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַתְּכֵלֶת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (במדבר טו לח): ״וְנָתְנוּ עַל צִיצִת הַכָּנָף פְּתִיל תְּכֵלֶת״.


**“On the four corners” (Dt. 22:12)—**
**This excludes from the rule**
**garments of three, five, six, seven, or eight corners**.¹⁶¹
**Another word:**
“*Tassels* shall you make for yourself” (Dt. 22:12)—
This refers to those of white.
How do I know that
it includes as well those of azure?
The Teaching states:
“And tie, in addition to the fringed corner, a strand of azure” (Nu. 15:38).

**תַּעֲשֶׂה** – וְלֹא מִן הֶעָשׂוּי, שֶׁלֹּא יוֹצִיא נִימִים מִן הַטַּלִּית וְיַעֲשֶׂה. **עַל אַרְבַּע** – וְלֹא עַל שְׁמוֹנֶה. **כְּסוּתְךָ** – פְּרָט לְטָגָא, וּלְתוֹבְלָא, וּלְתִיבְלָטִירִים, לְתַקְרָקִים לְבוּרְסִים לְבוּרְדְּסִים, לְפִי שֶׁאֵינָם מְרֻבָּעִים. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא יִתֵּן עַל אֶמְצַע בֶּגֶד, אֶלָּא עַל שְׂפָתוֹ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **עַל אַרְבַּע כַּנְפוֹת**.


2. “You shall *make*” (Dt. 22:12)—
but not from a ready-made article.
So that you won’t [be tempted to] extract
loose-threads from a cloak and
*make* them [into tassels].
“On the *four* corners” (Dt. 22:12)—
but not on *eight* of them!
“Of your *garment*” (Dt. 22:12)—
this excludes from the rule:
**A *toga*, a *tebenna*, a *fivlaterion*, a *nerbixa,***
**a *birrus,* and a Burdisian cloak,**
**none of which is square**.¹⁶² 234, see H: 243 and p. 471, *Pisqa’* 234, ns. 3-10.
3. R. Eliezer b. Jacob says:
How do I know that tassels are not placed
In the middle of a garment, but on the *hem*?
The Teaching states:
“On the four *corners*” (Dt. 22:12).

**כְּסוּתְךָ** – פְּרָט לְכַר; **כְּסוּתְךָ** – פְּרָט לְסָדִין. **תְּכַסֶּה** – פְּרָט לְסָגוֹס.

with the exception of a pillow-case.

## Paragraph 235

###### Sifrei Devarim 235:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/235:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/235:1)


(דברים כב יג) **כִּי יִקַּח אִישׁ אִשָּׁה וּבָא עָלֶיהָ וּשְׂנֵאָהּ**, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם בָּא עָלֶיהָ – לוֹקֶה, וְאִם לָאו – אֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה.


**Pisqa’ 235**¹⁶³
1. “Should a man take a wife, *consort* with her, and *come* to *hate* her” (Dt. 22:13)
R. Judah says:
If he *still* consorts with her [after coming to hate her],
he should receive a [judicially administered] beating!
But if not, he doesn’t receive a [judicially administered] beating.

footnotes:
¹⁶³ H:243-245; JN2:151-153.


###### Sifrei Devarim 235:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/235:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/235:2)


**וּשְׂנֵאָהּ**, מִכָּן אַתָּה אוֹמֵר: עָבַר אָדָם עַל מִצְוָה קַלָּה – סוֹפוֹ לַעֲבוֹר עַל מִצְוָה חֲמוּרָה. עָבַר עַל (ויקרא יט יח) ״וְאָהַבְתָּ לְרֵעֲךָ כָּמוֹךָ״ – סוֹפוֹ לַעֲבוֹר עַל ״לֹא תִקֹּם וְלֹא תִטֹּר״ וְעַל (ויקרא יט יז) ״לֹא תִשְׂנָא אֶת אָחִיךָ בִּלְבָבֶךָ״ וְעַל ״וְאָהַבְתָּ לְרֵעֲךָ כָּמוֹךָ״ וְעַל (ויקרא כה לו) ״וְחֵי אָחִיךָ עִמָּךְ״, עַד שֶׁבָּא לִידֵי שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים. לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר **כִּי יִקַּח אִישׁ אִשָּׁה**.


2. “And come to *hate her*” (Dt. 22:13)—
on this basis you can teach:
If a person transgresses
a simple commandment,
he will in the end transgress
an arduous commandment.
If he transgresses:
“Love your kinsman as yourself”(Lv. 19:18),
he will in the end transgress others, such as:
“Don’t seek vengeance and don’t harbor a grudge” (Lv. 19:18).
And then he’ll transgress:
“Don’t hate your brother in your heart” (Lv. 19:17).
And then: ¹⁶⁴
“So that your brother may thrive with you” (Lv. 25:36)—
until he ultimately spills innocent blood.
This is why it is stated:
“Should a man take a wife. . . and *come* to hate her” (Dt. 22:13).

footnotes:
¹⁶⁴ At this point, F:267, l.8 repeats the citation of Lv. 19:18. TA brackets the quotation, which is also lacking in mss Vatican and others.


###### Sifrei Devarim 235:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/235:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/235:3)


(דברים כב יד) **וְשָׂם לָהּ עֲלִילוֹת דְּבָרִים**, יָכוֹל אֲפִלּוּ אָמַר לָהּ הִקְדַּחְתְּ הַתַּבְשִׁיל וְהִיא לֹא הִקְדִּיחָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **עֲלִילוֹת דְּבָרִים**, (דברים כב יז) ״עֲלִילוֹת דְּבָרִים״ – לִגְזֵרָה שָׁוָה. מָה עֲלִילוֹת דְּבָרִים הָאָמוּר לְהַלָּן – טַעֲנַת בְּתוּלִים, אַף עֲלִילוֹת דְּבָרִים הָאָמוּר כָּאן – טַעֲנַת בְּתוּלִים. אִי מָה עֲלִילוֹת דְּבָרִים הָאָמוּר לְהַלָּן – מְקוֹם בְּתוּלִים, אַף עֲלִילוֹת דְּבָרִים הָאָמוּר כָּאן – מְקוֹם בְּתוּלִים, מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת בִּיאָה אַחֶרֶת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וְהוֹצִיא עָלֶיהָ שֵׁם רָע**.


3. “And then he will level *scandalous charges* against her” (Dt. 22:13)—
is it possible to say that
[his complaint is considered]
even if he charges:
You burned supper!—
when she hadn’t burned it?
The Teaching mentions [first]:
*scandalous charges* (Dt. 22:14),
and, a second time: *scandalous charges* (Dt. 22:17).
This enables us to draw an
analogy from similar Scriptural terms.
Just as the *scandalous charges*
noted elsewhere (Dt. 22:17)
concern a claim against her hymen,¹⁶⁵ That is, a claim that the hymen is not intact due to sexual relations.
so, too, the scandalous charges noted here (Dt. 22:14)
[must concern a claim against her hymen].
Or, perhaps:
Just as the *scandalous charges* noted elsewhere (Dt. 22:17),
concern the *place* [covered by] the hymen,¹⁶⁶. The vaginal canal. Where the hymen is intact, the claimant may resort to the charge that the bride has had anal intercourse.
So, too, the “scandalous charge” noted here (Dt. 22:14),
must concern the *place* [covered by] the hymen.
How do I know that
we include a charge of anal penetration¹⁶⁷ literally, “unconventional intercourse.”
[that nevertheless leaves the hymen intact]?
The Teaching states:
“And he brought her into *disrepute*” (Dt. 22:14).

footnotes:
¹⁶⁵ Heb.: ta`anat betulim.
¹⁶⁶ Heb.: maqom betulim
¹⁶⁷ Heb: bi’ah ‘akheret;


###### Sifrei Devarim 235:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/235:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/235:4)


**וְאָמַר אֶת הָאִשָּׁה הַזֹּאת** – מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאֵין אוֹמֵר דְּבָרָיו אֶלָּא בַּעֲמִידָתָהּ.


“By saying: *this* woman” (Dt. 22:14)—
*this* teaches that
he lays his charge before her
only while she stands in his presence.


###### Sifrei Devarim 235:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/235:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/235:5)


**לָקַחְתִּי וָאֶקְרַב אֵלֶיהָ וְלֹא מָצָאתִי לָהּ בְּתוּלִים** – הֲרֵי עֵדִים שֶׁזִּינְּתָה בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ!


4. “This woman I took, and . . . *I found no* signs of her *maidenhood*!”(Dt. 22:14)—
test-cloths¹⁶⁸ literally, “witnesses.” In this context the reference is to cloths used to detect the presence of blood associated with vaginal penetration. See M. Nid. 1:7. showed that she had

###### Sifrei Devarim 235:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/235:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/235:6)


**כִּי יִקַּח אִישׁ אִשָּׁה**, לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר? לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ויקרא כ י) ״אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִנְאַף אֶת אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ״, אַחַת שֶׁבָּאוּ לָהּ עֵדִים בְּבֵית בַּעְלָהּ שֶׁזִּנְּתָה בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ וְאַחַת שֶׁבָּאוּ לָהּ עֵדִים בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ שֶׁזִּנְּתָה בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ, מַשְׁמַע שֶׁתְּהֵא נִדּוֹנֵת עַל שַׁעַר הָעִיר? וַהֲרֵי הַכָּתוּב מוֹצִיא אֶת שֶׁבָּאוּ לָהּ עֵדִים בְּבֵית בַּעְלָהּ שֶׁזִּנְּתָה בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ שֶׁתְּהֵא נִדּוֹנֵת עַל פֶּתַח בֵּית אָבִיהָ! לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר **כִּי יִקַּח אִישׁ אִשָּׁה**.


“Should a man *take a wife*, *consort* with her, and come to *hate* her” (Dt. 22:13)—
Why is this stated?
Because it is stated:
“The man who *despoils* a married woman” (Lv. 20:10).
[The two verses together cover the entire range of possibilities.]
It’s all the same whether witnesses came
*from* her *husband’s* house
[where she now lives in marriage],
to claim that she fornicated in her *father’s* house,
[and there is reason to suspect her
in her husband’s house as well (i.e., Dt. 22:14)].
Or :
If witnesses came *from* her *father’s* house
[where she lived prior to her marriage],
to claim that she fornicated in her *father’s* house,
[and there is reason to suspect her
in her husband’s house as well (i.e., Lv. 20:10)].
This suggests that
[either way] she is judged at the gate of the city.
But, indeed—
the verse excludes from the rule a case in which
witnesses came to her *husband’s* house
to claim she had fornicated in her *father’s* house—
for she is to be judged at her father’s house!
Therefore it is stated:
“Should a man take a wife, consort with her, and *come to hate her*” (Dt. 22:13)

Come and see the trouble caused by hatred!
For it delivers us into
the clutches of slanderous speech.¹⁶⁹

(דברים כב טו) **וְלָקַח אֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָה וְאִמָּהּ** – אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ אָב וָאֵם, יֵשׁ לָהּ אָב וְלֹא אֵם, אֵם וְלֹא אָב, לֹא אָב וְלֹא אֵם מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **נַּעֲרָה**, מִכָּל מָקוֹם. אִם כֵּן, לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר **אֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָה וְאִמָּהּ**? הֵם, שֶׁגִּדְּלוּ גִּדּוּלִים רָעִים – יָבוֹאוּ וְיִתְנַוְּלוּ עִם גִּדּוּלֵיהֶם.


5. “Then the *father and mother* of the young lady¹⁷⁰; literally, “female youth,” from about the age of 13 years and a day (M. Nid.5:4). shall take” (Dt. 22:15)—
I might infer only that the rule applies
to someone with a *living* father and mother.
How do I know how the rule applies
if she has a father, but no mother,
or a mother, but no father,
or neither a father nor a mother?
The Teaching states:
“The *young lady*” (Dt. 22:15)—
the rule applies equally
[to a child of one living parent, or if both are dead].
If so, why does the verse specify:
“The *father and mother*” (Dt. 22:15)?
So that these people,
who raised such disgraceful offspring,
shall come and be disgraced along with their offspring!

## Paragraph 237

###### Sifrei Devarim 237:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/237:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/237:1)


(דברים כב יז) **וּפָרְשׂוּ הַשִּׂמְלָה** – יְחַוְּרוּ דְּבָרִים כַּשִּׂמְלָה. זֶה אֶחָד מִן הַדְּבָרִים שֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל דּוֹרֵשׁ מִן הַתּוֹרָה בְּמָשָׁל. כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ (שמות כב ב): ״אִם זָרְחָה הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ עָלָיו דָּמִים לוֹ״, וְכִי עָלָיו הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ זוֹרַחַת? וּמַה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אִם זָרְחָה הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ עָלָיו דָּמִים לוֹ״? מָה הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ – שָׁלוֹם לָעוֹלָם, אַף זֶה, אִם הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהוּא שָׁלוֹם מִמֶּנּוּ וַהֲרָגוֹ – הֲרֵי זֶה חַיָּב. כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ (שמות כא יט): ״אִם יָקוּם וְהִתְהַלֵּךְ בַּחוּץ עַל מִשְׁעַנְתּוֹ״ – עַל בּוּרְיוֹ. וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר **וּפָרְשׂוּ הַשִּׂמְלָה** – יְחַוְּרוּ דְּבָרִים כַּשִּׂמְלָה.


**Pisqa’ 237**¹⁷⁴
1. “Then they *spread out her night-dress*” (Dt. 22:17)—
that is, let the evidence be as clear
as [a blood-stain on] a night-dress!
**This is one of the instances in which**
**R. Ishmael would interpret the Torah metaphorically.** ¹⁷⁵ often, “parable” or “analogy.” //Mechilta Ishmael, *neziqin,* 6.
**A similar instance:**
**“If the sun rises upon *him*, he is responsible for the blood” (Ex. 22:2)—**
**now, is the sneak-thief the only one**
**upon whom the sun rises?**
**What, then, can the Teaching mean by:**
**“If the sun rises upon *him*?”**
**Just as the sun’s light**
**augurs peace for the world**
**[by illuminating darkness],**
**so, too, had this guy known that**
**the intruder meant to be peaceful,**
**but [went and] killed him anyway—**
**he is indeed liable for the death.**¹⁷⁶
**A similar instance:**
**“If he shall get up and walk about in the street upon his *staff*” (Ex. 21:19)—**
***staff* in this case represents**
**the patient’s restored well-being.**
**A similar instance:**
**“Then they *spread out her night-dress*” (Dt. 22:17)—**
**that is, let the evidence be as clear**
**as [a blood-stain on] a night-dress!**¹⁷⁷ 6.

רַבִּי עֲקִיבָה אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר **וּפָרְשׂוּ הַשִּׂמְלָה לִפְנֵי זִקְנֵי הָעִיר** – נִמְצְאוּ עֵדֵי הַבַּעַל זוֹמְמִים. **וּפָרְשׂוּ הַשִּׂמְלָה**, יָבוֹאוּ עֵדָיו שֶׁל זֶה וְעֵדָיו שֶׁל זֶה, וְיֹאמְרוּ דִבְרֵיהֶם **לִפְנֵי זִקְנֵי הָעִיר**.

And, similarly, Scripture says:
“Then they *spread out her night-dress* before the elders of the city” (Dt. 22:17)—
that is, if the husband’s witnesses are found to be in collusion against her
[the stained night dress is acceptable evidence to restore her reputation].¹⁷⁸
“Then *they spread out her night-dress* before the elders of the city” (Dt. 22:17)—
that is, let the witnesses for each party
present their cases before the elders of the city.

###### Sifrei Devarim 238:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/238:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/238:6)


**וְנָתְנוּ לַאֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָה** – וְלֹא לַאֲבִי הַבּוֹגֶרֶת. **וְנָתְנוּ לַאֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָה** – פְּרָט לְגִיּוֹרֶת שֶׁהָיְתָה הוֹרָתָהּ שֶׁלֹּא בִּקְדֻשָּׁה וְלֵידָתָהּ בִּקְדֻשָּׁה, שֶׁאֵין לָהּ מֵאָה כֶסֶף.


“Which they must give to the *young lady’s* father” (Dt. 22:19)—
but not to the father of an *adult* woman¹⁸⁰ literally, “having reached maturity.” The *na`arah* becomes a *bogeret* from thirteen and a half years of age.
[who is no longer part of her father’s household].
“Which they must give to the *young lady’s* father” (Dt. 22:19)—
**this excludes [the father of] a female proselyte,**
**whose conception was not consecrated**
**[by her mother’s conversion],**
**but whose birth *was* consecrated**
**[by her mother’s conversion].**¹⁸¹
**For, [when slandered by her husband], she is not entitled**
**to [compensation of] one hundred silver *sel`as***¹⁸² (Latin: *tetradrachma*) is the equivalent of two *sheqels.*
**[and neither, therefore, is her father].**¹⁸³

“For he brought *her* into disrepute” (Dt. 22:14)—
he didn’t merely bring *this one* into disrepute;

**וְלוֹ תִהְיֶה לְאִשָּׁה**, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁשּׁוֹתֶה בַּעֲצִיצוֹ; וַאֲפִלּוּ הִיא חִגֶּרֶת, וַאֲפִלּוּ הִיא סוּמָה, וַאֲפִלּוּ הִיא מֻכַּת שְׁחִין! נִמְצָא בָהּ דְּבַר זִמָּה, אוֹ שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לָבוֹא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, יָכוֹל יְהֵא רַשַּׁי לְקַיְּמָהּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וְלוֹ תִהְיֶה לְאִשָּׁה**, אִשָּׁה הָרְאוּיָה לוֹ.


2. “**And *she* shall be his wife” (Dt. 22:19)—**
**this teaches that**
**he drinks from his own urinal!**
**For, even if she is lame,**

**However—if he found in her a trace of lewdness,**

**[by circumstances of birth]**

## Paragraph 239

###### Sifrei Devarim 239:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/239:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/239:1)


(דברים כב כ) **וְאִם אֱמֶת הָיָה הַדָּבָר**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ; שֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **הָיָה**. יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה בִּיאָה בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **הַזֶּה**.


**Pisqa’ 239**¹⁸⁵
1. “But if this charge were true” (Dt. 22:20).
Now, I might infer only that
the rule applies to conventional sexual practices.¹⁸⁶; literally, “in her way,” i.e., “in the normal fashion.”
How do I know that
the rule also applies to unconventional sexual practices?¹⁸⁷ literally, “not in her way,” i.e., “not in the normal fashion.”
The Teaching states:
“If . . .it *were* true” (Dt. 22:20)—
[that she craved conventional practices,
she is likely to have pursued others as well].
Is it possible to say that
I can include
penetration of the other place?¹⁸⁸literally, “penetration from another place,” i.e., “anal penetration.”
The Teaching states:
“*This* charge” (Dt. 22:20)—
[the specification*, this*, warrants
inclusion of any sort of penetration].

footnotes:
¹⁸⁵ H:146-147;JN2:158
¹⁸⁶ Heb: kedarkah
¹⁸⁷ Heb: shelo kedarkah;
¹⁸⁸ Heb: bi’ah bemaqom ‘akher;


###### Sifrei Devarim 239:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/239:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/239:2)


**לֹא נִמְצְאוּ בְתוּלִים לַנַּעֲרָה** – אֵין עֵדִים לְהָזֵם עֵדָיו שֶׁל זֶה.


2. “And the young lady showed *no signs* of virginity” (Dt. 22:20)—
that is, there are no *witnesses* to impugn
this guy’s testimony.


###### Sifrei Devarim 239:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/239:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/239:3)


(דברים כב כא) **וְהוֹצִיאוּ אֶת הַנַּעֲרָה אֶל פֶּתַח בֵּית אָבִיהָ**, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ אָב וְיֵשׁ לָהּ פֶּתַח בֵּית אָב, יֵשׁ לָהּ פֶּתַח בֵּית אָב וְאֵין לָהּ אָב מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וְהוֹצִיאוּ אֶת הַנַּעֲרָה** מִכָּל מָקוֹם. אִם כֵּן לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר **אֶל פֶּתַח בֵּית אָבִיהָ**? – מִצְוָה.


“And they shall bring the young lady out to the *door* of her *father’s house*” (Dt. 22:21)—
**I might infer only that**
**[the trial must be held]**
**for a daughter with *a living father*,**
**and for one whose father has a *door* to his house.**¹⁸⁹
How do I know that
[the rule also applies]
if her father’s house has a door,
but he is no longer living?
The Teaching states:
“And they *shall bring* the young lady out” (Dt. 22:21)—
whatever [her father’s circumstances may be].
If so, why is it specified:
“To the *door* of her *father’s house*” (Dt. 22:21)?—
this is the proper procedure.

footnotes:
¹⁸⁹ Cf. M. Ket.4:3.

**Now, can *all* the men of her city**
**actually *pummel* her?**

**from among all the men of her city.**

###### Sifrei Devarim 240:2

**בָּאֲבָנִים**, יָכוֹל בַּאֲבָנִים מְרֻבּוֹת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (ויקרא כ ב): ״בָּאֶבֶן״. אִי בָּאֶבֶן, יָכוֹל בְּאֶבֶן אַחַת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **בָּאֲבָנִים**. אֱמֹר מֵעַתָּה: אִם לֹא מֵתָה בָרִאשׁוֹנָה תָּמוּת בַּשְּׁנִיָּה.


**“With *stones*” (Dt. 22:21)—**
**is it possible to say that many stones are used?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“With *stone*” (Lv. 20:2).**
**If “with *stone*”—**
**is it possible to say, then, that only *one* stone is used?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“with *stones*” (Dt. 22:21)!**
**From this you may conclude that**
**if she doesn’t die from the first stone,**
**let her die from the second!**¹⁹² 220.1

###### Sifrei Devarim 240:4

**לִזְנוֹת בֵּית אָבִיהָ**, נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״אָבִיהָ״ וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן (ויקרא כא ט) ״אָבִיהָ״, מָה אָבִיהָ הָאָמוּר לְהַלָּן, זְנוּת עִם זִיקַת הַבַּעַל – אַף אָבִיהָ הָאָמוּר כָּאן, זְנוּת עִם זִיקַת הַבַּעַל.


**“By fornicating in the house of *her father*” (Dt. 22:21).**
***Her father* is mentioned here (Dt. 22:21),**
**And *her father* is mentioned elsewhere (Lv. 21:9).**¹⁹³?
**Just as *her father* elsewhere is mentioned**
**in the context of fornication that**
**violates the connection to her husband,**
**so, too, *her father* is mentioned here,**¹⁹⁴ 240, n.3
**in the context of fornication that**
**violates the connection to her husband.**¹⁹⁵, per.1:15.

###### Sifrei Devarim 242:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/242:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/242:5)


**וּסְקַלְתֶּם אֹתָם בָּאֲבָנִים**, יָכוֹל בָּאֲבָנִים מְרֻבּוֹת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (ויקרא כ כז): ״בָּאֶבֶן״. אִי ״בָּאֶבֶן״, יָכוֹל אֲפִלּוּ בְּאֶבֶן אַחַת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **בָּאֲבָנִים**. אֱמֹר מֵעַתָּה: אִם לֹא מֵתוּ בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה, יָמוּתוּ בַּשְּׁנִיָּה.


**“Where you shall *pelt* them with *stones* till they die” (Dt. 22:24)—**
**Is it possible to say that many stones are used?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“With *stone*” (Lv. 20:2).**
**If “with *stone*”—**
**is it possible to say, then, that only one stone is used?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“With *stones*” (Dt. 22:24)!**
**From this you may conclude that**
**if they don’t die from the first stone, let them die from the second!**²⁰⁴ 220.1, 240.1, etc.

²⁰⁴ // Sifre Nu., 114. Cf. Pisqa’ot


###### Sifrei Devarim 242:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/242:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/242:6)


**אֶת הַנַּעֲרָה עַל דְּבַר אֲשֶׁר לֹא צָעֲקָה**. כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר **עַל דְּבַר** עַל פִּי הַתְרָאָה, לְהָבִיא אֶת הַמְּזִידָה בְּהַתְרָיַת עֵדִים.


3. “The young lady, *for the reason* of not calling out” (Dt. 22:24).
When He says, *for the reason of*²⁰⁵ literally, “on the word/matter of.” Dt. 22:24),
[it implies that she ignored] “an oral warning.”²⁰⁶; literally, “according to a warning.” For a similar exegesis of Dt. 22:24, see *Pisqa’* 250.1.
Thus the rule applies to a woman who—
warned by onlookers [of the Torah’s severity in this matter]—
brazenly ignores their warnings.

###### Sifrei Devarim 242:7

**וְאֶת הָאִישׁ עַל דְּבַר אֲשֶׁר עִנָּה אֶת אֵשֶׁת רֵעֵהוּ**, כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר **עַל דְּבַר** – עַל פִּי הַתְרָיָה.


4. “And the man, for the reason of assaulting his kinsman’s wife” (Dt. 22:24)—
when He says, *for the reason of*,
[it implies that the man ignored] “an oral warning”
[that raping a married woman is a capital offense].


###### Sifrei Devarim 242:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/242:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/242:8)


(דברים כב כה) אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בָּעִיר, בַּשָּׂדֶה מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (דברים כב כה): **וְאִם בַּשָּׂדֶה יִמְצָא הָאִישׁ**.


I might infer only that
this rule applies in a town.
How do I apply it in the countryside?
The Teaching states:
“But if the man found her in the countryside” (Dt. 22:25).


###### Sifrei Devarim 242:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/242:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/242:9)


**וְשָׁכַב עִמָּהּ**, פְּרָט לְשֶׁאֶחָד מַחֲזִיק וְאֶחָד שׁוֹכֵב, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.


“And he bedded her” (Dt. 22:25)—
this excludes [an attack in which]
one man holds her down while the other beds her down:
Words of R. Judah.


###### Sifrei Devarim 242:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/242:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/242:10)


**וּמֵת הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר שָׁכַב עִמָּהּ לְבַדּוֹ**, הָרִאשׁוֹן בִּסְקִילָה וְהַשֵּׁנִי בְּחֶנֶק.


“Then, only the man *who* bedded her shall die” (Dt. 22:25)—
**That is, the first assailant, [who “bedded” her,] is executed by stoning**
**[like any rapist of a married woman],**
**while the second, [who pinned her down,]**
**is executed by strangulation.**²⁰⁷

## Paragraph 243

###### Sifrei Devarim 243:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/243:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/243:1)


(דברים כב כו) **וְלַנַּעֲרָה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה דָבָר** – מְלַמֵּד שֶׁפְּטָרָהּ הַכָּתוּב מִן הַמִּיתָה. מִנַּיִן אַף מִן הַקׇּרְבָּן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **חֵטְא**. מִנַּיִן אַף מִן הַמַּכּוֹת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **חֵטְא מָוֶת**.


**Pisqa’ 243**²⁰⁸
1. “But, do *nothing* to the young lady” (Dt. 22:26)—
This teaches that
the verse releases her from [the penalty of] execution.
How do I know that
it also [releases her from the obligation] to bring a sacrifice?²⁰⁹
The Teaching states:
“The young lady has committed *no sin* worthy of the death sentence” (Dt. 22:26)—
[therefore, she has no obligation to make an offering
in absolution of such a sin].
How do I know that
the verse releases her as well from
the option of a judicial lashing?
The Teaching states:
“No sin *worthy* of the death sentence” (Dt. 22:26).

footnotes:
²⁰⁸ H:248-249;JN2:163-164.
²⁰⁹ A Purification-offering.


###### Sifrei Devarim 243:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/243:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/243:2)


**כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר יָקוּם אִישׁ עַל רֵעֵהוּ וּרְצָחוֹ נֶפֶשׁ**, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכָּל אֲנוּסִים שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה פְּטוּרִים וּמַצִּילִים אוֹתָם בְּנַפְשָׁם. אֵין לִי אֶלָּא זֶה, מִנַּיִן אַף הָרוֹדֵף אַחַר חֲבֵרוֹ לְהָרְגוֹ וְאַחַר הַזָּכוּר? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **כֵּן הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה**. יָכוֹל אַף הָרוֹדֵף אַחַר הַבְּהֵמָה וְהַמְחַלֵּל אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְהָעוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **הַזֶּה** – זֶה בִּסְקִילָה וְאֵין כָּל אֵלּוּ בִּסְקִילָה.


2. “For that matter, should a man rise up *intending only to strike* his kinsman,
but he delivers instead a fatal wound” (Dt. 22:26)—
this teaches that
any transgression of the Torah,
committed accidentally,
is released from penalty.
But one may save a victim
[from a murderous attack]
at the cost of [the attacker’s] life.
I might infer only that the rule
applies to this case [of the murderer].
**On what basis do I know that it also applies**
**to someone pursuing his companion [intending] to kill him?**
**Or to someone pursuing a male [in order to sodomize him]?** ²¹⁰
The Teaching states:
“*This* is a *comparable case*” (Dt. 22:26)—
[in which the victim is saved at the cost of the assailant’s life].3. **Is it possible to say that the same rule applies**
**even to someone chasing a beast [for sexual gratification],**
**or to one rushing off to desecrate the Sabbath,**
**or to another rushing off to engage in the rites of a foreign cult?**²¹¹
The Teaching states:
“*This* is a *comparable case*” (Dt. 22:26)—
*this* refers to transgressions
that involve stoning.
But these others do not involve stoning.

footnotes:
²¹⁰ = M. San. 8:7; // T. San. 11:10.
²¹¹ = M. San.8:7; // T. San.11:11.


###### Sifrei Devarim 243:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/243:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/243:3)


(דברים כב כז) **כִּי בַשָּׂדֶה מְצָאָהּ**, יָכוֹל בָּעִיר חַיֶּבֶת, בַּשָּׂדֶה תְּהֵא פְטוּרָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **צָעֲקָה הַנַּעֲרָה הַמְאֹרָשָׂה וְאֵין מוֹשִׁיעַ לָהּ**. הָא אִם יֵשׁ לָהּ מוֹשִׁיעַ, בֵּין בָּעִיר בֵּין בַּשָּׂדֶה חַיֶּבֶת, וְאִם אֵין לָהּ מוֹשִׁיעַ, בֵּין בָּעִיר בֵּין בַּשָּׂדֶה פְּטוּרָה.


4. “For he found her in the *countryside*” (Dt. 22:27)—
is it possible to say that
she would be under liability
if the assault occurred in town,
but in the field, she has no liability?
The Teaching states:
“The betrothed young lady did, indeed, cry out, but *there was none* to save her” (Dt. 22:27)—
Consider this:
**if someone can, indeed, save her**
**[and she fails to cry out]—**
**whether in town or in the countryside—**
**she is held liable [for provoking the attack];**
**but if there is, in fact, none to save her**
**[and she failed to cry out]—**
**whether in town or in the countryside**—
**she has no liability**.²¹² 13.

²¹² Mechilta Ishmael, neziqin,

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/243:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/243:4)


**צָעֲקָה**, פְּרָט לְשֶׁאָמְרָה הַנַּח לוֹ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.


**“*She did* . . . cry out” (Dt. 22:27)—**
**this excludes the victim who says to witnesses—leave him be:**
**Words of R. Judah.**²¹³

## Paragraph 244

###### Sifrei Devarim 244:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/244:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/244:1)


(דברים כב כח) **כִּי יִמְצָא אִישׁ נַעֲרָה בְּתוּלָה**, נֶאֱמַר כָּאן בְּתוּלָה וְנֶאֱמַר בְּתוּלָה בַּמְפַתֶּה, מָה אוֹנֵס חָמוּר אֵינוֹ חַיָּב אֶלָּא עַל בְּתוּלָה, מְפַתֶּה הַקַּל אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא חַיָּב אֶלָּא עַל בְּתוּלָה? אוֹ חִלּוּף, אִם מְפַתֶּה הַקַּל הֲרֵי הוּא חַיָּב עַל בְּתוּלָה וְעַל שֶׁאֵינָהּ בְּתוּלָה, אוֹנֵס חָמוּר אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁיְּהֵא חַיָּב עַל הַבְּתוּלָה וְעַל שֶׁאֵינָהּ בְּתוּלָה? מַה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר בְּתוּלָה בָּאוֹנֵס? שֶׁיָּכוֹל לֹא יְהֵא נוֹתֵן לְאָבִיהָ אֲבָל יְהֵא נוֹתֵן לָהּ, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **בְּתוּלָה** פְּרָט לִבְעוּלָה. אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בְּעוּלָה, מֻכַּת עֵץ מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **בְּתוּלָה** פְּרָט לְמֻכַּת עֵץ. נֶאֱמַר כָּאן **אֲשֶׁר לֹא אֹרָשָׂה** וְנֶאֱמַר בַּמְפַתֶּה ״אֲשֶׁר לֹא אֹרָשָׂה״, מָה אוֹנֵס חָמוּר אֵינוֹ חַיָּב עַל שֶׁנִּתְאָרְסָה וְנִתְגָּרְשָׁה, מְפַתֶּה הַקַּל אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא חַיָּב עַל שֶׁנִּתְאָרְסָה וְנִתְגָּרְשָׁה? אוֹ חִלּוּף, מָה אִם מְפַתֶּה הַקַּל הֲרֵי הוּא חַיָּב עַל שֶׁנִּתְאָרְסָה וְנִתְגָּרְשָׁה, אוֹנֵס חָמוּר אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁיְּהֵא חַיָּב עַל שֶׁנִּתְאָרְסָה וְנִתְגָּרְשָׁה? מַה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר **אֲשֶׁר לֹא אֹרָשָׂה** בָּאוֹנֵס? שֶׁיָּכוֹל לֹא יְהֵא נוֹתֵן לְאָבִיהָ אֲבָל יְהֵא נוֹתֵן לָהּ, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **אֲשֶׁר לֹא אֹרָשָׂה** **אֲשֶׁר לֹא אֹרָשָׂה** שְׁתֵּי פְעָמִים, שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא נוֹתֵן לֹא לָהּ וְלֹא לְאָבִיהָ. נֶאֱמַר כָּאן **נַעֲרָה** וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר **נַעֲרָה** בַּמְפַתֶּה, מָה אוֹנֵס חָמוּר אֵינוֹ חַיָּב אֶלָּא עַל הַנַּעֲרָה, מְפַתֶּה הַקַּל אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא חַיָּב אֶלָּא עַל הַנַּעֲרָה? אוֹ חִלּוּף, מָה מְפַתֶּה הַקַּל הֲרֵי הוּא חַיָּב עַל נַעֲרָה וְעַל שֶׁאֵינָהּ נַעֲרָה, אוֹנֵס חָמוּר אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁיְּהֵא חַיָּב עַל נַעֲרָה וְעַל שֶׁאֵינָהּ נַעֲרָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וְנָתַן לַאֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָה** וְלֹא לַאֲבִי הַבּוֹגֶרֶת. וַהֲלֹא דְבָרִים קַל וָחֹמֶר, וּמָה אוֹנֵס חָמוּר אֵינוֹ חַיָּב עַל הַבּוֹגֶרֶת, מְפַתֶּה הַקַּל אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא חַיָּב עַל הַבּוֹגֶרֶת? לְהַחֲלִיף אֶת הַדִּין אִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל שֶׁהֲרֵי כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר **נַעֲרָה נַעֲרָה** שְׁתֵּי פְעָמִים.


**Pisqa’ 244**²¹⁴
1. “Should a man find a virginal young lady,²¹⁵ cf.H: 473, *Pisqa’* 244, n.6.” (Dt. 22:28)—
*Virginal* is mentioned here in a case of rape (Dt. 22:28).
and *virginal* is mentioned elsewhere in a case of seduction (Ex. 22:15).
**Just as in the grave crime of rape,**
**he is obliged only to**
**[compensate the father of]**
**a *virginal* young lady,**
**isn’t it only logical that,**
**in the lesser crime of seduction,**
**he should be obliged only**
**[to compensate the father of]**
**the *virginal* young lady**
**[instead of marrying her (Ex. 22:15)] ?**²¹⁶ 17.
Now, let’s reverse the logic:
If, in the lesser crime of seduction,
the seducer is indeed obliged
[to dower and marry the young lady (Ex. 22:15)],
whether or not [after seduction] she
remains virginal,
isn’t it only logical that,
in the grave crime of rape,
the rapist should be obliged
[to compensate the father of]
a virginal young lady
as well as [the father of] a young lady
who has not remained virginal?
What, then, does the Teaching add by saying
“Virginal” (Dt. 22:28)?
The rule applies to her rape.
2. **Is it possible to say that**
**we should not compensate the father,**
**[whose daughter has been raped,]**
**but only compensate the daughter?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“Virginal” (Dt:22:28)—**
**excluding a woman who has already been mounted**
**[prior to the rape].**²¹⁷ 17.
**Now I might infer only that**
**the rule applies to a woman who has**
**already been mounted.**
**How do I know about a woman**
**who was struck by a stick?**
**The Teaching states:**
**“*Virginal*” (Dt. 22:28)—**
**this is to exclude from the rule**
**one struck by a stick.**²¹⁸
3. Here, [regarding the rape-victim,] it is stated:
“Who is *not betrothed*” (Dt. 22:28),
and it is stated elsewhere, of the seduced:
“Who is *not betrothed*” (Ex. 22:15)—
Just as in the grave crime of rape,
the rapist is not obliged [to compensate]
a betrothed woman who was expelled
[from the betrothal prior to the rape],
So, too, in the lesser crime of seduction—
isn’t it only logical that
the seducer should not be obliged [to compensate]
A betrothed woman who was expelled
[from the betrothal prior to the seduction]? ²¹⁹ The rape victim, receives these three, in addition to compensation for pain. Cf. M. Ket.3:7.
Now, let’s reverse the logic:
Just as in the lesser crime of seduction,
we note that the seducer is obliged [to compensate]
a betrothed woman who was expelled
[from the betrothal prior to the rape,]
isn’t it only logical that,
in the grave crime of rape,
he should also be obliged [to compensate]?
What, then, does the Teaching add by
[stressing the phrase:]
“Who *is not* betrothed” (Dt. 22:28)?
The rule applies to rape
[rather than to seduction].
Is it possible to say that
we should not compensate the father,
but only compensate the victim?
The Teaching states two times:
“Who is not betrothed” (Dt. 22:28)
and “who is not betrothed” (Ex. 22:15)—
Thus, neither she nor her father is due compensation.4. Here, [in the case of rape,]
The term, *young lady*, appears (Dt. 22:28),
while it does *not* appear
in the case of seduction (Ex. 22:15).
Just as in the severe crime of rape,
the rapist is obliged [to marry the victim]
only if she is a *young lady*,
isn’t it only logical that
in the lesser crime of seduction,
the seducer should be obliged [to marry the victim]
only if she is a *young lady*?
Now, let’s reverse the logic:
Just as in the lesser crime of seduction,
we note that the seducer is obliged
[to marry the victim,]
whether or not she is still a *young lady*—
isn’t it only logical that,
in the grave crime of rape,
the rapist should be obliged
[to marry the victim]
whether or not she is still a *young lady*?
The Teaching states:
“And the man who beds her shall give to the father of *the young lady*” (Dt. 22:29)—
but not to the father of an adult woman.4. Now, isn’t this a matter of logic?
For, just as in the severe crime of rape—
the rapist owes nothing [to the father],
on account of the rape of an adult daughter—
So, too, where the lesser crime
of seduction is committed,
isn’t it only logical that
the seducer owes nothing [to the father]?
Now there’s no reversing this logic!
For, indeed, the term, *young lady,*
has already been mentioned twice (Dt. 22:28, Dt. 22:29)

**One may marry the near kin of**

**[and is not liable under the rules of incest].**
**But one who rapes or seduces**
**the near kin of a married woman**
**stands under liability [for execution].**
**A man may marry the near kin of**

**He stands under liability,**
**as he would for a**

**For this reason is it stated:**
**“A man shall not take *his father’s wife*” (Dt. 23:1**).²²⁴

###### Sifrei Devarim 248:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/248:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/248:2)


אֵיזֶהוּ מַמְזֵר? כָּל שְׁאֵר בָּשָׂר שֶׁהוּא בְּ״לֹא יָבוֹא״, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָה. שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים כג א): ״לֹא יִקַּח אִישׁ אֶת אֵשֶׁת אָבִיו וְלֹא יְגַלֶּה כְּנַף אָבִיו״, (דברים כג ג) ״לֹא יָבֹא מַמְזֵר בִּקְהַל ה׳״ – מַה אֵשֶׁת אָב מְיוּחֶדֶת שֶׁהִיא שְׁאֵר בָּשָׂר שֶׁהוּא בְּ״לֹא יָבוֹא״ וְהַוָּלָד מַמְזֵר, כָּךְ כָּל שְׁאֵר בָּשָׂר שֶׁהוּא בְּ״לֹא יָבוֹא״ הַוָּלָד מַמְזֵר.


**What, then, constitutes impaired lineage?**
**Any offspring of near kin**
**[whose marriage] places them under the**
**rule of *No Entry*:**
**Words of R. Akiva.**²³⁶
For it is stated:
“A man shall not take his father’s wife” (Dt. 23:1), and
“No one of impaired lineage shall enter the Community of HASHEM” (Dt. 23:3)—
Just as a father’s wife is distinctive,
being near of kin and under the rule of *No Entry*,
such that her offspring carries impaired lineage,
so, too, shouldn’t the offspring
of anyone who is near of kin, and under the rule of *No Entry*,
carry impaired lineage?

²³⁶ =M. Yev. 4:13.


###### Sifrei Devarim 248:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/248:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/248:3)


שִׁמְעוֹן הַתֵּימָנִי אוֹמֵר: כָּל שֶׁחַיָּבִים עָלָיו כָּרֵת בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם הַוָּלָד מַמְזֵר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים כג א): ״לֹא יִקַּח אִישׁ אֶת אֵשֶׁת אָבִיו וְלֹא יְגַלֶּה כְּנַף אָבִיו״, (דברים כג ג) ״לֹא יָבֹא מַמְזֵר בִּקְהַל ה׳״ – מָה אֵשֶׁת אָב מְיֻחֶדֶת שֶׁחַיָּבִים עָלֶיהָ כָּרֵת בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם הַוָּלָד מַמְזֵר, כָּךְ כָּל שֶׁחַיָּבִים עָלָיו כָּרֵת בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם הַוָּלָד מַמְזֵר.


2. **Shimon the Temanite says:**
**Any [marriage] that places [the couple]**
**under judgment of Heavenly excision—**
**the offspring carries impaired lineage,**²³⁷
as it is said:
“A man shall not take his father’s wife” (Dt. 23:1), and
“No one of impaired lineage shall enter the Community of HASHEM” (Dt. 23:3)—
Just as a father’s wife is distinctive,
in that [one who marries her] is placed
under judgment of Heavenly excision,
and the offspring carries impaired lineage,
so, too, shouldn’t [the offspring of any couple]
whose marriage places them
under judgment of Heavenly excision,
also carry impaired lineage?

²³⁷ =M. Yev. 4:13.


###### Sifrei Devarim 248:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/248:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/248:4)


רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: כָּל שֶׁחַיָּבִים עָלָיו מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין הַוָּלָד מַמְזֵר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים כג א): ״לֹא יִקַּח אִישׁ אֶת אֵשֶׁת אָבִיו״, וּכְתִיב (דברים כג ג): ״לֹא יָבֹא מַמְזֵר״ – מָה אֵשֶׁת אָב מְיֻחֶדֶת שֶׁחַיָּבִים עָלֶיהָ מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין וְהַוָּלָד מַמְזֵר, כָּךְ כָּל שֶׁחַיָּבִים עָלָיו מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין הַוָּלָד מַמְזֵר.


3. R. Joshua says:
Any[marriage] that places the couple
under judgment of judicial execution—
the offspring carries impaired lineage,²³⁸
as it is said:
“A man shall not take his father’s wife” (Dt. 23:1), and
“No one of corrupted lineage shall enter the Community of HASHEM” (Dt. 23:3)—
Just as a father’s wife is distinctive,
in that [one who marries her] is placed
under judgment of judicial execution,
and the offspring carries impaired lineage,
so, too, shouldn’t the offspring of
any [couple whose marriage places them]
under judgment of judicial execution,
also carry impaired lineage?

###### Sifrei Devarim 248:5

**דּוֹר עֲשִׂירִי**, נֶאֱמַר כָּאן דּוֹר עֲשִׂירִי וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן דּוֹר עֲשִׂירִי, מַה דּוֹר עֲשִׂירִי הָאָמוּר לְמַטָּה עַד עוֹלָם אַף דּוֹר עֲשִׂירִי הָאָמוּר כָּאן עַד עוֹלָם.


4. “Even to the *tenth generation*” (Dt. 23:3)—
[does this mean that the exclusion will
at some point expire]?
Here, the *tenth generation* is mentioned (Dt. 23:3),
and elsewhere, the *tenth generation* is mentioned (Dt. 23:4).
Just as the *tenth generation* mentioned elsewhere (Dt. 23:4) implies *forever*,
so, too, the *tenth generation* mentioned here implies *forever*.



## Paragraph 249

###### Sifrei Devarim 249:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/249:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/249:1)


(דברים כג ד) **לֹא יָבֹא עַמּוֹנִי וּמוֹאָבִי בִּקְהַל ה׳** – בִּזְכָרִים הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר וְלֹא בִנְקֵבוֹת, עַמּוֹנִי וְלֹא עַמּוֹנִית מוֹאָבִי וְלֹא מוֹאָבִית, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: ״עַל דְּבַר אֲשֶׁר לֹא קִדְּמוּ אֶתְכֶם בַּלֶּחֶם וּבַמַּיִם״, מִי דַרְכּוֹ לְקַדֵּם? אֲנָשִׁים וְלֹא נָשִׁים.


**Pisqa’ 249**²³⁹
1. “Neither an *Ammonite* nor a *Moabite* shall enter the Community of HASHEM” (Dt. 23:4).
The verse is discussing males, not females.
**“An Ammonite” (Dt. 23:4)—**
**but an Ammonite woman is not excluded.**
**“A Moabite” (Dt. 23:4)—**
**and a Moabite woman is not excluded:**
**Words of R. Judah.**²⁴⁰
But sages say:
“In the matter of their failure to extend hospitality to you, with bread and water” (Dt. 23:5)—
Now, who normally extends hospitality?
Isn’t it the men rather than the women?
[Thus, the Ammonite and Moabite women,
who are blameless for the sin of the males,
should not share their punishment]!

###### Sifrei Devarim 249:2

שֶׁהָיָה בַדִּין: וּמַה מַּמְזֵר שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ ״עַד עוֹלָם״ עָשָה בוֹ נָשִׁים כַּאֲנָשִׁים, עַמּוֹנִים וּמוֹאָבִים שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהֶם ״עַד עוֹלָם״, אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁנַּעֲשֶׂה בָהֶם נָשִׁים כַּאֲנָשִׁים? אוֹ חִלּוּף: מַה עַמּוֹנִים וּמוֹאָבִים שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהֶם ״עַד עוֹלָם״ לֹא עָשָה בָהֶם נָשִׁים כַּאֲנָשִׁים, מַּמְזֵר שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ ״עַד עוֹלָם״ אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁלֹּא נַעֲשֶׂה בוֹ נָשִׁים כַּאֲנָשִׁים? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לֹא יָבֹא מַמְזֵר״, בֵּין אִישׁ בֵּין אִשָּׁה.


2. **Well, I could have reasoned otherwise:**
**Just as a man carrying impaired lineage**
**is not said to be excluded from the community “forever” (Dt. 23:4),**
**yet, the women among them are treated like the men—**
**[both subject to the same ten-year period of exclusion,]**
**shouldn’t it follow that**
**[in the case of male] Ammonites and Moabites—**
**who *are* excluded from the community “forever”—**
**the women among them are treated like the men—**
**[both subject to the same permanent period of exclusion?]** ²⁴¹
Or, perhaps, reverse the argument!
Just as Ammonites and Moabites,
who *are* said to be excluded from the community “forever” (Dt. 23:4),
and, the women among them are treated like the men—
both being subject to an endless period of exclusion,
shouldn’t it follow that
[in the case of males] carrying impaired lineage,
yet, who are *not* said to be excluded from the community “forever,”
the women should *not* be subject to the same
[ten years of exclusion] as the men?
The Teaching states:
“*No one* of impaired lineage shall enter the Community of HASHEM” (Dt. 23:3)—
whether a man or a woman.

אַחַר שֶׁרִבָּה הַכָּתוּב מִיעֵט, הָא אֵין עָלֶיךָ לָדוּן אֶלָּא כְּדִין הָרִאשׁוֹן: וּמַה מַּמְזֵר שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ ״עַד עוֹלָם״ עָשָׂה בּוֹ נָשִׁים כַּאֲנָשִׁים, עַמּוֹנִים וּמוֹאָבִים שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהֶם ״עַד עוֹלָם״ אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁנַּעֲשֶׂה בָּהֶם נָשִׁים כַּאֲנָשִׁים? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״עַמּוֹנִי״ וְלֹא עַמּוֹנִית, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.


3. Now, when the verse expands the range of the rule (i.e., Dt. 23:4),
[by permitting female Ammonites and Moabites
to enter the community immediately,]
it constricts [the range of a second rule (i.e. Dt. 23:3),
by excluding impaired females for ten years]!
Look—
you only need reason in accord with
the conclusions of the former argument!²⁴²
Just as a man carrying impaired lineage
is *not* excluded from the community “forever” (Dt. 23:4),
and the women among them are subject to the same
[ten-year period of exclusion],
shouldn’t it follow that
[in the case of male] Ammonites and Moabites,
who are said to be excluded from the community “forever,”
the women among them should be subject to
the same [permanent] exclusion?
The Teaching states:
“An Ammonite” (Dt. 23:4)—
but not an Ammonite woman:
Words of R. Judah.

אִם נֶאֱמַר **דּוֹר עֲשִׂירִי** לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר **עַד עוֹלָם**? מוּפְנֶה לְהַקִּישׁ וְלָדוּן גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה. נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״דּוֹר עֲשִׂירִי״ וְנֶאֱמַר לְמַעְלָה ״דּוֹר עֲשִׂירִי״, מַה דּוֹר עֲשִׂירִי הָאָמוּר כָּאן עַד עוֹלָם, אַף דּוֹר עֲשִׂירִי הָאָמוּר לְמַעְלָה עַד עוֹלָם.


4. If the verse states:
“The tenth generation” (Dt. 23:4),
why does it add: “Forever?” (Dt. 23:4)
*Forever* is open-ended,
leaving it free for comparative exegesis
on the basis of analogical reasoning.
Here, the *tenth generation* is mentioned (Dt. 23:4),
and elsewhere, the tenth generation is mentioned (Dt. 23:3).
Just as the *tenth generation*, mentioned elsewhere (Dt. 23:3) implies *forever*,
So, too, the “tenth generation” mentioned here implies *forever*.

###### Sifrei Devarim 250:5

(דברים כג ו) **וְלֹא אָבָה ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ לִשְׁמֹעַ אֶל בִּלְעָם**, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהַמְּקַלֵּל הוּא הַמְּקֻלָּל. **וַיַּהֲפֹךְ ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְּךָ אֶת הַקְּלָלָה לִבְרָכָה** מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאַף הַמְּקַלֵּל מִתְקַלֵּל. מִפְּנֵי מָה? **כִּי אֲהֵבְךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ**.


“But HASHEM your God did not consent to listen to Bilaam” (Dt. 23:6)—
this teaches that
the one uttering a curse [upon Israel]
is himself the accursed!
“And HASHEM your God up-ended the curse, transforming it into a blessing” (Dt. 23:6)—
this teaches that
the one uttering a curse winds up bringing a curse upon himself.²⁴⁸ (“to curse”) structures each verb in this series of assonantal exegeses: *meqalel* (“utter a curse”), *mequlal* (“accursed”), *mitqalel* (“to curse oneself”).
And why is this so?
“Because HASHEM your God loves you!” (Dt. 23:6)

## Paragraph 252

###### Sifrei Devarim 252:1

(דברים כג ח) **לֹא תְתַעֵב אֲדֹמִי**, מִפְּנֵי מָה? **כִּי אָחִיךָ הוּא**, וּגְדוֹלָה אַחְוָה.


**Pisqa’ 252**²⁵³
1. “Do not despise an Edomite” (Dt. 23:8)—

and brotherhood is praiseworthy.

###### Sifrei Devarim 252:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/252:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/252:2)


**לֹא תְתַעֵב מִצְרִי**, מִפְּנֵי מָה? **כִּי גֵר הָיִיתָ בְאַרְצוֹ**. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה: הַמִּצְרִים לֹא קִבְּלוּ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶלָּא לְצֹרֶךְ עַצְמָם, וְקָבַע לָהֶם הַמָּקוֹם שָׂכָר. וַהֲלֹא דְבָרִים קַל וָחֹמֶר: אִם מִי שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּן לְזַכּוֹת וְזִכָּה מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִלּוּ זִכָּה, הַמִּתְכַּוֵּן לְזַכּוֹת עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה.


“Do not despise an Egyptian” (Dt. 23:8)—
Why not?
“Because you were a migrant in his land” (Dt. 23:8)—
[therefore, you are in his debt].2. Said R. Elazar b. Azariah:
The Egyptians received Israel with ulterior motives;
yet the All-Present endowed them with a reward.
**Now, isn’t this a matter of simple logic?**
**If someone had *no* intention to earn merit,**
**yet his deed was meritorious,**
**Scripture considers him to have earned merit—**
**if he *intended* to earn merit,**
**shouldn’t we expect all the more so that**
**he be considered to have earned merit?**²⁵⁴ 283.6

²⁵⁴ =T. Peah 3:10. Cf. Pisqa’


###### Sifrei Devarim 252:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/252:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/252:3)


רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מִצְרִים הֵם טִבְּעוּ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמַּיִם, וַאֲדוֹמִים קִדְּמוּ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּחֶרֶב וְלֹא אֲסָרָם הַכָּתוּב אֶלָּא עַד שְׁלֹשָׁה דוֹרוֹת, עַמּוֹנִים וּמוֹאָבִים מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנָּטְלוּ עֵצָה לְהַחֲטִיא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲסָרָם הַכָּתוּב אִסּוּר עוֹלָם, לְלַמֶּדְךָ שֶׁהַמַּחֲטִיא אֶת הָאָדָם קָשֶׁה לוֹ מִן הַהוֹרְגוֹ, שֶׁהַהוֹרְגוֹ אֵין מוֹצִיאוֹ אֶלָּא מִן הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְהַמַּחֲטִיאוֹ מוֹצִיאוֹ מִן הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וּמִן הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.


R. Shimon says:
Egypt drowned Israel in the waters [of the Nile]
and Edom greeted them with the sword—
yet Scripture forbids them entry
into the Community [of Israel]
for only three generations (Dt. 23:4)]!
The Ammonites and Moabites,
however, are forbidden forever,
because they took Balak’s counsel ²⁵⁵ 250.1 on Micah 6:5.
and enticed Israel into sin.
This teaches you that
one who entices a person into sin
does him more harm than his murderer.
For a murderer expels him only from the present eon,
but one who entices a person into sin
expels him from the present eon
as well as the coming eon.

**Pisqa’ 253**²⁵⁶

אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: קַל וָחֹמֶר הַדְּבָרִים, וּמָה אִם בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁאָסַר זְכָרִים אִסּוּר עוֹלָם הִתִּיר אֶת הַנְּקֵבוֹת מִיָּד, מָקוֹם שֶׁלֹּא אָסַר אֶת הַזְּכָרִים אֶלָּא עַד שְׁלֹשָׁה דוֹרוֹת אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁנַּתִּיר אֶת הַנְּקֵבוֹת מִיָּד? אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אִם הֲלָכָה נְקַבֵּל, וְאִם לְדִין יֵשׁ תְּשׁוּבָה. אָמַר לָהֶם: לֹא כִי, הֲלָכָה אֲנִי אוֹמֵר וְהַכָּתוּב מְסַיְּעֵנִי, **בָּנִים** וְלֹא בָנוֹת.


2. **Said R. Shimon:**
**It’s a simple matter of logic!**
**Just as in a context**
**in which males are excluded forever,**
**females are granted immediate entry,**²⁵⁸ 249.1-2.
**doesn’t it follow logically that,**
**in a context such as ours (i.e., Dt. 23:9),**
**in which males are excluded for only three generations,**
**we should we grant females immediate entry?**
**They replied to him:**
**If this rule has been transmitted as tradition,**
**we must consider it;**
**but if it’s only a logical deduction,**
**it can always be refuted!**
**He answered them:**
**No, indeed—**
**I’m transmitting a tradition!** ²⁵⁹
The verse supports me:
“Sons” (Dt. 23:9)—
[are excluded for three generations,]
but not daughters!

###### Sifrei Devarim 253:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/253:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/253:3)


**דּוֹר שְׁלִישִׁי**, יָכוֹל רִאשׁוֹן וְשֵׁנִי מֻתָּר וּשְׁלִישִׁי יְהֵא אָסוּר? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **דּוֹר שְׁלִישִׁי יָבֹא לָהֶם בִּקְהַל ה׳**. אֱמֹר מֵעַתָּה רִאשׁוֹן וְשֵׁנִי אָסוּר וּשְׁלִישִׁי מֻתָּר. אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: בִּנְיָמִן גֵּר מִצְרִי הָיָה לִי חָבֵר מִתַּלְמִידֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, וְאָמַר: אֲנִי גֵּר מִצְרִי וְנָשׂוּי אֲנִי אִשָּׁה גִּיּוֹרֶת מִצְרִית, וַהֲרֵינִי הוֹלֵךְ לְהַשִּׂיא אֶת בְּנִי אִשָּׁה בַּת גִּיּוֹרֶת מִצְרִית כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא בֶּן בְּנִי רָאוּי לָבֹא בַקָּהָל, לְקַיֵּם מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: **דּוֹר שְׁלִישִׁי יָבֹא לָהֶם בִּקְהַל ה׳**.


3. “By the *third* generation they may enter the Community of Israel” (Dt. 23:9)—
is it possible to say that
the first- and second-generation offspring
[of converted Edomites and Egyptians]
shall have permission to enter,
but only the third generation shall be excluded?
The Teaching states:
“By the *third* generation they may enter the Community of Israel” (Dt. 23:9)—
On this basis you can teach that:
First- and second-generation offspring
are forbidden entry into the community,
but the third generation is permitted.4. **Said R. Judah:**
**Benjamin,**²⁶⁰ **the Egyptian proselyte,**
**was a companion of mine among the disciples of R. Akiva.**
**And he announced:**
**I am an Egyptian proselyte,**
**and I am married to a woman who is an Egyptian proselyte,**
**and please note that I’m planning to marry my son off**
**to a woman who is the daughter of an Egyptian proselyte—**
**all so that my son’s son**
**may appropriately enter the community,**
**and fulfill what is stated:**
**“By the third generation they may enter the Community of Israel” (Dt. 23:9).** ²⁶¹

###### Sifrei Devarim 254:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/254:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Sifrei%20Devarim/r/254:3)


**וְנִשְׁמַרְתָּ מִכֹּל דָּבָר רָע**, שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי בְּטָהֳרוֹת וּבְטֻמְאוֹת וּבְמַעַשְׂרוֹת הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: עֶרְוָה. אֵין לִי אֶלָּא עֶרְוָה, מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וּשְׁפִיכַת דָּמִים וְקִלְלַת הַשֵּׁם? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **וְנִשְׁמַרְתָּ מִכֹּל דָּבָר רָע**. אִי **וְנִשְׁמַרְתָּ**, יָכוֹל בְּטָהֳרוֹת וּבְטֻמְאוֹת וּבְמַעַשְׂרוֹת הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: עֶרְוָה – מָה עֶרְוָה מְיֻחֶדֶת מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁגָּלוּ עָלָיו כְּנַעֲנִים וּמְסַלֵּק אֶת הַשְּׁכִינָה, כָּךְ כָּל מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁגָּלוּ עָלָיו כְּנַעֲנִים וּמְסַלֵּק אֶת הַשְּׁכִינָה.


2. “You must carefully guard yourself against any *harmful thing*”²⁶³; literally, “a bad thing.” (Dt. 23:10)—
shall I understand this verse as requiring
separation of clean things from unclean things,
or separation of Tithes from [untithed] produce? The Teaching states:
“A *lewd thing*”²⁶⁴ literally, “an indecent thing.” (Dt. 23:15; 24:1)—
[implying some sexual impropriety].²⁶⁵ 269.1-6.
I might infer only that
*lewd* suggests [sexual] license.
How do I know that it might include
participation in a foreign cult,
shedding innocent blood,
or cursing the Name?
The Teachings states:
“You must carefully guard yourself against *any harmful* thing” (Dt. 23:10)—
[certainly including idolatry, bloodshed, and blasphemy]!3. Well, if *you must carefully guard yourself*,
isn’t it possible to say that the verse concerns
separation of clean things from unclean things,
or the separation of Tithes from [untithed] produce? The Teaching states:
**“A *lewd* thing” (Dt. 23:15; 24:1)—**
**just as *lewdness* is distinctive,**
**causing the expulsion of the Canaanites,**
**as well as the repulsion of the Presence,**
**so, too, *lewdness* [describes] any act that**
**causes the expulsion of the Canaanites,**
**or the repulsion of the Presence.**²⁶⁶ 258.3
